title: As NFL prepares to stage Steelers-Saints in Paris, local unrest intensifies
summary: First-ever game in France is scheduled for October 25.
full_text: In little more than a week, the Steelers and Saints will play the NFL's first-ever game in Paris. Although the league recently said it plans to proceed amid persistent local unrest, the situation seems to be getting worse. On Saturday, more than 1,200 arrests were made after an " escalation in violence " that occurred with roughly 550,000 citizens protesting. The demonstrations, sparked by concerns regarding conditions in schools and the cost of living, have lingered for weeks. Said the NFL on Wednesday: “We’re excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25. As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month.” If the NFL is going to pivot from Paris to New Orleans (the Saints are the home game for the Week 7 contest), a decision may need to be made soon. Obviously, the NFL has a very strong interest in following through with all of its international games. Then there's the fact that the game is set for a 9:30 a.m. ET standalone broadcast window on NFL Network. When the Chiefs-Rams game moved from Mexico City to L.A. in 2018 due to poor field conditions, the time for the game (Monday night) didn't change. If the NFL pulls the plug on the Paris game and plays in New Orleans, would the game begin at 9:30 a.m. ET? It's also possible, in theory, to play the Steelers-Saints game in London, if either Tottenham Hotspur Stadium or Wembley Stadium are available. Either way, any change in location would become a potential logistical nightmare for the NFL, the teams, and the fans that have made plans to travel to France. That outcome is still better than having NFL personnel, team personnel, or NFL fans caught in the middle of the mess that continues to play out in Paris.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aqib Talib tees off on Ryan Fitzpatrick for his comments about Bo Nix
summary: Four years ago, Aqib Talib and Ryan Fitzpatrick were scheduled to become colleagues on Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football.
full_text: ' Four years ago, Aqib Talib and Ryan Fitzpatrick were scheduled to become colleagues on Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football . If Talib hadn't stepped aside from the job after his brother shot and killed a man at a youth football game, the most recent postgame show could have gotten very spicy. After Thursday nights 17-14 overtime win by the Broncos over the Seahawks, Fitzpatrick went all in as to Broncos quarterback Bo Nix. Fitzpatrick called Nix's performance "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position" before later saying, "That right there is garbage. That effort is garbage." It felt personal or, frankly, planted by someone from the Broncos in an effort to send a message to Nix. Either way, it was over the top. And it has prompted a reaction from Talib, whose career included a stint with the Broncos. “You are disrespectful to the quarterback position because you suck ," Talib said on the Gridiron podcast. "Period." Talib had plenty more to say about Fitzpatrick. "We’re talking about a guy who played for nine different teams in 17 years," Talib added. "Ain’t nobody want his ass. We’re talking about a guy who only played for a team for more than two years once. That’s Buffalo. And his record as a starter in Buffalo was 19-35. That’s fucking suck. A guy who played 17 years, 147 starts, and never sniffed a playoff game. He never touched the playoffs ever. That’s disrespectful to the quarterback position. "You suck. You suck, bro. We’re talking about a guy who got 169 interceptions, more interceptions than he has starts. How can a quarterback of his caliber talk about what is disrespectful to the quarterback position? I know Amazon is begging for you to be more entertaining, and you've just got to just blabber out some bullshit. Nobody’s worried about what Fitzpatrick said. Nobody was worried about playing against you. You suck.” It's a harsh, blunt critique from Talib. But it's not much more harsh or blunt than what Fitzpatrick said about Nix. And it will be interesting to see whether Fitzpatrick has anything to say in response to Talib.
author: Mike Florio

title: After overcoming severe colitis in 2024, Auburn's Alex McPherson kicks game-winner vs. No. 1 Georgia
summary: Evan McPherson is in his sixth season as the kicker of the Cincinnati Bengals.
full_text: Evan McPherson is in his sixth season as the kicker of the Cincinnati Bengals. His younger brother, Alex, is doing the family business proud. Alex McPherson kicked a 34-yard field goal as time expired, vaulting unranked Auburn to a 27-24 win over No. 1 Georgia. It's the second straight weekend in which the No. 1 team lost to an unranked foe, after Oklahoma defeated No. 1 Texas last Saturday. Auburn was an 18.5-point underdog for the game played in Athens, Georgia. Alex McPherson's personal story makes his achievement far more noteworthy. In 2024, a bout with s evere ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease resulted in the removal of his entire large intestine. “That week I began to feel sick, I would run to the bathroom 15-20 times a day," Alex McPherson said last year. "I thought I just had the flu or a stomach bug or something going on. My weight was down. I had lost 20 pounds.” He eventually lost 55 pounds. When he was admitted to the hospital, he weighed 110 pounds. He's now back to full health. In high school, Alex kicked a 61-yard field goal. “It’s been really fun, really excited just to be back to normal from where I was,” Alex McPherson said at the SEC Media Days in July 2026. “Just to have that strength back to kind of kick how I want to and how I used to. I think I’m kicking as good as I have since before I got sick and it’s just really exciting to be able to do that and play with the guys to the full extent.” Alex McPherson is in his final year at Auburn. Come 2027, he could be joining his big brother in the NFL. It's an outcome that would have been inconceivable two years ago.
author: Mike Florio

title: Steve Sarkisian doesn't rule out benching Arch Manning
summary: The 2026 season for the University of Texas is quickly imploding.
full_text: The 2026 season for the University of Texas is quickly imploding. And it could result in the benching of quarterback Arch Manning. Via Danny Davis of the Austin American-Statesman , Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian opened the door to replacing Manning after Saturday's 27-24 loss to Florida. Asked whether Sarkisian considered making a change at quarterback, he said, "I just felt like we didn't play good offensive football and we're not playing great offensive football right now. So everything is going to be evaluated." Sarkisian then was asked whether that means his starting quarterback. "Everything means everything," Sarkisian replied. If K.J. Lacey replaces Manning, the college career of Peyton and Eli's nephew would be thrown for a loop. Not long ago, Arch was the betting favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 draft. If Sarkisian removes Manning from the lineup, he'd likely take another year before joining the NFL — possibly after transferring to a new program. Against Florida, Manning struggled . Last week, a pair of fourth-quarter interceptions in the Red River Rivalry set the stage for the first Texas loss of the season, 27-24 to Oklahoma. Next week, Texas hosts Mississippi. Carrying the Manning name is equal parts blessing and curse. It has allowed Arch to earn millions in NIL payments. It also has invited significant scrutiny and the creation of a high bar that he's currently falling far short of meeting.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Juszczyk set to return for 49ers, Mike Evans listed as questionable
summary: Fullback Kyle Juszczyk is set to return to the 49ers' lineup on Monday night.
full_text: Fullback Kyle Juszczyk is set to return to the 49ers' lineup on Monday night. Juszczyk missed last Sunday's win over the Seahawks with a knee injury, but was up to full practice participation on Saturday. The team did not give him an injury designation for their home game against the Commanders. Wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is listed as questionable to play. Evans did not practice this week, but the 49ers are leaving the door open for him to play. Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee, calf), wide receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring), safety Marques Sigle (ankle), and linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring) have been ruled out. Defensive tackle Gracen Halton (quad), wide receiver Christian Kirk (calf), safety Siran Neal (neck), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder), and defensive end Mykel Williams (knee) are all listed as questionable.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bill Belichick beats Duke for the first time, as North Carolina wins in Durham
summary: Bill Belichick has claimed that the first words he ever spoke were "Beat Duke," because his father was an assistant coach at North Carolina.
full_text: Bill Belichick has claimed that the first words he ever spoke were "Beat Duke," because his father was an assistant coach at North Carolina. Now, a Belichick has beaten Duke for the first time. Belichick's North Carolina team beat Duke today, 24-20, blowing a 17-0 lead, falling behind 20-17 and then coming back with the game-winning touchdown with less than two minutes remaining. In Belichick's first season at North Carolina last year, his Tar Heels lost to Duke. And North Carolina went 0-3 against Duke in the three years that Belichick's father, Steve Belichick, was a Tar Heels assistant. So this win was special for Belichick. It's also special because it's more evidence that Belichick is turning things around after his disappointing debut season. The Tar Heels are now 4-2 after finishing 4-8 last year. Whether Belichick can turn North Carolina into a college football power remains to be seen, but he has his team heading in the right direction, with a big win over a big rival today.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Will Troy Aikman finish the season with Monday Night Football?
summary: Because millions care intensely about NFL football, they have similarly strong feelings about the voices that narrate the action on TV.
full_text: Because millions care intensely about NFL football, they have similarly strong feelings about the voices that narrate the action on TV. And the unexpected escalation of tensions between Troy Aikman and ESPN/ABC has plenty of people wondering whether the relationship will end before his current contract expires. Boomer Esiason raised the question this week on his WFAN morning show of whether Aikman would walk away. “I don’t think he would do it , that’s not his nature, I don’t think," Esiason said Friday, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing . Of course, it may not be Aikman's choice. ESPN could yank him from the broadcast whenever it chooses, if the situation continues to deteriorate. Sure, they'd need to replace him on the fly. But they currently have a small army of NFL voices on the payroll — many of whom would drive a lawnmower through a minefield for a chance to fill the spot. It's hard to imagine Aikman walking away in a Super Bowl year. But if he becomes sufficiently disillusioned with the situation, it can't be ruled out. Much of it depends on whether any of the apparent animosity makes its way into a broadcast. For now, it hasn't. But everyone who's aware of the situation (and, frankly, many who watch Monday Night Football aren't and won't be) will be watching and listening for any hint in any stray comment or pointed remark. Ultimately, it takes two to tango in any employment relationship. And if the two sides know the music will stop once the confetti falls in L.A. on Valentine's Day, a premature record scratch is possible. In some respects, it's already happening.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bradley Chubb fined for taunting Alaric Jackson before Jackson punched him
summary: Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb did not retaliate physically after Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched him in the aftermath of Buffalo's Week 5 win in Los Angeles, but he did get disciplined by the league for his part in the altercation.
full_text: Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb did not retaliate physically after Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched him in the aftermath of Buffalo's Week 5 win in Los Angeles, but he did get disciplined by the league for his part in the altercation. The NFL announced on Saturday that Chubb has been fined $14,239 for taunting Jackson before Jackson took a swing at him. Chubb acknowledged that he initiated the interaction between the two men. Jackson was suspended two games for his actions, but the ban was reduced to one game after he appealed the punishment. He will lose $934,555 while sitting out Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Bills running back James Cook was fined $21,167 for illegal use of the helmet and safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was fined $11,194 for unnecessary roughness. Rams defensive lineman Braden Fiske was fined $11,941 for a facemask foul.
author: Josh Alper

title: Reports: Caleb Williams to start for Bears Sunday
summary: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was coy about his availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons during a Friday press conference, but he seemed to send a message with a social media post later in the day.
full_text: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was coy about his availability for Sunday's game against the Falcons during a Friday press conference, but he seemed to send a message with a social media post later in the day. Williams posted a video that strongly suggested he would be returning from the hamstring injury that caused him to miss the last three weeks and multiple reports on Saturday afternoon confirm that is the case. Williams is set to start for the 3-2 Bears against the 2-3 Falcons. Williams was a full participant in practice all week, but the Bears listed him as questionable on Friday. The Bears won the first two games that Williams missed, but they struggled with Tyson Bagent at quarterback in last Sunday's loss to the Packers.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles sign RB Jaydon Blue to active roster with Jalen Hurts officially on IR
summary: The Eagles announced the move to place quarterback Jalen Hurts to injured reserve on Saturday afternoon and they also made a move to fill the open space on their 53-man roster.
full_text: The Eagles announced the move to place quarterback Jalen Hurts to injured reserve on Saturday afternoon and they also made a move to fill the open space on their 53-man roster. Running back Jaydon Blue has been signed off of the practice squad. Blue signed with the Eagles after being cut by the Cowboys at the end of the summer. Blue was a fifth-round pick in Dallas in 2025. He had 38 carries for 129 yards and a touchdown in five appearances during his rookie season. With Saquon Barkley ruled out and two other backs on injured reserve, Blue will join Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as the available running backs against the Panthers on Sunday. The Eagles also announced that they have elevated linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby and safety Cole Wisniewski from the practice squad for Sunday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Minkah Fitzpatrick, five others fined for player safety fouls in Week 6
summary: The NFL confirmed that Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick was fined for his hit on a defenseless KC Concepcion in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns and they announced five other players were fined for the player safety fouls that count toward potential suspensions.
full_text: '' The NFL confirmed that Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick was fined for his hit on a defenseless KC Concepcion in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns and they announced five other players were fined for the player safety fouls that count toward potential suspensions. Fitzpatrick said this week that he plans to appeal the $17,911 fine for the hit, which knocked Concepcion out of the game with a concussion. Concepcion has cleared concussion protocol and is set to play against the Ravens in Week 6. Fitzpatrick was also fined $11,941 for tackling Concepcion by the facemask earlier in the game. Colts linebacker Austin Ajiake and 49ers safety Malik Mustapha were also fined for hits on defenseless players. Ajiake's fine was $5,583 and Mustapha's was $6,998. Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike ($17,911), Lions defensive end D.J. Wonnum ($12,611), and Titans cornerback Micah Robinson ($5,583) were all fined for hip-drop tackles. It is the first infraction for each player. Any player who is fined three times for one of five player safety rules — horse-collar tackles, launching and blindside blocks are the others — is subject to a one-game suspension.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots activate A.J. Brown
summary: A.J.
full_text: '' A.J. Brown is back for the Patriots. The team announced on Saturday that Brown has been activated from the injured reserve list ahead of Sunday's home game against the Jets. The wide receiver has been out since injuring his ankle in New England's Week 1 loss to the Seahawks. Sunday's game will be Brown's first home game as a member of the Patriots. He had three catches for 26 yards before his injury. The Patriots also announced that they have elevated defensive back Elliott Davison and running back Hassan Haskins from the practice squad. The fact that they did not add any offensive line help could be a sign that left tackle Will Campbell will be able to play after being listed as questionable with a knee injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jalen Hurts will go on injured reserve, miss at least four games and possibly more
summary: Hurts has a blood clot and will not play until Week 11 at the earliest.
full_text: The Eagles will be without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for at least four games. Hurts has been placed on injured reserve because of a blood clot, the team announced. That comes after a previous ESPN report said the Eagles hadn’t even discussed putting Hurts on injured reserve. That seemed hard to believe at the time, and now the team hasn't just discussed it but has done it. The Eagles' next four games are against the Panthers, Cowboys, Commanders, and Giants, then have their bye. It's possible that Hurts could be back after the bye. But he's currently considered out indefinitely, and it's possible he'll be gone for most or all of the rest of the season. Players who have to go on blood thinners are typically out for more than a month. The 2-3 Eagles are still contenders in the NFC East, and they'll hope to get Hurts back for a playoff push late in the season. But that's no sure thing. While Hurts is out, backup quarterback Tanner McKee will start. Rookie Cole Payton is currently McKee's backup, and the recently signed Joe Milton is the No. 3 quarterback in Philadelphia.
author: Michael David Smith

title: The "black box" idea could be adopted by some teams
summary: In the aftermath of the Commanders' overtime clock debacle against the Giants, it became impossible to figure out exactly what had happened.
full_text: In the aftermath of the Commanders' overtime clock debacle against the Giants, it became impossible to figure out exactly what had happened. Especially with everyone involved taking the blame for it. A reader had an idea that was good enough to steal and use: Teams should record and preserve all communications, like the "black box" on an airplane. We floated that concept, and at least someone was listening. “Yeah, it’s chaos,” an unnamed head coach told Albert Breer of SI . “The coordinator’s gotta have discipline. I mean, it is fucking chaos. It’s like, 'Everyone, shut the fuck up.' Florio had a good one — they should black box the headsets . You could make a movie off of that shit." Maybe some teams already do it; if they do, they don't advertise it. And those who may start doing it likely won't make the communications available to the public. Still, it's critical for internal purposes. How can ownership (other than Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, who puts herself in the fray for precisely such seasons) know what truly happened when left to the inherent flaws of human memory, especially when things are happening in a chaotic environment and when human nature will prompt some to slip into a CYA posture? It can't be difficult to save the conversations, and it wouldn't be expensive. As we learned on Sunday, it's necessary to knowing how a strange situation unfolded. That knowledge could go a long way toward figuring out who has the true responsibility for the ensuing snafu, and how to best prevent it from happening again.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders list Stefon Diggs, eight others as questionable
summary: The Commanders played without wide receiver Stefon Diggs last Sunday and they'll wait to make a call on his availability for Monday's game against the 49ers.
full_text: The Commanders played without wide receiver Stefon Diggs last Sunday and they'll wait to make a call on his availability for Monday's game against the 49ers. Diggs has been listed as questionable to play after practicing on a limited basis the last two days. Diggs, who had 18 catches in the first four games, has been battling a hamstring injury. The Commanders listed eight other players as questionable as well. The group includes cornerback Trey Amos (ankle), linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring), and running back Jeremy McNichols (quad). All three players would need to be activated in order to play in Week 6. Safety Percy Butler (hamstring), safety Nick Cross (illness), defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw (ankle, knee), safety Tyler Owens (hamstring), and offensive lineman Lucas Patrick (illness) are the other questionable players on the active roster. Head coach Dan Quinn announced earlier on Saturday that running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), and defensive end Charles Omenihu (groin, ankle) will not play.
author: Josh Alper

title: Grant Delpit sums up difference between Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley in four words
summary: On Sunday, Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley will make his 19th career NFL start (including playoffs).
full_text: ' On Sunday, Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley will make his 19th career NFL start (including playoffs). For the Ravens, he's 6-7 with three straight wins. On Friday, Browns safety Grant Delpit addressed some of the similarities between Huntley and two-time MVP Lamar Jackson. Delpit then was asked to identify the biggest difference. " One is Lamar Jackson ," Delpit said. He's right. But Huntley has proven to be capable. Last week, he completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions. He added 20 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. So while he's not Lamar (no one is), Huntley can do enough. Delpit's acknowledgement of the obvious could give Huntley a little extra incentive to prove that the gap may not be quite as large as Delpit thinks. The stakes are high. A win by Cleveland (which would be their fourth straight in the AFC North, a first since 1987) would tie the Ravens and Browns at 4-2. A loss would give Baltimore a two-game lead over the Browns and the first half of the head-to-head tiebreaker.
author: Mike Florio

title: Arch Manning struggles and Colin Simmons is carted as Texas loses to Florida
summary: Formerly No. 1 Texas lost its second straight game on Saturday, and it was a particularly rough day for the Longhorns' two highest-profile 2027 NFL draft prospects.
full_text: Formerly No. 1 Texas lost its second straight game on Saturday, and it was a particularly rough day for the Longhorns' two highest-profile 2027 NFL draft prospects. Texas quarterback Arch Manning, who until recently was the betting favorite to go first overall in next year's draft, had another bad game. Manning had been up and down throughout, but when Texas got the ball back down by three with two and a half minutes to play, it looked like an opportunity for Manning to engineer a great comeback. Instead, Manning was sacked and fumbled, Florida recovered, and that was that. Florida won, 27-24. The other top draft prospect on the Longhorns, Texas pass rusher Colin Simmons, the NCAA leader in sacks and a potential Top 5 pick in 2027, was carted off with a left leg injury in the fourth quarter. Manning has been known to make big plays with his legs at times, but he couldn't do that today against Florida. In one particularly rough sequence, Manning attempted to run for a first down on third-and-1 but lost a yard. Texas then went for it on fourth-and-2, Manning again tried to run, and he again was tackled behind the line of scrimmage for a turnover on downs. He also repeatedly failed to escape pass pressure. Florida running back Jadan Baugh, considered by some the best running back prospect in the 2027 draft class, scored the fourth-quarter winning touchdown for the Gators. He finished with 25 carries for 91 yards. But the story of the game will be Manning, who has failed to live up to the hype. This was an ugly performance, following an ugly performance in last week's loss to Oklahoma, and it's fair to question whether Manning is a future NFL star, or whether he just shares the same last name as three past NFL stars.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Steelers put Roman Wilson on injured reserve
summary: Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson will be out of the lineup for an extended period of time.
full_text: Steelers wide receiver Roman Wilson will be out of the lineup for an extended period of time. Wilson was placed on injured reserve Saturday due to the finger injury that led the team to rule him out of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers. Wilson will now have to miss at least four games before he will be able to return to action. Wilson has 14 catches for 188 yards and two touchdowns on the season. He joins Michael Pittman Jr. on the injured reserve list and Ben Skowronek has also been ruled out for this week. The Steelers elevated a pair of wideouts from the practice squad to help fill out the group. Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson will both be available Sunday before reverting back. Running back Lew Nichols was signed off of the practice squad to take Wilson's roster spot.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay believes the Harrison Mevis blocked field goal would have missed anyway
summary: After Monday night's overtime loss to the Bills, Rams coach Sean McVay minced no words — he said the field goal unit lost the game.
full_text: After Monday night's overtime loss to the Bills, Rams coach Sean McVay minced no words — he said the field goal unit lost the game . The next day, kicker Harrison Mevis lost his roster spot. And it wasn't just that the potential game-winning field goal from 48 yards was blocked . McVay believes, even without the effort from Gregory Rousseau to get a hand on the ball, the kick would have missed. “I didn't think it would have gone in, I did not," McVay told reporters on Friday. "I could be wrong, but it didn't look like the trajectory was on alignment.” If so, the block straightened it out. And it nearly had enough distance to clear the crossbar. With Mevis gone, Blake Grupe takes over. "He has a nice demeanor about himself," McVay said regarding the team's new kicker. "There's a quiet confidence, but a humility that you want. I'm looking forward to seeing him produce and then I think it's part of our job to put him in positions that have successful outcomes. Ideally, it's more extra points than anything else." Still, Grupe's range (his career long is 60 yards) gives the team a broader window for attempting field goals. “I think having a strong leg is attractive, especially like at the end of a half or at the end of the game," special-teams coordinator Bubba Ventrone told reporters. "You need the range to be able to do so and to be able to hit it with accuracy. I think he's done a good job in his career to be able to do that. He gets good elevation on his kicks. He has a strong leg despite his size. He is an explosive guy. I really am excited to work with him.” Elevation is a key factor. Mevis wasn't able to get the ball over Rousseau's hand. Even if it had, McVay thinks it would have missed the mark.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars look to match best six-game start in team history
summary: As the Jaguars prepare to play their second straight game in London, they have an opportunity to do something they haven't done in 27 years — start the year 5-1.
full_text: As the Jaguars prepare to play their second straight game in London, they have an opportunity to do something they haven't done in 27 years — start the year 5-1. The Jaguars last started 5-1 in 1999. That year, they finished 14-2 and lost in the AFC Championship, to the Titans. This year, Jacksonville has a chance (thanks to the division it's in) to win enough games to secure the No. 1 seed. The next test is a big one, however. The Texans have done well against the Jaguars in recent years. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has a 3-7 record against the Texans, with eight touchdown passes and 11 interceptions in those games. Via NBC Sports research, no player since Lawrence's rookie season has thrown more interceptions against a single opponent than Lawrence against the Texans. The Texans, meanwhile, have a 15-5 record in division games since DeMeco Ryans became the head coach. In those games, quarterback C.J. Stroud has a record of 12-5, with 24 touchdown passes and five interceptions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers activate Taylor Moton, Turk Wharton, Trevor Etienne
summary: Panthers offensive tackle Taylor Moton is set to make his 2026 debut.
full_text: '' Panthers offensive tackle Taylor Moton is set to make his 2026 debut. Moton returned to practice this week after missing all of training camp and the first weeks of the regular season while recovering from blood clots in his lung. The Panthers announced that he has been activated from the physically unable to perform list on Saturday. Moton could be back at his familiar right tackle spot against the Eagles. First-round pick Monroe Freeling has been manning the spot, but he is doubtful to play due to a knee injury. The Panthers also activated defensive lineman Turk Wharton and running back Trevor Etienne from injured reserve. They elevated running back Anthony Tyus and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad to round out the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears activate Kyler Gordon, sign Nick McCloud to active roster
summary: Bears General Manager Ryan Poles said in September that he didn't know if cornerback Kyler Gordon would play for the Bears again, but it looks like he'll be back in their lineup against the Falcons on Sunday.
full_text: Bears General Manager Ryan Poles said in September that he didn't know if cornerback Kyler Gordon would play for the Bears again, but it looks like he'll be back in their lineup against the Falcons on Sunday. The Bears activated Gordon from the physically unable to perform list on Saturday. Gordon has been working his way back from a calf injury that also kept him off the field for most of last season. Defensive back Nick McCloud will also be available for Sunday's game. The Bears signed him to the active roster from the practice squad. They made room for Gordon and McCloud by placing defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve and releasing defensive back Xavier Woods. In addition to those moves, linebacker Buddy Johnson and running back Zavier Scott have been elevated from the practice squad for Sunday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders won't have Jacory Croskey-Merritt Monday night
summary: The Commanders will be without their top running back for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
full_text: The Commanders will be without their top running back for Monday night's game against the 49ers. Head coach Dan Quinn said on Saturday that Jacory Croskey-Merritt has been ruled out. Croskey-Merritt is dealing with a groin injury that kept him out of practice all this week. Croskey-Merritt also missed time with a groin injury this summer and the current issue steps from an aggravation of that issue. The Commanders are dealing with several other injuries in the backfield. Rachaad White has a shoulder injury and Austin Ekeler has a chest injury, but both players have been practicing. Washington could also activate Jeremy McNichols from injured reserve. Linebacker Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Charles Omenihu (groin, ankle), and Marcus Mariota (knee) will also miss the game. The Commanders will release their full injury report later on Saturday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers say DK Metcalf will play, Pat Freiermuth is questionable with calf injury
summary: Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf is no longer on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, but tight end Pat Freiermuth now is.
full_text: Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf is no longer on the injury report for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, but tight end Pat Freiermuth now is. The Steelers announced today that Metcalf, who had previously been listed as questionable with an illness, is now healthy and ready to go on Sunday. Freiermuth, however, is now listed as questionable for a calf injury. It's unclear how Freiermuth suffered the injury, but he wasn't listed on yesterday's report. The 3-2 Steelers are 2.5-point favorites at 1-4 Tampa Bay on Sunday.
author: Michael David Smith

title: College football player Tyler Ulrich dies five days after suffering traumatic injury during a game
summary: Tyler Ulrich, a 21-year-old football player at Southern Nazarene University, died Thursday.
full_text: ' Tyler Ulrich, a 21-year-old football player at Southern Nazarene University, died Thursday . He had suffered a traumatic injury five days earlier. The injury happened in a game against Ouachita Baptist University in Arkansas. There are no details about the injury suffered by Ulrich, who played safety at SNU. Via KOCO, the Southern Nazarene play-by-play announcer Dave Myrick said Ulrich was down on the field after the play, but that he couldn’t tell what had happened . It's an unimaginable tragedy for Ulrich's family and his team. Saturday's game at Southwestern State University has been canceled . A GoFundMe account has been established to assist Tyler's family during this time. We extend our condolences to Tyler Ulrich's family, teammates, coaches, and friends.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles don't plan to put QB Jalen Hurts on injured reserve
summary: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely with a blood clot in his leg.
full_text: ' Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely with a blood clot in his leg. The Eagles apparently believe it won't cause him to miss at least four games. Via ESPN, the Eagles aren’t planning to place Hurts on injured reserve . The article from ESPN includes this line: "The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve." That's odd, if true. The Eagles have no idea how much time he'll miss. Hurts is being treated with blood thinners, and he can't play while he's taking them. The Eagles play four games over the next 22 days (Panthers, Cowboys, at Commanders, at Giants) before entering their bye. Why not consider the possibility of giving him a full five weeks to recover, while also opening up a roster spot? The Eagles are already using a 52-man roster, given the decision to keep right tackle Lane Johnson on the team for 2027 cap purposes despite the fact that he has retired. So they're now down to 51. There's another interesting nugget in the ESPN article, which carries the bylines of Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. For the second straight week, Schefter has shared the opinions of doctors who haven't treated the player — even though last week’s article about Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and his dislocated elbow and the opinions of doctors who haven't treated him fell flat . This time, the doctors who haven't treated the player suggest that Hurts could miss up to six weeks. Regardless, the point for now is that the Eagles don't plan to place their starting quarterback on IR. Which, coupled with Johnson's presence on the roster, gives the Eagles two fewer players than every other team has available to it.
author: Mike Florio

title: All AFC, NFC North teams could emerge from Week 6 above .500
summary: One of the basic realities of life in the NFL is that each team is assigned to a division with three other teams, permanently.
full_text: One of the basic realities of life in the NFL is that each team is assigned to a division with three other teams, permanently. (Until there's a reason to realign, which last happened in 2002.) And whether a team is in a good division or a bad division controls much of a team's success, or not, in a given year. Of the 17 games played, six of them are determined by the division to which it is assigned. If the other teams are really good, it makes it harder for an otherwise good team to be as good as it can be. If the other teams aren't very good, it's easier. The fact that this is so obvious shows how fundamentally unfair it is. It can give some lesser teams a shot at hosting a playoff game. It can give the one good team in an otherwise bad division a chance to win enough games to emerge as the top seed in a conference (for example, the Patriots throughout most of the 2010s). This year, the teams of the AFC and NFC North will each have a tougher road to whatever their best-case scenario could be, based simply on membership in a predetermined division. All of them are over .500 through five weeks. Via NBC Sports research, a full division has been above .500 after six weeks only three times since 2002 (the 2025 NFC North, the 2024 NFC North, and the 2005 NFC East). Depending on how this weekend goes, both the AFC North and NFC North can turn that list of three into five. The Vikings, Lions, and Bengals are off, so the six-week hay is in the barn as to each of them. To complete the feat, the 3-2 Browns need to beat the 4-1 Ravens, the 3-2 Bears need to beat the Falcons, the 3-2 Packers need to beat the Cowboys, and the 3-2 Steelers need to beat the Buccaneers. If the Bears and Packers win, it'll be the third straight year that every team in the NFC North is above .500 through six weeks. Which will make it harder for each of them to get to wherever they want to be. That will likely change when the NFL expands the regular season to 18 games and seeds the playoff tree without regard to whether a team has won its division. That still won't solve the problem, and it will bolster the argument that there should be no divisions at all. Or, alternatively, that the two games per year against each of the other teams in the division should become one game per year. The point for now is that each of the four teams in the AFC North and NFC North could end up being objectively playoff-worthy in 2026, but playing six games against those other teams will make it harder to qualify. Meanwhile, someone from the NFC South will be winning the division and hosting a playoff game — even if (like last year) none of them ends up at or above .500. The entire approach makes it harder for the NFL to honor sports' most basic, longstanding message: "May the best team win." Given the way the NFL arranges its teams, the best team could end up with roadblocks that the not-best team won't have to navigate. Which could make it easier for the not-best team to win the Super Bowl.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers' JJ Jansen to play his 282nd game, most ever for a long snapper
summary: Carolina's JJ Jansen will become the NFL's all-time record holder for games played by a long snapper on Sunday.
full_text: Carolina's JJ Jansen will become the NFL's all-time record holder for games played by a long snapper on Sunday. The Panthers-Eagles game will be Jansen's 282nd, breaking a tie with Trey Junkin for the most games played at long snapper in NFL history. The 40-year-old Jansen long snapped at Notre Dame and then signed with the Packers as an undrafted free agent in 2008 but played only in the preseason, spending the regular season on injured reserve. In 2009 the Panthers needed a long snapper, so they traded a conditional 2011 draft pick for Jansen. He's been their long snapper ever since. Long snapping is a skill that few players ever learn, and most who do have a story of a football mentor who taught them the technique that can earn playing time on the varsity high school team, a college scholarship for some, and NFL riches for a select few. For Jansen, that mentor was his father, who had been a high school long snapper. "I still remember we practiced in the same way every single time," Jansen told Darin Gantt of Panthers.com. "We had like a square piece of grass that was probably 20 yards by 20 yards. I'd stand at one end in front of a tree that was right in the middle. My dad would stand at 15 yards away, and I would snap it . We'd have those legendary long nights where you're good, and then you stink, and then you're good, and you stink, and you're mad at yourself because you stink, so you yell at your dad, and he's yelling back at you and, there's this whole, you know, boys and their fathers moments." Jansen has played the second-most games of any active player, behind only Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell, who has played 283 games. If both Campbell and Jansen play all 17 games this season, at the end of the year Campbell will have played 295 games, tying him with Darrell Green for the 16th-most in NFL history, and Jansen will have played 294, good for 18th-most in NFL history. All 281 of Jansen's games have been with the Panthers. Former Lions kicker Jason Hanson has the NFL record for most games played with one team, at 327. If Jansen keeps playing every game in Carolina, he'll move ahead of Hanson in the final game of the 2028 season. Jansen is showing no signs of slowing down.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Chiefs nose tackle Khyiris Tonga is playing almost as much offense as Travis Hunter
summary: Jaguars cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter has been much-hyped for his status as a two-way player, first as a Heisman Trophy winner at Colorado and now in the NFL.
full_text: Jaguars cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter has been much-hyped for his status as a two-way player, first as a Heisman Trophy winner at Colorado and now in the NFL. But there's another two-way player in the NFL this season who hasn't received as much hype: Chiefs nose tackle and fullback Khyiris Tonga. Like Hunter, Tonga has started every game on defense this season. Like Hunter, Tonga has played only limited offensive snaps this season. Tonga has two carries; Hunter has two catches. Both have picked up one first down. Hunter plays a little bit more on offense, but not much more: Hunter has played 6.8 percent of the Jaguars' offensive snaps, while Tonga has played 4.2 percent of the Chiefs' offensive snaps. The Jaguars have said Hunter is capable of being a full-time player at both wide receiver and cornerback, while the Chiefs consider Tonga only a situational short-yardage fullback in addition to his duties as a starter on the defensive line. But as far as their usage this season, both players are comparable. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, himself a former defensive player who occasionally lined up on offense as well, started using Tonga as a blocking fullback last season, when Tonga played 14 snaps on offense in New England. This year, Tonga signed a three-year, $21 million free agent contract with the Chiefs, and the Chiefs have increased his role on offense, including not just blocking but also running the ball. Tonga said on the Chiefs’ YouTube channel that it was a thrill the first time he went into the offensive huddle with quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker. "It was super cool," Tonga said. "Being in the offensive huddle is amazing, especially having the players we have, to share the huddle with them. The only thing in my mind was, Don't mess it up. I just went out there to have fun. It makes it easy blocking for a guy like K9." Tonga even ran a route on a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass to Jalen Royals in Week 2, and Tonga said he was prepared to catch it if Mahomes threw to him but was a little relieved when Mahomes looked past him and threw to Royals. "I was just making sure I didn't drop it. Look it in if it came to me. It went past me, so it was OK," Tonga said. Could Tonga do anything else in Andy Reid's offense? He said he'd even be up for throwing the ball on a trick play if that gets called. "Having a guy like 15, I hope they don't make me throw the ball, but if we have to I'm ready," Tonga said. Tonga, who has also played 19 snaps on special teams this season, is willing to do whatever he has to do to help his team win.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Titans CEO Burke Nihill: Our organization believes in coach Robert Saleh, GM Mike Borgonzi
summary: The Titans have fired a head coach or GM each of the last four years, but they say they're going to be patient with their current coach and GM.
full_text: The Titans are 0-5 in head coach Robert Saleh's first season, and 3-19 five games into General Manager Mike Borgonzi's second season. But Titans CEO Burke Nihill says the franchise believes the right leadership is in place. "I personally feel a sense of stability," Nihill told ESPN on Friday. "I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football. The train is on the tracks. It just hasn't picked up momentum, but it will. I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster." Those comments would mean more coming directly from Titans owner Amy Adams-Strunk, but the ESPN report says Nihill is empowered to speak for her. Nihill says the organization knows the fans are frustrated. "The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we're sorry," Nihill said. "There's nobody in this building that doesn't feel . . . a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we've let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun. I think it starts on the field and the state of the franchise. We're 0-5, and that's not nearly good enough. It hasn't been for a while." The Titans fired General Manager Jon Robinson during the 2022 season, fired head coach Mike Vrabel after the 2023 season, fired General Manager Ran Carthon after the 2024 season and fired head coach Brian Callahan during the 2025 season. All those firings haven't turned the franchise around. Now they're pledging patience with Borgonzi and Saleh.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Cowboys vs. Packers prediction: Dak Prescott, Jordan Love set for high-flying showdown on 'SNF'
summary: The last time these two teams met in Week 4 of the 2025 season, they combined for the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era
full_text:
One of the NFL's highest-scoring rivalries will be renewed on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6 when the Green Bay Packers (3-2) host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) at Lambeau Field on Sunday night.
Last season, the Packers traveled down to Texas to face the Cowboys at AT&T Stadium, and the two teams tied at 40-40, the highest-scoring tie in the Super Bowl era, since 1996, per CBS Sports Research. The game featured seven lead changes, including six consecutive touchdown drives with a lead change in the second half.
However, this rivalry hasn't exactly been very competitive in terms of the games' final outcomes, with the Cowboys seeking their first win against the Packers since the 2016 regular season, quarterback Dak Prescott's rookie year. Since that game, Dallas is 0-5-1 in the last six games against Green Bay despite scoring 31 points per game in that stretch. The problem is their defense has allowed a combined 37 points per game during the six-game winless streak against the Packers. That's the most points per game scored by a team's offense during a six-game winless span against an opponent in NFL history, per CBS Sports Research.
Sunday will mark Packers quarterback Jordan Love's first home start against the Cowboys, with both of his games against Dallas coming on the road -- a 48-32 wild card round win in the 2023 season and the 40-40 tie last year. It will also mark a homecoming for two former Packers who are now Cowboys: three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Kenny Clark and Pro Bowl edge rusher Rashan Gary .
Let's dig into this primetime fight against two of the NFL's most historic franchises, but first, here's how you can watch:
Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay, Wisconsin) TV: NBC | Stream: Fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -1.5, O/U 53.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)
Cowboys looking to fix bad vibes on defense: In Week 5, Dallas lost a home game 24-16 on "Thursday Night Football" to the previously 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers , a team it was favored by 9.5 points. Tampa Bay was starting undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels , making his second career start in place of an injured Baker Mayfield , and Dallas allowed the Buccaneers to control the game with 241 rushing yards. That was the most for the Buccaneers in a game since the 2024 season.
This week, there has been speculation from owner and general manager Jerry Jones about first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker moving upstairs to the booth, but Parker and head coach Brian Schottenheimer maintained he will remain on the sideline. Dallas' performance improvement plan has begun with the hiring of former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019.
Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked defense (395.4 total yards allowed per game), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game), and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it.
How fixable are the issues?
"Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable."
Cowboys All-Pro defensive tackle Quinnen Williams agrees.
"Just from the aspect of the things that we can control are the things that we're messing up on. Effort. Playing with our technique. Playing better, things like that. Those are things we can control as a unit, we can control as a unit. It's fixable. We just have to make our best effort to fix those things.
Packers' Jordan Love aims to maintain an explosive passing game to Christian Watson and Matthew Golden : Packers quarterback Jordan Love is fresh off his best game of 2026 in Week 5, a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field.
Love completed 25 of his 31 throws for 367 yards and 2 touchdowns against Chicago, which makes him the Packers' record holder for the most passing yards in a game against the Bears at Lambeau Field. He beat the previous record of 345 yards passing by Lynn Dickey, set back in 1983. The victory, 24 points, ranks as the largest win against the Bears since 2014, the year Rodgers won the second of his four NFL MVPs. The Packers are now 5-3 against the Bears in Love's eight career starts against them since 2023, including playoffs.
"We were flowing today. Executed at a really high level. I was proud of everybody. That's what it looks like when we play to our standard, and we got playmakers making plays down the field, O-line doing a great job," Love said postgame on FOX . "That's the standard for us. ... This is huge. This is a win we needed at home, getting us rolling and keep building off this."
Love went big-game hunting with regularity to both wide receiver Christian Watson (143 yards receiving and 2 receiving touchdowns on 6 catches) and wide receiver Matthew Golden (123 yards receiving on 6 catches), making Watson and Golden the first Green Bay duo with 120-plus yards receiving in a game since 2016. It last occurred when Davante Adams and Jordy Nelson accomplished the feat against the Tennessee Titans 10 years ago. Love hit Watson for gains of 42 yards (the game's first touchdown that made the score 7-0), 31 yards and 53 yards (Love's second touchdown pass that made the score 20-7 with 13:10 left in the third quarter). He connected with Golden on throws of 36 yards and 50 yards.
In total, Love connected on six of eight of his eight throws of 20-plus air yards for a career-high 258 yards and 2 touchdowns on his passes of 20-plus air yards. Per the league's Next Gen stats , only Russell Wilson (264 with the New York Giants in Week 2 of the 2025 season against the Dallas Cowboys ) had more in the NGS era (since 2016). According to ESPN Insights , Love joined Ben Roethlisberger as the only players with five completions of 30-plus air yards in a game since ESPN began tracking the metric 20 years ago in 2006.
Slowing this high-flying passing attack down will be a tall task for a struggling Cowboys defense.
A stoppable force vs. a movable object: The Packers rank dead last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4) and third-down offense (27.6% conversion rate) thanks to missing running back Josh Jacobs while he was on the commissioner's exempt list and dealing with some offensive line injuries. Across from them on the line of scrimmage at Lambeau Field on Sunday will be the Cowboys' last-ranked run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and last-ranked third-down defense (52.6% conversion rate allowed). Whichever team can find an edge here will likely emerge victorious.
New Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr . primed to return in primetime: New Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was set to play his first full game as a Cowboy in Week 5 before a stomach bug made him a late scratch hours before kickoff. However, Porter Jr. is now recovered from his illness and aims to play a full starter's load of snaps. He played on 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans in Week 4 just days after being acquired in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier that week. He is officially listed as questionable to play on Sunday with an ankle injury, but on Wednesday he said he is "definitely" ready to be a full-time starter for Dallas. Parker agreed, saying the team is ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Packers.
Despite Porter Jr. likely returning to action for Dallas in Week 6, their defense won't be able to stifle Love, Watson and Golden through the air. Whichever receiver between Watson and Golden that cornerback DaRon Bland , who has struggled with his footing on the field of late, will break free for big gains on a consistent basis. Yes, the Cowboys do have the NFL's No. 7 scoring offense (27.6 points per game) powered by Prescott, wide receiver CeeDee Lamb , wide receiver George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams .
However, Dallas' defense…

title: Bears expected to start Caleb Williams vs. Falcons, per report
summary: The Chicago Bears are likely getting their No. 1 pick back this week
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are planning to start quarterback Caleb Williams on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons , according to multiple reports . Williams missed three games due to a torn hamstring and this week was able to return to practice at full capacity and took the starter's reps.
He is officially listed as questionable for their Week 6 game, but a full week of practice showed he was trending in the right direction.
Before going down with his injury, Williams played in two games: a 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers and a 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the game where he suffered the torn hamstring. He had a 65.6 completion percentage, 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in his two appearances.
Williams reposted a compilation video on TikTok earlier on Saturday that had many believing he was celebrating his return. The video starts with a compilation of criticisms of how he reacted to his injury, followed by a message from a fictional character from the Chicago-based show "The Bear," who says, "I think that flicked a switch in me where I was like, f--- you. Watch this." The video then goes into highlights of Williams playing.
Caleb Williams reposted this TikTok He might go off on Sunday 😳 pic.twitter.com/6UVgluc3Fx
The 24-year-old has openly criticized how people have reacted to his injury. When he was carted off, Williams gave a thumbs-up and raised his fist, which, to many, made it seem like the injury was very severe. Shortly after, there were reports that Williams may not miss a game.
Williams feels his "character has been attacked" and said to the media this week , "It was a hamstring tear and a pretty serious one. We got a grade, but I wouldn't say it's deserved to be put out there after all the false ones. So next question."
In his absence, the Bears have leaned on Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum , who were able to record two wins of the three games without their starter. Chicago is coming off a 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers .
In Week 5's loss, head coach Ben Johnson benched Bagent for Keenum after Bagent went 12-of-21 with 87 yards, two picks and no touchdowns. Keenum didn't fare much better, going 11-of-19 with 108 yards, one interception and no touchdowns.
Getting Williams back should be a big boost for the Bears offense, as they sit at 3-2 in a difficult division where the race is close and the top team, the Vikings , have yet to lose.
Williams was drafted as the top pick in the 2024 draft and helped lead the team to the playoffs in his second season with the team. He did not miss a game in his first two seasons.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: A.J. Brown injury update: Latest rumors, news on WR's status for Patriots in Week 6
summary: Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and has missed the last four games
full_text:
The New England Patriots offense will get a major boost this week. The team announced it activated star wide receiver A.J. Brown off injured reserve to play against the New York Jets on Sunday.
Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and has missed four weeks so far, the minimum required when a team places any player on IR. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to practice this week, but was limited all three days. His official game designation is questionable.
The WR had just three receptions on four targets for 26 yards before going down against the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl rematch season opener.
The Patriots offense was rocky to start the season, with quarterback Drake Maye struggling with forcing passes and committing turnovers. Their biggest offensive struggle came against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3, as they failed to get into the end zone and lost 35-6.
Without Brown, the worry was that the Patriots couldn't march down the field without a true WR1. Maye's capabilities were called into question, with many wondering whether last year's near-MVP season was a fluke.
Despite his absence, the Maye and Co. have seemed to get it together and have increased production tenfold. They look like a team to beat over the last two weeks, having defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26 and the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17. The Patriots are currently 10th in passing yards (1,274), but tied for most interceptions (7).
Brown returning should elevate the offense, finally give fans a look at what a Maye-Brown offense looks like, and continue the upward trajectory.
If Brown does not return this week against the Jets, he could return in Week 7 against the Chicago Bears .
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Jalen Hurts blood clot: Expert weighs in on Eagles' situation, and when QB could return to the field
summary: A cardiologist weighs in on how Hurts' condition contrasts with DVTs, standard treatment methods and what could determine the recovery timeline
full_text:
Jalen Hurts ' 2026 season was put on pause this week, as the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot that had experienced some movement and the team placed him on IR on Saturday.
The team diagnosed the clot and informed the league of Hurts' situation last week, but he was cleared to suit up and play in their Week 5 London loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . After a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the clot, the team announced that Hurts would have to sit out for at least one week while they treated him. It initially looked like the quarterback would avoid injured reserve, but ESPN reported Saturday afternoon that after consultations with doctors and experts, the Eagles decided to place Hurts on injured reserve -- meaning he will miss at least the next four games.
What is a superficial blood clot and how much time could Hurts miss? CBS Sports spoke to Dr. Henry Han at UT Southwestern to get some answers. Dr. Han is a board certified cardiologist that works at the intersection of cardiology and vascular medicine. He has seen clot-related diseases, diseases related to aneurysms, tears in blood vessels, and is very familiar with superficial vein thrombosis.
A superficial blood clot could be classified as "superficial thrombophlebitis," or a much easier term: "superficial vein thrombosis."
Dr. Han: "Basically it's a blood clot that's in one of the veins that's on the surface level underneath the skin. We typically find it in the leg, sometimes we find it in the arm. What happens is when the clot forms there, the vein gets inflamed. And so the area turns really red, it gets warm and it gets tender."
This is a situation that deserves monitoring, but it's also not the more serious "deep vein thrombosis" we've seen in sports before. Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, for example, was forced to miss the final 30 games of the 2024-25 season after doctors discovered deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. Then there's two-time NBA champion Chris Bosh, who was forced to retire early due to a clotting condition.
Dr. Han: "Superficial clots that sit near the surface on your surface veins are a lot less dangerous compared to the DVT (deep vein thrombosis). In sports we hear about the DVTs that for some athletes end up being sort of career-enders. The interesting part is that the superficial vein thromboses typically are not dangerous to that degree and the treatment for what you would need for both is a little bit different as well."
In their statement released on Thursday, the Eagles said that four days after the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams , Hurts requested treatment on his calf. He believed he was kicked or cleated in the game.
It's true that trauma to the area could have caused this clot, but we simply don't have enough information to say that definitively.
Dr. Han: "I can't speak to the exact specific case, but sort of generalities, anything that irritates a vein or slows the blood flow can trigger it. So we actually see this for people who have gotten IVs or blood draws when you have a needle in the vein that causes the irritation and damage. Other things too, like long flights. We know that certain hormone medications, pregnancy for women. But definitely trauma is one of the major causes that can cause this sort of superficial thrombophlebitis."
There are numerous cases of NFL players missing time due to blood clots. Take Carolina Panthers star right tackle Taylor Moton for example, who hasn't played at all this season because doctors found blood clots in his lung this summer. That situation required Moton to immediately be placed on blood thinners.
Moton having blood clots found in one of his lungs is a much more serious situation than superficial thrombophlebitis. It varies case to case, of course, but treatments for what Hurts has been diagnosed with can sometimes be simple.
Dr. Han: "Usually what we end up doing for standard of care is that within the first week, you can actually for a lot of patients and a lot of people, you can actually do conservative treatment, which involves things like anti-inflammatory medications, things like ibuprofen or naproxen, staying active, keeping the leg elevated, compression as sort of the first line.
"In these kinds of situations, we actually often think that the superficial thrombophlebitis is a self-contained issue. Usually what I do for my patients is that we do a follow-up scan either 7 or 14 days after the fact.  And if we see that the quality of the clot has changed, whether the clot is extended or it has moved or we do find it in deeper veins, then that kind of changes the equation for being more aggressive with treatments, which would include things as we typically do for deep vein thrombosis, the DVTs. That would be the full-on blood thinners, anticoagulants."
Dr. Han: "If it's for superficial thrombophlebitis, not every case needs to be treated with blood thinners. The cases that I treat with blood thinners are for patients that are have the clots that are getting longer or building up, so to speak, or if the patients are profoundly symptomatic with lots of pain that ibuprofen and warm compresses and elevating legs and wearing a compression garment is not cutting it. For those patients, then we do often think about reaching towards anticoagulants, blood thinners. Although the period for treatment for superficial thrombophlebitis is actually much shorter than what we would treat for DVTs. The treatment here is usually a month and a half, 45 days of treatment is sufficient, whereas the DVT sometimes is lifelong, sometimes it's between three to six months."
Everyone wants to know: when could the Eagles quarterback return to the field? Since this is not a worst-case scenario like deep vein thrombosis, we asked Dr. Han before Hurts was placed on injured reserve if there was any chance he could miss just one or two weeks
Two key factors are whether he requires blood thinners and whether this clot is indeed a self-contained issue.
Dr. Han: "It is possible. Again, just because I don't know the details of the case. The risk as I see it is being on a blood thinner and playing a contact sport would put him at extremely high risk of bleeding. And that's all bleeding complications -- blood trauma, but also internal bleeding. Oftentimes for athletics to this degree, it becomes a very strong safety consideration for being able to play or not. It's also a little hard for me to speculate if their phrasing for it -- 'It's moving' -- means that there are clots in other places, then the timeline for when he might come back is a lot harder for me to say.
"I would say the standard is if he was on blood thinners for just superficial thrombophlebitis that could be -- for symptomatic treatment -- that could be upwards of 45 days for treatment. But if there are extenuating circumstances that would have progressed or made it more dangerous or had turned into a deep vein thrombosis or something like that, then the treatment times could be much longer."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Eagles place Jalen Hurts on IR, as he deals with superficial blood clot
summary: Hurts is out indefinitely and will miss the game against the Panthers on Sunday, and at least three more
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles are placing quarterback Jalen Hurts , who is out this week with a superficial blood clot, on injured reserve, the team officially announced on Saturday , after consultations with numerous doctors and experts. Going on IR sidelines a player for at least four weeks, meaning Hurts will miss this weekend's game, as the team previously announced, along with three divisional games.
He will miss matchups against the Carolina Panthers , Dallas Cowboys, Washington Commanders and New York Giants . Hurts will be eligible to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22, but that doesn't mean he is guaranteed to be back then.
With Hurts out, Tanner McKee will be leading the offense , and rookie Cole Payton will be the backup.
The Eagles released a statement saying Hurts requested treatment on his calf four days after their Week 4 loss against the Los Angeles Rams . The Eagles performed an ultrasound on his leg after they landed in London for their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and found the superficial blood clot.
The team's medical staff determined he could play, and the team conducted a follow-up ultrasound where they found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation.
When he can play will be determined by his medical team, meaning he could miss more than just four games. Hurts is still working on the best treatment plan for the situation and the team believes it is treatable. Hurts and the team are both still looking into more options and are putting the quarterback's health as top priority.
Blood thinners are a main treatment for blood clots and a player cannot play while on that medication. Typically, a patient would be on blood thinners for six weeks, but if the clot is minor, it may be treatable with other measures, such as anti-inflammatories.
If the clot worsens, it could mean more time on blood thinners, which would, in turn, mean more time away from the field.
The Eagles added some security in the quarterback position this week, signing Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad.

title: NFL Week 6 player props, anytime TD best bets: Steelers' Jaylen Warren is on a heater

Sunday around the NFL , the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns will fight for the AFC North lead, while the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers face off under the lights in Lambeau Field. Get ready for another wild week.

This is a massive game for the Texans, who are looking to find a rhythm following their slow start and make up ground in the AFC South. I like Marks to score.
Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren has been on fire. Last Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , he racked up 188 total yards and two touchdowns -- becoming the first player since Herschel Walker in 1986 to score a 50-yard rushing touchdown and an 80-yard receiving touchdown in the same game.
Warren has actually recorded the second-most scrimmage yards (640) through five games in Steelers history, behind Le'Veon Bell in 2014, and has the third-most scrimmage yards in the NFL despite receiving the 17th-most touches (89). He's been a beast, and the Steelers' best weapon on offense.

He caught seven of nine targets for a season-high 83 yards last week against the Steelers, and also rushed for a touchdown. Warren has two of the Colts' three receiving touchdowns on the season, and he's Indy's most important weapon behind Jonathan Taylor .
It looked like Dalton Kincaid was going to be a pillar in Joe Brady's revamped offense, but the Buffalo Bills tight end has recorded seven yards receiving in each of the last two weeks. The NFL keeps chugging along, and as with every upcoming slate, injuries have become a central focus. Unlike previous weeks, where it feels like it's been more about who is out of the lineup rather than who is in it, Week 6 is more of a mixed bag on the injury front, which can be looked at as a glass half full.
However, if you're a Ravens fan, you're certainly not ecstatic about the latest injury developments as Lamar Jackson is slated to miss his second-straight game due to an ankle injury. That means Tyler Huntley will get another start after defeating the Falcons last Sunday night. Meanwhile, the Eagles are drowning in injury news and will also be starting a backup quarterback in Tanner McKee . This comes after the revelation that starter Jalen Hurts is dealing with a blood clot in his calf. He headlines what is a CVS receipt-sized injury list for Philadelphia this season.
But, as we mentioned, it's not all doom and gloom from an injury standpoint. Michael Penix Jr . (rib) has the green light to play for the Falcons, while it's not out of the realm of possibility that Caleb Williams makes his return to the Bears or A.J. Brown reinserts himself into the Patriots offense this week, either.

As for Ingram and To'oTo'o, they both practiced fully on both Thursday and Friday and seem more on the probable side of the questionable designation.

Caleb Williams was a full participant throughout the week of practice, but is officially questionable to make his return in Week 6. On Thursday, Williams told reporters he does "not know if I'm playing yet."
Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) was a full participant in practice on Friday and carries no injury designation, so the Falcons starter will play in Week 6 against Chicago. Atlanta won't have corner C.J. Henderson, however, as he's still dealing with a groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Ravens.
Baltimore will be without Lamar Jackson for the second straight week as he continues to deal with an ankle injury. The two-time NFL MVP has yet to practice since suffering the injury, and his absence will thrust backup Tyler Huntley into the starting role yet again. Meanwhile, Jurgens will miss Sunday's divisional matchup as he is still in concussion protocol. That'll likely result in Vega Ioane starting at center. On the bright side, Zay Flowers is good to go as he carries no injury designation after being limited on Thursday and Friday with a toe injury.
Cleveland saw Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Carson Schwesinger all return to practice on Friday in a limited capacity after missing the start of the week due to injury. They are each questionable to play, but that return to the field does leave the door open for them to play in Week 6.

title: Texans vs. Jaguars prediction: Marvin Harrison Jr. makes Houston debut in London
summary: Everything you need to know to catch a key AFC South game in London
full_text:
The Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars are across the pond this week. The Jags have back-to-back international games, both taking place in London.
They defeated the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week. The last-second win put them at 4-1 on the season, tied for the second-best record in the AFC.
The Texans come in with a bit different standing, sitting at 1-4, though, like the Jags, they are also coming off a win. Houston got their first win against the Tennessee Titans , who now sit at 0-5.
Jaguars London history: The Jags are pretty much London's home team, playing there at least once a year since 2013, with the exception of 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic, with an 8-7 record across the pond. Their first-ever game in England was in 2013, a loss to the 49ers at Wembley Stadium. Their first international win was their third of the kind, a 2015 game against the Bills . And of course, their most recent win came in Week 5 against the Eagles.
Marvin Harrison Jr. : The biggest news out of Houston is the addition of former No. 4 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr. joining the team. Harrison's time with the Arizona Cardinals didn't work out as expected, but he and the Texans are hoping a fresh start will be reflected in his stat line. What should help the WR make a quick adjustment to his new team is the reunion with quarterback C.J. Stroud , who he had great success with at Ohio State. Harrison will be one to watch this week as the Texans offense has the tall task of keeping up with a solid Jaguars offense. Stroud has played well despite their record, so adding Harrison could be huge for the Texans' offense.
Jaguars o-line vs. Texans defense: The Jags will be without left tackle Anton Harrison , who needs surgery. The offensive line will be going up against defensive end Will Anderson Jr. , who has 27 total tackles, 7.5 sacks, a league high, and one forced fumble and recovery this season. The Jags need to protect Trevor Lawrence, especially so he can continue to improve in his game-time decisions.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 9:30 a.m. ET Location: Wembley Stadium (Wembley, England) TV: NFL Network | Stream: fubo Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Jaguars -2.5 ( via DraftKings )
This one should go to the Jaguars, who have proven to be one of the top AFC teams this season. Divisional games are always interesting, so I think the Texans could make this an interesting one. The Jaguars struggled a bit against the Eagles, so they will need to shake that off and go back to how they looked at the start of the season. Jaguars: 30-13
