title: Bills vs. Raiders prediction: Can Las Vegas end losing streak? Everything to know for AFC matchup
summary: Everything you need to know to catch this AFC matchup
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills were expected to be one of the best teams in the AFC, while the Las Vegas Raiders were, well ... not. However, the Raiders have surprised everyone and started the season 3-0.
Their hot start has cooled down a bit, thanks to facing some heavy hitters in the conference. They lost their last two games, first falling to the Kansas City Chiefs ,30-27, in a hard-fought AFC West battle. Last week, they struggled against the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots , losing 45-17 and showing cracks in their unlikely season.
The Bills can relate to Vegas' last loss, because Buffalo's only defeat this season came against their AFC East rival. Buffalo lost to the Patriots 29-26 in Week 4.
Last week, the Bills squeaked out a win against the Los Angeles Rams in overtime, with a blocked kick saving the game for Buffalo.
Ball security: The Bills do well in many categories, but turnovers have been an issue lately. Bills have nine turnovers in the last three games, with four coming from Josh Allen . Last week, running back James Cook had a crucial turnover in overtime, and while it worked out in the end, it did add to the turnover problem building on Buffalo's offense. The Bills' turnover differential is -4, and the Raiders' is +3.
Offenses by the numbers: The Raiders' numbers are superior to the Bills' in the pass game, but Buffalo has them beat in the run game. The Raiders are seventh in the league in passing yards (1,317), while the Bills are 11th (1,249). Las Vegas is second in passing touchdowns (12), while the Bills are in the middle of the pack in the category (7). The Bills excel in rushing yards, ranking fourth in the NFL (790) and leading the NFL in rushing touchdowns (13). The Raiders have the fifth-fewest yards on the ground (410) and are toward the bottom in rushing touchdowns (2). Buffalo is tied for average points per game at 32.8.
Defenses by the numbers: The Bills have the second-worst pass defense in the league in terms of yards allowed (1,479), while the Raiders are fourth-worst in rushing yards allowed (703). Raiders Maxx Crosby is tied for third-most quarterback pressures in the NFL (36) and Vegas' 10 takeaways are tied for most in the league.
Date: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 4:25 p.m. ET Location: Allegiant Stadium (Las Vegas) TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bills -5.5 ( via DraftKings )
The Raiders were put in a difficult stretch, facing the Chiefs, Patriots and Bills back-to-back-to-back. While Vegas got off to a solid start this season, I think their recent stretch is a bit too much for them to attack. I think the last two losses may be hard to shake off. I think the Bills will start to shake off their ball security problems and Allen just seems to be unstoppable, even when he is committing turnovers. I'm picking the Bills here, but I think the Raiders will have a good fight in them. Pick: Bills 31, Raiders 24

title: Steelers vs. Buccaneers prediction: Both teams hoping to build off of impressive Week 5 wins
summary: Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
full_text:
If their Week 5 performances are any indication of what's on tap on Sunday, the Steelers and Buccaneers ' showdown might be one of the best on the Week 6 slate.
After dropping their first four games, the Buccaneers stunned the Cowboys in front of a prime-time audience. Tampa Bay's 24-16 win was spearheaded by Bucky Irving (who ran for a career-high 165 yards) and a defense that forced three turnovers.
The Steelers rebounded from a disheartening loss in Cleveland to post a double-digit win over the Colts last Sunday. The star of Pittsburgh's 34-22 win was running back Jaylen Warren , who became the first player since Herschel Walker (back in 1986) to have a 50-yard touchdown run and an 80-yard touchdown reception in the same game.
Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction.
With Baker Mayfield still on the mend, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third career start.
Daniels' first two starts were impressive. He completed over 70% of his passes in both games and showed impressive poise for a rookie. Against the Cowboys, Daniels completed a whopping 76% of his throws for 189 yards and a touchdown. He also took care of the ball after throwing two interceptions a week earlier against the Packers .
He doesn't rely on his legs, but Daniels uses them as an asset nonetheless. He took off seven times against the Cowboys and had 55 yards on eight carries against the Packers.
A key matchup will be Warren and the Steelers' running game against the Buccaneers' run defense.
Warren, who is averaging 5.9 yards-per-carry and is Pittsburgh's leader in rushing and receiving, will face a Buccaneers defense that is second in the NFL in fewest rushing yards allowed (364), rushing touchdowns allowed (2) and average yards-per-carry allowed (3.3). It should be noted that the Buccaneers' defense has faced the sixth-fewest run plays in the NFL.
Expect the Steelers to stay with the running game, even if it isn't bearing fruit early on.
The Steelers will be without receivers Michael Pittman (foot), Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) for Sunday's game. Fellow wideout DK Metcalf has been tabbed as questionable with an illness that kept him from practicing on Friday.
Last week, Pittsburgh's other pass catchers stepped up when Wilson and Skowronek exited early. Warren led the Steelers with 87 yards on six catches, rookie Germie Bernard set career-highs with six receptions and 80 yards, and tight end Pat Freiermuth caught two of Rodgers' three touchdown passes. Massive tight end Darnell Washington also caught two passes.
Pittsburgh will once again share a field with Danny Smith, a 32-year NFL coaching veteran who spent the previous 13 seasons as the Steelers' special teams coach. Smith joined Tampa Bay's coaching staff shortly after Mike Tomlin stepped down in January.
Rest assured that Smith will look to exploit the weaknesses in Pittsburgh's special teams, which has not been one of the Steelers' strengths so far. The Steelers' kickoff returners are averaging just 22.7 yards per return (which is more than three yards under league average). Chris Boswell, a former Pro Bowler and one of the NFL's most reliable kickers over the past decade-plus, has already missed three field goals this season.
The Steelers will have to overcome the absence of Skowronek, who was named to the Pro Bowl last season for his special-teams play.
Pittsburgh feasted on rookie quarterbacks under Tomlin, and while he is no longer the Steelers' coach, expect new Steelers defensive play caller Patrick Graham to follow Tomlin's blueprint.
The blueprint is pressure, which is the Steelers' calling card regardless of who the opposing quarterback is. Pittsburgh has unmatched depth at outside linebacker in T.J. Watt , Alex Highsmith , Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer . Expect each of them to find their way into Tampa Bay's backfield on Sunday. Score: Steelers 19, Buccaneers 13

We'll have last-minute picks for every game as well as five best bets.
Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami, and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6.
NFL odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
Things have certainly gone sideways for the Philadelphia Eagles as injuries have continued to pile up across the organization. This week, they'll be without starter Jalen Hurts after it was revealed that he's dealing with a blood clot in his calf. That'll thrust Tanner McKee in under center. McKee has started two games in his NFL career leading up to Sunday, but both were in Week 18, so this is his first taste of true action. He'll look to pull off the upset without his top running back, Saquon Barkley, who is out for this game due to a hamstring injury, but will have No. 1 wideout, DeVonta Smith. Even if all things were equal, we gave Carolina a shot to win in Philly because of a massive rest disparity between these two clubs. As Philly comes off of an international game in London last week, the Panthers were on the bye, so they have a clear rest advantage on top of being healthier.
Projected score: Panthers 26, Eagles 19 The pick: Panthers -3
This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog.
Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game.
Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +2.5
You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket.
Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7

Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. title: Avieon Terrell’s first start can reshape the future of the Falcons secondary
summary: Atlanta Falcons rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell is expected to make his starting debut on Sunday against the Chicago Bears, replacing injured C.J. Henderson. It marks a long-awaited starting debut for the team’s top selection in the 2026 NFL Draft and could give Atlanta a glimpse of a bright future for its secondary. Although Henderson is […]
full_text: Atlanta Falcons rookie cornerback Avieon Terrell is expected to make his starting debut on Sunday against the Chicago Bears, replacing injured C.J. Henderson . It marks a long-awaited starting debut for the team’s top selection in the 2026 NFL Draft and could give Atlanta a glimpse of a bright future for its secondary. Although Henderson is the player Terrell is stepping in for, most people want to swap out Mike Hughes, who will start opposite Terrell against the Bears. It’s been a rough year for Hughes, who has repeatedly been a punching bag, whether it’s Henderson or Avieon’s elder brother, A.J., manning the opposite spot. Per PFF , Hughes has allowed 288 receiving yards, the third-highest among all NFL corners. He’s also allowing a 69 percent completion rate, which stands out negatively for a Falcons defense that has allowed the seventh-lowest completion rate, 61 percent. Hughes, in particular, has struggled to prevent easy completions and explosive plays in zone coverage, allowing 83 percent of passes completed against him and 16 yards per attempt in PFF’s zone charting. But despite Hughes’ early-season struggles, the Falcons have been reluctant to bench him for Avieon Terrell. The team has been slow-playing Terrell’s development, unlike how it handled every other defensive rookie over the past two seasons under defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich. A.J.’s Week 2 groin injury gave the team every excuse to give Avieon a longer look over the past three games. Still, outside of platooning for a few series with both Henderson and Hughes, the team has been reluctant to give the younger Terrell brother a longer look. Now Henderson’s injury will force their hand. Avieon’s promising early returns Terrell has looked good both inside and outside, and Ulbrich recently expressed optimism about Avieon’s long-term outlook at outside corner. PFF’s charting shows the younger Terrell allowing just 58 percent of passes completed against him, dipping to 50 percent and just 4 yards per attempt when he’s playing in zone. Terrell was at his best in zone at Clemson, so it’s no surprise the early returns have been promising despite the small sample size of four zone targets. Ulbrich has repeatedly heaped praise on veterans like Henderson and Hughes whenever he’s at the microphone, but that often feels like standard coachspeak. Ulbrich is glowing about all his players, which can annoy other coaches . Still, because his defenses have been consistently getting positive results, Ulbrich gets a pass, especially since the Falcons have developed a legitimate pass rush for the first time in decades. However, the results could be even better if the team had better back-end coverage, and early signs suggest Terrell has enormous potential to provide that, especially if Hughes is benched in his favor. With older brother A.J. eligible to return to the roster off injured reserve next week, the Falcons could soon have two Terrell brothers manning both outside spots. This makes this weekend’s Bears game a critical one for Avieon’s near-term outlook. Depending on Sunday’s results, it could completely change the outlook for the Falcons secondary in the long term. Avieon is auditioning for 2027 and beyond Currently, the Falcons have Billy Bowman and Sydney Brown handling the team’s slot reps in nickel and big nickel, a role Avieon had before the former returned in Week 3. With Bowman and Brown holding down the slot role for now, Avieon’s immediate path to more playing time appears to be at outside cornerback. After this season, Henderson is a free agent, and Hughes has no more guarantees on his contract, giving Atlanta a natural opportunity to make a pivot at the outside spot in 2027. Avieon is the first to audition for that role, and should he pass, it becomes one less need the Falcons may be looking to address entering next offseason. However, if Terrell struggles against the Bears and in any subsequent games where he gets an extended look outside, he might be forced to bump back inside to the slot in 2027. That could prompt the Falcons to target a high-priced free agent as part of their offseason strategy to upgrade the roster, using a league-leading amount of cap space . Avieon can cause ripple effects across Falcons secondary Bumping Terrell back inside could change Bowman and Brown’s 2027 roles, as either could move to safety. Jessie Bates is also a free agent after this season, and the Falcons could look to get younger and cheaper at the position, depending on how the rest of 2026 goes. Terrell’s performance against the Bears could have ripple effects on the entire secondary this year and beyond. The Falcons have leaned into Terrell’s versatility so far, using him at both inside and outside, which makes sense given the team’s cornerback injuries and the fact that he’s still a rookie. But by 2027, the Falcons will need to start cementing a long-term plan for Terrell. Right now, it’s trending towards him being a strong option at outside cornerback. Whether Sunday’s Bears matchup is a temporary spot start or the early launch of a years-long starting streak, Avieon’s long-awaited audition has arrived. If the rookie delivers, he’ll give Atlanta another foundational piece in their secondary for years to come, matching the other young building blocks they’ve mined so effectively in recent drafts. Cornerback is the one defensive piece that has eluded the Falcons, but Avieon’s emergence means that the secondary’s bright future is finally at hand.

title: The Falcoholic Reacts: Improvement is needed in the dropback passing game
summary: Following Sunday night’s dramatic overtime game, national analysts focused on the Ravens’ resilience rather than the Falcons’ mistakes. It was understandable given Baltimore’s star power and status in the league. While the Falcons were unfortunate to fall short, the game still gave viewers a clear look at where Kevin Stefanski’s team failed to produce. They […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 11: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons looks to pass against the Baltimore Ravens during the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following Sunday night’s dramatic overtime game, national analysts focused on the Ravens’ resilience rather than the Falcons’ mistakes. It was understandable given Baltimore’s star power and status in the league. While the Falcons were unfortunate to fall short, the game still gave viewers a clear look at where Kevin Stefanski’s team failed to produce. They were all over the place trying to contain a heavy zone-based running game. The Ravens will run over plenty of teams with Derrick Henry leading the charge. It remains alarming how incapable the Falcons were at times of getting off blocks. The inability to convert pressure into sacks was frustrating against a backup quarterback. Missing several open-field tackles led to allowing more explosive plays. For all their defensive struggles, fans believe the issues in the dropback passing game need to be addressed the most. Michael Penix Jr. looked rattled by Jesse Minter’s varied looks and didn’t come close to converting in pure dropback situations on third-and-long. Although he started to connect with Drake London in the second half, the offense is too talented and well-coached to be completely overwhelmed. That forced the defense on the field for long stretches, leading to them collapsing late in the game. Penix Jr. has played well in his return, but his tendency to panic in the pocket under duress and struggle to create out of structure leaves the passing game somewhat limited. That is where he’ll need to improve, as well as the coaching staff’s ability to get more on early downs when they can’t impose their will on the ground. The disappointing loss hasn’t damaged the fanbase’s belief in the team’s direction, as they remain confident going forward. This result is brought to you by FanDuel Sportsbook.

title: Falcons vs. Bears series history: Win-loss record, matchup results
summary: The Falcons move back into NFC play in Week 6 and this time it’s a matchup against another team from the North against whom they’ve had a pretty even history. In 30 games even, the Bears have a slender 16-14 all-time lead. The Falcons of the 1970s were a pretty bad team, securing their first-ever […]
full_text: Photo by Jim Prisching/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images The Falcons move back into NFC play in Week 6 and this time it’s a matchup against another team from the North against whom they’ve had a pretty even history. In 30 games even, the Bears have a slender 16-14 all-time lead. The Falcons of the 1970s were a pretty bad team, securing their first-ever playoff appearance in 1978 and losing many games to many different teams. The Bears of the ’70s, however, were one team the Birds routinely found success against, going 5-2 in that period (one of those losses ironically in that ‘78 season which was Atlanta’s most successful of the decade) which, combined with back to back wins at the end of the ‘60s and another back to back in the first matchups of the ’80s, asserted what can be considered a decade and a half of dominance. That was promptly put to bed when the seemingly unbeatable 1985 Bears, led by the great coach Mike Ditka (who left a major hole in the sport of football with his passing last week), absolutely kicked Atlanta’s butt 36-0. That started a run of five consecutive Bears wins and eight wins in nine tries overall until a rookie Matt Ryan executed his Rookie of the Year moment with a game-winning drive to forge an improbable comeback in 2008. Chicago is currently on a run of four wins in the last six matchups which started in the 2010s. When these teams met last The Falcons and Bears were fading from postseason contention quickly, with Atlanta still having somewhat of a chance at 7-8 but really needing to win their last couple of games along with getting major help when they met the Bears at solider field on New Years Eve in 2023. We did not know it yet but probably could have guessed that this would be Arthur Smith’s penultimate game as head coach of the Falcons as he was really coaching for his job down the stretch. As such, things did not look too good for him when the Bears jumped out to a quick 14-0 lead in the freezing temperatures of Soldier Field. The Falcons had a meager 180 passing yards in this one and 75 of them came on a Tyler Allgeier screen pass he took to the house to limit the bleeding, but Justin Fields and the Bears offense just overwhelmed Atlanta’s overmatched defense. The Bears put up 37 points on the afternoon while Taylor Heinicke’s last pass of the day went for an interception before Desmond Ridder entered in relief in the middle of the blowout, before his own last pass of the day also went for an interception. Smith was fired one week later.

This Saturday, the cream of the crop will show up in multiple ranked matchups, along with a few ranked-vs.-unranked games featuring real talent that may pop up in the 2027 NFL Draft. Nick Marsh, WR, Indiana vs. Ohio State Memorial Stadium – Bloomington, IN – 12 pm EST – Fox Nick Marsh route salesmanship. Very snappy mover at 6025 & his head fakes at the top of the stem are so convincing pic.twitter.com/QeOrGcF5Ex — James Foster (@NoFlagsFilm) October 6, 2026 While Charlie Becker may be the more well-rounded prospect, Nick Marsh has the tools a quarterback like Michael Penix might find appealing. He wins on out-breaking routes; he snaps his head and hips at the top of the route, forcing separation and making himself an immediate target for quarterbacks who throw with anticipation, like Penix. Overall, Marsh projects as a solid X or Z receiver in a Tommy Rees offense, allowing Drake London to move around the formations and unlock even more production. Emmanuel Oyebadejo, DL, Florida @ Texas DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium – Austin, TX – 12 pm EST – ABC Florida DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo (6'6 299) was a basketball player in England before giving football a try first at University of Exeter, then Jacksonville state and now Florida He's still very raw but he also shows the traits of a starting NFL DL. Size/Power/Athleticism #NFLDraft pic.twitter.com/rtJt1NIDgj — Draft Capital Podcast (@TheDraftCapital) September 20, 2026 6’6”, 300 pounds is not supposed to move as it does for Florida defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. A former English basketball player, Oyebadejo is still a raw prospect who needs to learn some of the nuances of the defensive line. However, Oyebadejo already has the raw movement skills, power, and quickness needed to be a high-end prospect. Isaac Smith, S, Mississippi State @ LSU Tiger Stadium – Baton Rouge, LA – 12 pm EST – ESPN Isaac Smith from Mississippi State is a massive dude for a safety. I have some concerns about the lateral agility and overall athleticism for sticking at safety, so a move to linebacker could make some sense for the next level. pic.twitter.com/Wmn20bnQsu — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) May 20, 2026 Having a big body at safety is always an advantage; when that safety can play the run like a linebacker, it adds another layer of versatility to the defense. Isaac Smith is a big safety at 6’0”, 220 pounds, and he can come in on day one and add to the special teams unit with his ability to find a ball carrier and bring him to the turf. Xavier Gilliam, DT, Tennessee vs. Alabama Neyland Stadium – Knoxville, TN – 3:30 pm EST – ABC The Xavier Gilliam Auburn tape is some pretty electric stuff for an IDL. Reminds me of a lighter footed Walter Nolen. Sky's the limit. pic.twitter.com/uudcA32rUX — Cooper Petagna (@cooperpetagna) October 15, 2026 The Falcons have done a sensational job getting the most out of their defensive line, largely thanks to the synergy between defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich and defensive line coach Nate Ollie. Gervon Dexter and Brandon Dorlus are two of the best at the position right now at getting pressure on the quarterback, but adding a rookie like Xavier Gilliam to the rotation would be a dream come true. At 6’2”, 305 pounds, Gilliam is having the best season of anyone at the position; he has 11 tackles for loss, 22 QB pressures, and 16 run stops, according to PFF. Gilliam’s blend of speed and strength is extremely tantalizing. Patrick Kutas, OL, Ole Miss vs. Missouri Vaught-Hemingway Stadium – Oxford, MS – 3:30 pm EST – SEC Network Patrick Kutas (6’4 315) Ole Miss ✅ Wide base and stout anchor ✅ Technician on the line with great hand placement and strike timing ✅ Over 1,800 career snaps played entering the 2026 season ✅ Has logged snaps at every spot except left tackle during his career pic.twitter.com/B5wVFdEotk — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) June 18, 2026 The offensive line will need more depth as Stefanski’s offensive vision becomes clearer. Patrick Kutas has played every position on the line except for left tackle, dating back to his time at Arkansas. title: Falcons vs. Bears NFL Week 6 preview: Caleb Williams, Grady Jarrett, and what to expect on Sunday
summary: The Falcons take on the Bears Sunday in the first non-primetime game in weeks, and both teams are heading into this one with questions around the quarterback position. Michael Penix Jr. is expected to be fine to play on Sunday, despite leaving Week 5’s loss to the Ravens on Sunday Night Football with a rib […]
full_text: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Falcons take on the Bears Sunday in the first non-primetime game in weeks, and both teams are heading into this one with questions around the quarterback position. Michael Penix Jr. is expected to be fine to play on Sunday, despite leaving Week 5’s loss to the Ravens on Sunday Night Football with a rib injury. Penix said Wednesday that even though he experienced some discomfort during practice, he felt good overall and ready to play. Caleb Williams is a different story. Williams, who has been out for the past few weeks after suffering a hamstring injury, remains on the injury report but was able to participate fully in practice all week. Ben Johnson hasn’t committed to a starter, though, and Williams isn’t sure if he’ll play this week . That does make it a little more difficult to know what to expect on Sunday. Bill Zimmerman at Windy City Gridiron was kind enough to answer my questions about the Bears and give us a glimpse of how this matchup may go from a Bears perspective. If you’d like to check out my answers to his Falcons questions, you can find those here . If Caleb Williams starts this week—and I expect he will—what should the Falcons expect from him on the field? Well, that’s the million-dollar question, isn’t it? I mean, we’ve seen Caleb Williams play one game this season in good conditions, and the offense scored 59 points. We really don’t know how healthy he is at this point. Is he close to 100% or is he good enough to play? Now, before we fully dive into Caleb Williams, we have to at least look at the chance that he will not play. Caleb Williams said his status is uncertain, and Ben Johnson hasn’t committed to a QB. If Williams isn’t quite ready to play, the question is whether the Bears go back to Case Keenum after Tyson Bagent’s dreadful performance against the Green Bay Packers. It’s a unique situation where any of the three QBs could start on Sunday, but I do agree with you; I expect Williams to play. Williams is a rhythm QB and tends to get better as the game goes on. That being said, since he hasn’t played in a month and you have to figure, he will be a little rusty. You also have to wonder if he’s going to rely on his hamstring and be as fully mobile as he usually is, where he can escape the pocket and also take off and gain yards on the ground. If I tried to give you my best guess, I think Caleb Williams plays, and we see about an 85% version of Caleb where he tries to stay in the pocket a little more often and tries to operate in structure and does a little less of his scrambling around and play hero ball, which makes all the highlight reels. The Bears are 3-2 despite losing Williams to the hamstring injury for a few weeks — speaking for a fanbase that hasn’t seen any good backup quarterback play throughout this very weird start to the season, what’s their secret? There are a few things that have played into this, but the biggest thing is the running game. D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, behind a strong offensive line, took the pressure off Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent and kept the defense off the field. Monangai is out with turf toe, and the Bears don’t have a great RB2 to pair with Swift when he’s out, so that definitely was an issue against Green Bay last week. The Bears defense has also played surprisingly well in three of their five games. Can Dennis Allen keep the magic going against Atlanta? It’ll be even tougher because it looks like Montez Sweat (suspension), Dayo Odeyingbo (injury), and TJ Edwards (injury) are also out. Bears fans are hopeful that Kyler Gordon returns this week, and the Bears desperately need him. How should the Bears try to contain Bijan Robinson and the Falcons run game? I think the best chance is to convince Robinson the game is at 4:25 and steal his cell phone so no one can get a hold of him. I don’t think the Bears have the personnel to stop him if we’re being honest. Sweat is very good at setting the edge in the run game, but I don’t know how well that’s going to go with him out. Austin Booker doesn’t play the run as well as he rushes the passer. I think the Bears are going to have to try and load the box a little and hope the Falcons can’t beat them over the top with Drake London, something that Jordan Love did constantly even without the Bears packing the box. I have significant concerns about the Bears defense coming into this game with the injuries they have. I was honestly hoping Michael Penix was going to miss this one and stunt the Falcons offense. I think Bijan and Drake can both have big games on Sunday. The Bears OL is about middle-of-the-pack this season in QB pressures allowed, and the Falcons have been effective at pressuring opposing QBs this season even with depleted pass rusher ranks. How does Williams’ expected return change that estimation? That will depend on whether Williams has his usual mobility in the pocket. Last year, the Bears were one of the 10 worst teams in pressures allowed by one of the top 5 in least sacked. That was partially because Caleb occasionally holds onto the ball longer hunting for big plays, but the bottom line is Williams’ sack avoidance was so good last year that it prevented so many negative plays and was a huge help to the offense. If Williams has his traditional mobility, it certainly will help with the sack numbers. But overall, the Bears have a strong offensive line. It’s probably stronger at blocking the run than the pass, but there are plenty of concerns for the Bears heading into this game; I think their offensive line isn’t one of them. How do Bears fans feel about Grady Jarrett? We still love him here in Atlanta, and it’s going to be very difficult to root against him this week! When the Bears first signed Jarrett last March, Bears fans were tap dancing. Everyone was excited that Jarrett was going to boost their defensive line, but unfortunately, Jarrett’s 2025 was pretty rough and got plenty of fans agitated with his performance. Jarrett played through a lot of injuries during the 2025 season, and that probably played into his performance, but heading into last offseason, most fans (myself included) just looked at Jarrett as a guy the Bears just have to have for one more season before most of his guaranteed money was up and they could cut him after the 2026 season. All that being said, Grady Jarrett has played quite well this season. Jarrett isn’t the guy he was 6 or 7 years ago, but he’s making an impact this year. Jarrett may not be chalking up the traditional stats like sacks, but he is sixth among defensive tackles in pass-rush win rate and second in run-block win rate. Jarrett is winning his blocks and impacting the game in both the run and the pass. You asked earlier how the Bears can stop Bijan Robinson. A big part of it would have to be a pretty huge game from the former Falcon, Grady Jarrett.
author: Jeanna Kelley

title: NFL predictions: can Ravens run over injured Browns’ D-line?
summary: The Ravens are heading to Cleveland to take on the Browns in their first AFC North matchup of the year. Here’s how they can come home to Baltimore with a victory despite a second straight absence from Lamar Jackson. Offense Run the Browns ragged The Browns are fielding a bottom-10 run defense to start the […]
full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry (22) scores a two point conversion during the fourth quarter against Atlanta Falcons cornerback Mike Hughes (21) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Ravens are heading to Cleveland to take on the Browns in their first AFC North matchup of the year. Here’s how they can come home to Baltimore with a victory despite a second straight absence from Lamar Jackson. Offense Run the Browns ragged The Browns are fielding a bottom-10 run defense to start the 2026 season, a distant departure from previous units under Jim Schwartz. Injuries to defensive tackles Mike Hall, Mason Graham, and Kalia Davis have only exacerbated the issue. Hall and Davis are not playing on Sunday, and Graham seems more likely to join them after Cleveland elevated two DTs from their practice squad. Even if last year’s No. 5 pick plays, he will not be at 100%. The Ravens found a way to move the ball against a Falcons run defense that led the league entering Week 5 by running away from their imposing interior and attacking their injured edge. That mitigated the burden on Baltimore’s injured, re-shuffled offensive line. Declan Doyle will still send Derrick Henry on plenty of outside runs on Sunday, but he should be more confident between the tackles given the Browns’ injuries. Getting Tyler Huntley more involved in the run game should also be on the menu. He appeared to have room last week with Henry drawing the Falcons’ attention, but rarely kept the ball. The Browns’ linebacker will also be flowing to the middle to fortify their weakened line, which should create even more space for Huntley on the outside. Prepare for press The Falcons were comfortable rushing four, sitting back on coverage, and forcing Huntley to settle for underneath throws. That fit their existing defensive ethos and personnel, and for much of the game, it worked. Between Huntley’s indecision from the pocket, drops, and penalties, the Ravens struggled to mount long scoring drives. Expect a different approach from the Browns. Head coach Todd Monken is plenty familiar with Huntley from his time in Baltimore – and that includes his limitations. The Ravens try to give Huntley easy reads and high-percentage passes that minimize the impact of his relatively underwhelming arm and slow release motion. So the Browns will likely throw press coverage at the Ravens’ wideouts and force him to beat them over the top. Underneath defenders will likely be lurking for short, quick blitz-beaters, too, so Huntley will have to be careful when targeting his hot reads. Defense Get off the field on 3rd down The Browns’ run game has struggled to start the year, and Quinshon Judkins is coming in with an ankle injury. The Ravens defense should be able to control the game on early downs, which will set them up to face their biggest enemy of the 2026 season: third-and-long. Last Sunday’s game in Atlanta was almost comical. Baltimore would find a way to stuff Bijan Robinson and force third-and-long, only for Michael Penix to complete a pass beyond the sticks. Blitzes were not getting home, and coverage broke down after a few seconds. The Falcons kept spoiling the Ravens’ best efforts on early downs and extending their drives. Having Trey Hendrickson back on the field will be a fix of its own. He is by far the Ravens’ best individual pass rusher, and in his first three games, he showed a knack for executing line games with his teammates. That latter element has been lacking in his two-week absence, though Mike Green and Nnamdi Madubuike have still made a huge impact on their own. Those third-and-longs are the optimal time for Jesse Minter’s specialized pressure packages. Hendrickson will help, but his teammates need to do a better job of setting picks and freeing each other up for runs at the quarterback. Cleveland’s 11.3% sack rate leads the league, which might lend itself to sticking with a four-man rush and keeping numbers in coverage. But with Deshaun Watson’s 24.1% pressure-to-sack ratio among the worst in the league ( via Pro Football Focus ), Minter should still throw plenty of blitzes at Watson to get him to hold onto the ball and take costly sacks. Secure turnovers If the Ravens defense can execute on third down, they should be able to hold the Browns at bay throughout the game. But Sunday night’s win in Atlanta was a stark reminder of how turnovers can swing a game. The Falcons’ early fumble-return touchdown forced the Ravens to play from behind for virtually the entire game, while Kyle Hamilton’s overtime interception sealed the victory. Hamilton knows better than any other Raven the importance of finishing turnovers. He has infamously dropped several interceptions throughout his career, including an absolute sitter against the Browns in 2024 that would have won the game. Instead, it fell through his hands and Cleveland won on a late score. Contrast that with Hamilton’s play this year, which featured a fumble he forced and recovered on his own before last week’s pick. Every member of the defense needs to take advantage of turnover opportunities in the same way. Giving the Ravens offense shorter fields could help them build up a bigger lead early on and position Huntley and Henry to chew clock in the second half. title: Ravens activate Ja’Kobi Lane from IR, rookie WR to play vs. Browns
summary: The Baltimore Ravens activated Ja’Kobi Lane from injured reserve on Saturday, priming the rookie wide receiver to play on Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Lane, 22, is one of Baltimore’s most-hyped rookies in recent memory. The third round pick (No. 80 overall) dazzled throughout training camp and appeared to carve out the Ravens’ No. 3 […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Ja'kobi Lane #6 of the Baltimore Ravens lines up against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens activated Ja’Kobi Lane from injured reserve on Saturday, priming the rookie wide receiver to play on Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Lane, 22, is one of Baltimore’s most-hyped rookies in recent memory. The third round pick (No. 80 overall) dazzled throughout training camp and appeared to carve out the Ravens’ No. 3 wide receiver role entering the regular season. But he fractured his wrist after just 27 snaps in Week 1, forcing him to undergo surgery and landing him on IR for four weeks. Lane was designated to return on Wednesday and practiced in full all three days this week. Head coach Jesse Minter praised his rookie’s work ethic to be physically ready to play as soon as he was eligible. Baltimore’s receiving corps has played well in recent weeks, but Lane should still see plenty of opportunities in the offense. The unit lost blocking tight end Durham Smythe to a season-ending Achilles tear and rookie Matt Hibner for at least one week due to a hand injury. Mark Andrews is the Ravens’ best inline blocker now, and it might remain that way for the rest of the year. Lane’s 6-foot-5 frame was already expected to play a role in the red zone. now, he could be used as a big slot with Andrews taking on more inline work. The Ravens also signed linebacker Carl Jones to their 53-man roster, making him available to play in Cleveland. The 25-year-old has appeared in two games this season with 33 snaps, all on special teams. None of Baltimore’s core special teams contributors are injured, but Lane will not contribute in that phase, which could give Jones a role on Sunday.

title: AFC North Preview, Week 6: Bengals on bye as all four teams are above .500
summary: Updated Standings: Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1:00 pm EST The Steelers will look to string together consecutive wins for the first time this season after continuing to alternate victories and losses through five games. Pittsburgh is coming off a 12-point home win over the Indianapolis Colts, marking their first double-digit margin of […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 16: Mark Andrews #89 of the Baltimore Ravens scores a touchdown against the Cleveland Browns during the fourth quarter at Huntington Bank Field on November 16, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Updated Standings : Baltimore Ravens 4-1 Cleveland Browns 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1:00 pm EST The Steelers will look to string together consecutive wins for the first time this season after continuing to alternate victories and losses through five games. Pittsburgh is coming off a 12-point home win over the Indianapolis Colts, marking their first double-digit margin of victory so far in 2026. The Steelers showed more continued signs of offensive life, particularly in the run game led by Jaylen Warren (188 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns). Their opponent this week, the Buccaneers, have a much stingier run defense — allowing only 72.8 rushing yards per game (No. 2 in the NFL). Tampa Bay also ranks Top 10 in passing yards given up as well and, despite their 1-4 overall record, are coming off a strong win last Thursday night over the Dallas Cowboys. The Buccaneers will have a rest advantage and home-field advantage, so the Steelers will have their work cut out for them despite being favored to win. If the Steelers are stymied on the ground, the onus will turn to Aaron Rodgers and company in the passing attack. Rodgers has three passing touchdowns in three straight games. Pittsburgh’s defense will be facing undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, making his third start in-place of the injured Baker Mayfield. Daniels has been inconsistent as a passer and has thrown three interceptions but is a dynamic athlete. The Steelers will have to account for him in the run game in addition to running back Bucky Irving, who ran for 165 yards on 21 carries in Week 5. If the Steelers can key in on Irving in the backfield and force Daniels to beat them through the air, their defense should hold up well. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Cleveland Browns, 1:00pm EST The Ravens are coming off a third straight win, all by one possession, after securing a 30-23 overtime victory last Sunday night. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley, starting in place of Lamar Jackson (ankle) led two consecutive touchdown drives late in the game to erase an eight-point deficit. Huntley is set to start again this Sunday as the Ravens look to start 1-0 in the division with a win over the Browns. Baltimore has won three straight meetings against the Browns, two of which were 20+ point victories. However, the Browns have often played them tough, especially in Cleveland, so this won’t be a cakewalk by any means — especially without Jackson under center. Huntley will need to have another mistake-free performance and handle blitz packages well. The Browns will likely crowd the line of scrimmage and try to take away underneath passing routes, forcing Huntley to beat them with downfield throws. The Ravens are expected to get rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane back from injury in this game, which will provide another pass-catching weapon. Defensively, the Ravens will need to buckle down and limit points again. They allowed only 16 offensive points in last week’s win over the Atlanta Falcons. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has been at his best this season when blitzed and struggled more versus calmer pressure. That creates an interesting strategy dilemma for Jesse Minter. Regardless, the Ravens have done a good job limiting big plays in the passing game this year, which will come in handy against talented rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston. The Browns have other young playmakers that call for defensive attention as well. Cleveland Browns Matchup: vs. Baltimore Ravens, 1:00pm EST The Browns’ winning streak came to a conclusion last week after they dropped a 17-12 contest against the New York Jets. It was a sloppy offensive performance from both sides, but the Browns were in position to win after taking a lead in the fourth quarter, which they failed to retain or recoup. With the loss, the Browns dropped out of first place in the division, a spot they’ll look to get back by beating the Ravens this Sunday. This will be Todd Monken’s first game coaching against his former team, giving the Browns another source of extra motivation to win. Monken will look to attack a Ravens’ defense that ranks middle-of-the-pack in yardage and points allowed but is set to return a key piece in edge rusher Trey Hendrickson. The Browns’ offense has largely struggled this season, scoring the fifth-least points per game at just 18.6. Some of their most successful moments have come out of structure with Watson evading pressure and scrambling. Cleveland’s defense will be facing Huntley instead of Jackson, making for a much easier matchup. However, the Ravens scored 30 points last week, proving that their offense is still capable of producing with Huntley under center. The key for the Browns will be limiting Derrick Henry’s damage on the ground and taking away short-yardage throws. Huntley has rarely connected on deep throws in his career. The Browns will also need to find a way to keep the ball out of Zay Flowers’ hands as much as possible.

full_text: Oct 11, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley (5) celebrates with quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) after a touchdown during overtime against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Head coach Jesse Minter said that the decision was made in Jackson’s “best interest.” The 29-year-old quarterback has not practiced for the last two weeks due to an ankle injury suffered against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will get another start after leading the Ravens to an overtime win in Atlanta in Week 5. Jurgens, who arrived in Baltimore via trade from the Eagles last week, could not clear concussion protocol in time to play on Sunday. Rookie offensive lineman Vega Ioane will stay at center for one more game with a major question mark at right guard, where both potential starters – Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones Jr. – are listed as questionable. If neither can go, the Ravens could start Kyle Hergel, who signed in Baltimore after Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic were injured in Week 3. Also missing Sunday’s game are veteran defensive tackle Broderick Washington, who missed practice on Thursday and Friday, and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner, who suffered a hand injury against the Falcons. Hibner left the game and returned in a blocking-only capacity; Minter said that he would miss “maybe a week” and should not land on injured reserve. Here is Baltimore’s full Week 6 injury report: Out TE Matthew Hibner (hand) QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) C Cam Jurgens (concussion) DT Broderick Washington (ankle) Questionable G Emery Jones Jr. (knee) WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist, designated to return from injured reserve) G Andrew Vorhees (foot) The Browns ruled out five players, including defensive tackles Mike Hall and Kalia Davis. DT Mason Graham, linebacker Carson Schwesinger, and running back Quinshon Judkins retuned to practice on Friday in a limited capacity, leaving the door open for them to play on Sunday. title: 5 things Bills Mafia should know about the Raiders before Week 6 game
summary: The Buffalo Bills and their fans have taken Sin City by storm this weekend ahead of a Week 6 date with Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium Sunday afternoon. The Bills and Raiders will renew their AFL-rooted rivalry this weekend for the first time since the 2023 NFL season. To get us ready for Sunday […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - SEPTEMBER 17: Maxx Crosby #98 of the Las Vegas Raiders tackles James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and their fans have taken Sin City by storm this weekend ahead of a Week 6 date with Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium Sunday afternoon. The Bills and Raiders will renew their AFL-rooted rivalry this weekend for the first time since the 2023 NFL season. To get us ready for Sunday afternoon, I spoke with Matt Holder, who writes for Silver And Black Pride . An analytics guru with a great first name who has a wealth of experience in covering the Raiders and football, Matt Holder was very generous with his time this week to chat Bills-Raiders ahead of the big game. I highly recommend checking his work out in several arenas, which includes Pro Football Focus . Below, Matt and I talked shop about the Raiders, an ascending team that seems to have figured out things at head coach. Read on to find out all Matt had to say about first-time head coach Klint Kubiak, what makes tight end Brock Bowers and Las Vegas’ passing attack tick, and whether or not a shake-up is coming along the offensive line in Week 6. Additionally, we also cover ground on how best to attack the Raiders’ defense, and the best method to defend against LV’s offense. Plus, Matt lets us know the one key to victory should the Raiders find opportunity. My responses to Matt’s questions about the Bills can be found over at Silver And Black Pride. 1. The Raiders surprised many with their 3-0 start. Now at 3-2, what has the addition of Klint Kubiak meant for LV — and what’s different about this team that they can build on toward sustained success? Kubiak has changed the culture pretty quickly, and the results are showing on the field. The Raiders’ roster isn’t all that talented, but the team was doing the little things right to win games that many (myself included) didn’t think they were going to win heading into the year. It was pretty clear the team was much more well coached than they’ve been in the past, which gives confidence that the franchise has ended its long-time search for a long-term head coach. However, last week’s loss was pretty embarrassing and kind of felt like a reality check, so Kubiak still has plenty to prove in Las Vegas. 2. The Bills have struggled to stop teams’ passing attacks in 2026, with Brock Bowers and the Raiders’ eighth-ranked passing offense up next. How do the Raiders utilize Bowers and what else is key to powering their passing attack in tandem with Kirk Cousins? They aren’t the same type of player, so this isn’t a one-for-one comparison, but Kubiak is using Bowers similarly to what he did with Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Seattle last year. The 2025 Offensive Player of the Year would line up all over the Seahawks’ offense so that he could get favorable matchups. We haven’t seen Bowers deployed quite as diversely as JSN was a year ago, but he’s also only played in two games under Kubiak so far and is constantly at different alignments. It’s funny, despite being labeled as a “tight end”, the “ football robot from heaven ” has only been in-line on 13.6% of his pass snaps, per Pro Football F ocus . It’s kind of like how Sean Payton used to use Jimmy Graham, where Graham was split out wide so much that he tried to get wide receiver money when the Saints put the franchise tag on him back in 2014. Part of this is because Cousins has been either staring Bowers down (hard to blame him) or checking the ball down, but the Raiders are still looking for someone else to step up in the passing game. Wide receiver Tre Tucker can be a good deep threat, and he’s had one big game with five catches for 119 yards and a 40-yard touchdown in Week 2 but hasn’t done much outside of that. Tight end Michael Mayer and running back Ashton Jeanty would be the next in line since they can move the chains with their YAC skills, giving Cousins those check-down options. 3. Much has been made of the Raiders’ offensive line woes, with Kubiak even hinting at possible personnel changes. What’s gone wrong with the o-line and what, if anything, changes about LV’s offense with different in-house o-line personnel starting against the Bills? My hope is that they’re replacing starting left guard Spencer Burford. It’s funny you ask; my mailbag column that published on Saturday touched on this topic. Basically, he’s been the worst starting guard in the league when it comes to pass protection and is only average as a run blocker, which is causing problems with left tackle Kolton Miller, too. On top of that, right guard Jackson Powers-Johnson has been very inconsistent throughout his career and could also be on the chopping block, while center Tyler Linderbaum has been underwhelming. Linderbaum hasn’t been bad and isn’t getting replaced; he just hasn’t lived up to the historic contract he signed in the offseason. If Kubiak does make a change up front, second-year pro Caleb Rogers could slide in at right guard and rookie Trey Zuhn III could be on the left. Rogers got some action as a rookie last year and was solid, but he started in Week 4 against the Chiefs this season and had a tough time with Chris Jones. Meanwhile, Zuhn was cross-trained at nearly every offensive line position during training camp but has only been a jumbo tight end during the last few games and is questionable with an injury. 4. If you were game-planning against LV, what might film study have shown to be the best method when attacking their defense and defending against the Raiders’ offense? Defensively, the Raiders are very turnover-reliant. The unit doesn’t have a ton of talent, and first-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard has become a little predictable as a play caller. Leonard is running a variation of Mike Macdonald’s defense, but he’s still figuring out how to keep offenses on their toes. Vegas’ defense was able to create nine turnovers in the first three weeks of the season, but has just one during the two-game losing streak and has given up 75 points. If the Bills are safe with the ball, Josh Allen and Co. should have no problem putting points on the board. Offensively, loading up the box and getting pressure on Cousins has been the best formula so far. Kubiak is a good enough play caller to scheme his way out of it occasionally, but the offense is limited with Cousins’ lack of mobility and arm strength. He might beat you over the top on a few throws, but if the pass rush can heat him up, he’ll check it down or take a sack. In the running game, the offensive line isn’t good enough to handle loaded boxes and blitzes, while Ashton Jeanty isn’t 100% and hasn’t proven to be a back who can overcome some shortcomings up front. 5. What has to happen for the Raiders to defeat the Bills in Week 6? It goes back to my previous answer: create turnovers. I think the Raiders are going to have a tough time stopping Allen and the Bills’ offense, and the other side of the ball just doesn’t have enough firepower to keep up right now. But if the defense can get a few stops by getting Allen to play hero ball or force it down the field, and then punch the ball out from James Cook, the offense should have plenty of opportunities to at least stay within striking distance and put up points on a Bills defense that has struggled to begin the year. Keep an eye out for linebacker Nakobe Dean, who has forced three fumbles already this season. My thanks to Matt Holder for a tremendous discussion this week. You can check out more of his featured work at Silver And Black Pride , as well several additional outlets. Be sure to check out my Bills-focused side of the conversation over at Silver And Black Pride.

title: Buffalo Bills trending up, trending down: Brock Bowers is coming for Bills back seven
summary: The Buffalo Bills are coming off a Monday night win, 37-34 in overtime, over the Los Angeles Rams, and will play the second game in a row on the West Coast, this time against the up-and-coming Las Vegas Raiders. The Bills are listed as 5-point favorites, but the Raiders have the one player the Bills’ […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are coming off a Monday night win, 37-34 in overtime, over the Los Angeles Rams, and will play the second game in a row on the West Coast, this time against the up-and-coming Las Vegas Raiders. The Bills are listed as 5-point favorites, but the Raiders have the one player the Bills’ back seven has the most reason to fear: Brock Bowers. Here’s the big picture. Buffalo’s offense leads the league in scoring (32.8 points per game) and yards per play (6.7) and converts 50% of its third downs (26 of 52, second in the NFL), per Sharp Football. The Raiders’ defense allows 6.1 yards per play (28th) and has allowed 3.0 points per drive since Week 3 (30th). On the other side, Buffalo allows 28.2 points per game (28th), 21.8 passing points per game (31st), and a 6.5% touchdown rate (26th), and it has allowed multiple passing touchdowns in four of five games. Kirk Cousins is second in the NFL with 12 touchdown passes, and Bowers has 24 catches for 312 yards and three touchdowns in the three games since he returned from a meniscus procedure. A lot of players are banged up. Who needs to step up in Vegas to get the Bills to 5-1 before the bye? Heroes QB Josh Allen: MVP football with no No. 1 receiver DJ Moore didn’t play. Josh Palmer was out. The wide receivers who did suit up barely beat anybody: Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Skyler Bell combined for four catches on seven targets, and 57 of their 87 yards came on one Shakir play in overtime. Take that one away and the group had three catches for 30 yards. Josh Allen found other ways, though. The running backs caught six passes for 110 yards, more than half of his 210 passing yards, with Ty Johnson going 4-for-4 for 72. Buffalo ran 37 times for 234 yards (6.3 per carry) and three touchdowns. Allen added 10 carries for 121 yards and a score, and his 28.6% scramble rate was the second-highest of his career, per Sharp. The Bills had a season-low 146 team air yards and a season-low 49.1% dropback rate, and still scored 37 points against a defense that ranked third in EPA per play against the pass entering the night. We saw this last season, when the offense didn’t have a true No. 1 receiver, and we saw it again Monday with Moore on the sideline. Run the ball, use the backs, move the chains, and let the quarterback make the plays the receivers aren’t making. Allen finished with 331 total yards, two touchdowns, and the first overtime win of his career. If you’re building an MVP case, this is the game I’d put in the file. The Raiders are a good place for the formula to keep working. WalterFootball ranks their defense 24th in dropback EPA and 26th in dropback success rate. They have allowed 10 passing touchdowns in their last three games, and they have already given up rushing production to Malik Willis (39 yards and a touchdown), Tyler Shough (36), and Drake Maye (25 and a score). Moore and Palmer could both be out again. Allen’s arm doesn’t have to be the whole answer. OT Dion Dawkins: the Bills need his best version again to keep Crosby and Koonce off Allen I’ve been critical of him. Dion Dawkins bounced back at the right time. After a rough game against New England, with a sack allowed, a play that could have been a safety, and two penalties, PFF graded him 86.9 against the Rams, second-best on the team, with Alec Anderson third at 79.1. Aaron Donald graded 49.3 in the same game, per PFF, and Los Angeles finished with one sack and one quarterback hit on Allen. That is the kind of night this line has to repeat on Sunday. Las Vegas certainly can rush the passer. Maxx Crosby has 36 pressures this season, tied for third in the NFL, and Malcolm Koonce has 16 pressures on 100 pass-rush snaps through Week 5. Crosby has only a half-sack in his last four games but 22 pressures over that stretch, so the production is coming. The Raiders rush four on 76.6% of dropbacks, the second-highest rate in the league, and their pressure rate jumps to 63.4% when they blitz, the highest in the NFL, per TruMedia. Crosby has lined up across from the right tackle on 78.6% of his snaps, per Next Gen Stats, so Spencer Brown will see most of him. Brown left Week 5 after 15 snaps with a back injury, but practiced fully on Thursday and Friday and will play. Koonce is on the other side, which is Dawkins’ side, and the Raiders move Crosby around enough that the left tackle will see him too. With Moore and Palmer both questionable, Buffalo’s plan is the same one that worked Monday: run the ball, protect Allen and let him extend plays. Every one of those starts with the line. If Dawkins plays like he did against the Rams, Crosby and Koonce don’t get to Allen often. If he doesn’t, Allen is back to saving the offense on his own and could be in trouble. Head Scratchers RB James Cook: hate to have him there, but the fumbles must stop Jimbo is playing excellent football. He has 532 rushing yards through five games (third in the NFL) at 5.6 yards per carry with five touchdowns, he ran for 111 yards and two scores on 25 carries Monday, and he has been the NFL’s leading rusher since the start of 2025. Buffalo leads the league in runs of 10 or more yards (19.0% of carries), and the Raiders have allowed the sixth-most rushing yards to running backs. Cook should be a huge part of this game plan. Here’s why James Cook is on this list, though. He fumbled twice against the Rams and has four fumbles in five games, the most in the NFL, and 11 since the start of 2025, the most of any non-quarterback, per ESPN. He lost one two minutes into overtime with the Bills in field-goal range, and only Rousseau’s block kept it from costing them the game. Joe Brady took the ball out of his hands in the closing moments and warned him afterward that “the carries are gonna decrease” if it doesn’t improve. That is the head-scratcher, and it’s the only reason he’s here. If the fumbles continue, Buffalo won’t be able to use him as much as it wants to or needs to, and the carries go to Ty Johnson and Ray Davis. The offense is better with Cook on the field. He has to eliminate the problem for that to stay true. S C.J. Gardner-Johnson: Bowers and Mayer are coming for the whole back seven C.J. Gardner-Johnson graded 29.3 at PFF against the Rams, second-lowest on the team, after giving up multiple big plays, including a touchdown. He is the name on this list, but the problem is bigger than him. Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, Gardner-Johnson, Cole Bishop, and Damar Hamlin have been shaky in coverage, and the communication bothers me even more than the individual grades. When a Linebacker and a Safety pass a receiver between them and nobody takes him, a good offense turns that into a first down. Monday is what that costs: Matthew Stafford went 40-of-54 for 383 yards and three touchdowns, Puka Nacua caught 17 passes on 24 targets, and Tyler Higbee caught five of his six targets for 83 yards. Sunday’s test is a different animal. Bowers has a touchdown in all three of his games and 100 yards in two of them, including eight catches on 10 targets for 110 yards in the 45-17 loss in New England. Michael Mayer, the second Tight End, has 21 catches and is the Raiders’ third-leading receiver, and Klint Kubiak’s offense is expected to run two-tight-end sets regularly. Tre Tucker, their top Wide Receiver, is fourth on the team with 19 catches. This offense goes through the middle of the field, and the middle of the field is where Bernard, Williams, Gardner-Johnson, Bishop, and Hamlin live. Buffalo has allowed 300 yards to Tight Ends in five games, the 10th-most in the NFL, per Pro Football Reference, and the group it has faced is Dalton Schultz, Sam LaPorta, and Hunter Henry. Jim Leonhard called Bowers a problem this week and said the whole plan for the Raiders’ offense has to start with him. If there is a blown assignment, Bowers will make the Bills pay for it. Honorable Mentions Trending Up: OLB Greg Rousseau: He blocked the 48-yard field goal in overtime that kept Buffalo alive,…

title: Bills game-day food: Buffalo Hardtack for Week 6 at Las Vegas Raiders
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. Hardtack So last week I deviated things a bit and the theme started with a nod to the mascot (then worked in the city). I had fun with that, and with the Las Vegas Raiders game up I asked the question we all want the answer to this week. What did pirates eat? Well kids, on long sea voyages you needed food that wouldn’t spoil, had high calorie density, and you could easily make and store. Hardtack is exactly that. Used for long voyages and as a survival food, hardtack is made from flour, water, and sometimes a little salt. Not to be confused with a cracker or type of actual bread, hardtack is more like concrete that will keep you alive. Intended to be dipped and softened before consuming, traditional hardtack is mostly flavorless. Not mine. You still NEED to dip it/dunk it, but it should enhance what you’re pairing it with not just absorb it. Buffalo Hardtack Makes: About a dozen biscuits Active time: 20 min Total time: About 3 hours Ingredients 3 cups all-purpose flour, divided 1/3 cup hot sauce (see below) 2/3 cup water 1 tsp honey 1/4 tsp cumin 1/2 tsp onion powder 1/2 tsp garlic power Essentials: Measuring cup and spoons, mixing bowl, rolling pin, baking sheets, pizza cutter, fork, a love of adventure and long journeys Preheat oven to 250ºF Thoroughly combine 2 cups flour, hot sauce, water, honey, cumin, onion and garlic powder in mixing bowl. If the dough is still sticky, continue adding flour (about 2 tablespoons at a time) until no longer sticky (very slight tacky is OK); you might not need all three cups. Dust counter or other surface with flour; roll out dough to about 1/4-inch thickness. Segment dough into 3-inch by 3-inch squares using pizza cutter, if you want to be traditional (but smaller is fine too). Poke holes into dough with fork (see below); place dough segments onto baking sheet. Bake in preheated oven for about 3 hours, flipping every 30 min. Remove from oven and allow to cool; serve with some sort of liquid, such as soup. Wingin’ It tips Hardtack recipes typically call for thicker dough as it’s better for long-term storage. If you’re actually planning to do so, some recipes call for 1/2-inch thickness. The thinner version makes it a little easier to soften and eat. I even experimented with really thin to make crackers for adding into soup and the like. How long will this keep if you want to store it? If you’re a purist and use just water, flour, and salt; apparently there is Civil War-era hardtack on display at a few museums still believed to be not be spoiled. I chose ingredients that should retain shelf stability in that they can be dehydrated well. For the hot sauce, avoid anything with pulp. The standard sauce for wings is Frank’s, and that’s an excellent choice for this. The seasoning is already powdered, and honey is also known for shelf stability. That said, because I don’t want anyone to run with this and do something foolish, store this in an airtight container and I wouldn’t personally keep it around longer than a few weeks. As for tips, I did add food coloring to mine to add a little flair. If you look closely you can see a little swirl of pink. Speaking of coloration, because of the hot sauce and food coloring, the top the “biscuits” or “slabs” as I think of them got real pale, real quick. The bottom stayed a salmon pink with a little browning toward the end. Research indicates this is pretty normal. Here’s a picture gallery to give some idea of the process in case you’re a visual learner. And scope out the two I made with special shapes for the occasion. For my final thoughts; I want to express exactly what the hardtack experience is using the bread continuum, as it’s technically a type of bread. Have you ever dipped a slice of bread into soup? You know how you have to dip real quick and take it out so it doesn’t disintegrate? Yeah, that’s not this. You know with croutons in soup how you might put them in a few at a time so they don’t dissolve over time? That’s not this. Have you ever crumbled crackers into soup and they’re mushy kinda quick but hold together? Yeah, still not there. What about a whole cracker? Have you ever dropped one in and it gets floppy after a minute and falls apart? Yeah, that’s not hardtack. No. With this stuff (and remember mine is half the thickness most recipes call for); I put a “biscuit” into an entire bowl of soup right at the beginning. It was the last thing I ate. I could break it with my spoon. It was not floppy. It did not crumble. I still had to chew carefully. That said. It was delicious. Just more like flavorful concrete than a true bread. Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! Skarekrow likes certain products. Skarekrow likes money. Skarekrow recommends the following products and hopes you buy them from these links, which might result in Skarekrow getting money. Melinda’s Hot Sauces! Ninja Kitchen Appliances!
