title: NFL predictions: 3 bold takes for Bills-Raiders Week 6 game
summary: The Buffalo Bills have taken their show on the road out west, already winning a thriller against the Los Angeles Rams in primetime last Monday ahead of Week 6 at the Las Vegas Raiders. After sleepwalking through a first half in SoFi Stadium where quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills’ could do nothing to move […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball and gets tackled by Maxx Crosby #98 of the Las Vegas Raiders during a game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have taken their show on the road out west, already winning a thriller against the Los Angeles Rams in primetime last Monday ahead of Week 6 at the Las Vegas Raiders. After sleepwalking through a first half in SoFi Stadium where quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills’ could do nothing to move the football, the offense came alive late in action to break a winless overtime curse that spanned seven previous attempts. The catalyst for that surge was of course Allen himself, and he took over the game like few others can do against an NFL defense. Given Buffalo’s challenges on defense and its inability to stop almost any passing attack, Allen’s had to elevate his game to another level in 2026. That means there’s very little from Allen’s game that should come as a surprise. The man knows how to wear a cape and he’s done so with aplomb since taking over the reigns as QB1 for the Bills. That’s especially true early this season, partially out of necessity due to a defense unable to stop most opponents. With that in mind, how does one lay claim to a bold prediction about Josh Allen, if it’s not one that speaks to a lack of production? Well, I might have one idea to offer. Let’s dive in, starting with a bold take on Allen, well… at least leading off with a spicy take . Spoiler alert: There’ll be no bold claims made below of Buffalo’s defense. Without any intent to take away from all that outside linebacker Greg Rousseau has accomplished, it’s pretty obvious that we need to see it before believing most things true of the defense. Josh Allen stops fighting mechanics … and allows Josh Allen to be Josh Allen. Discussing his play after Monday Night Football , Allen’s self-reflection offered a glimpse at what might have been holding him back: “Early on, just didn’t feel like I was in a rhythm — wasn’t taking some of the underneath stuff. You know, fighting, mechanically, some stuff right now that I’m working on. But I felt like in that second half I got into a rhythm.” Allen is already discussed as among the greatest quarterback to play professional football, yet his statement about “ fighting, mechanically, some stuff ” is revealing. It’s also a perhaps a teaching moment for outsiders, as one that offers a pretty good alibi for his play in the first half against the Rams. It’s evident that second half in Los Angeles featured a more lock-in version of Allen, someone who was playing more instinctual football that allowed him to operate in better rhythm unsaddled by any critical focus on mechanics. Allen would later refute the idea that it’s unusual for him to be battling mechanics in-season , stating that it’s likely something “every quarterback fights throughout the year — it could be as simple as one thing.” In recent weeks, Allen’s decision making has come under a bit of fire thanks to a pair of ill-advised arm punts. One doomed a shot at winning, while another ended hope of putting up points before halftime. Were those decisions borne out of being hyper-focused on mechanics, or the result of throwing caution to the wind, mechanical flaws be damned? It’s possible both things are true, but many people will tell you that the most dangerous version of Allen is the one where he’s in a zone, playing instinctual football. Almost no one can touch him, figuratively and literally. Allen fueled almost exclusively by instincts may carry a turnover or two, but there’s a far better chance he’s scoring four or more touchdowns in such a state. I believe this is the version of Allen we see in Week 6. He may very well spend quite a bit of time on mechanics during the lead up in-week, but it’s a practice that should be put to bed at kickoff. This isn’t a situation akin to Tim Tebow’s, where he had major fundamental flaws as a passer. The amazing thing about Allen is his ability to make incredible things happen out of thin air, where other quarterbacks often fail due to mechanical breakdowns or otherwise. Allen has made incredible strides as a quarterback, thanks to the work he puts in to improve. We’ve seen what efficiency brings to his game, especially when there’s a talent void at wide receiver. His feeling the need to focus acutely on mechanics may be limiting Allen’s play. Instead, refusing to fight mechanics should allow Allen to play more free. It likely keeps Allen out of a headspace that binds him up while also playing voodoo with his internal clock. Allen himself will tell you the only thing that matters is getting a win. His play late against the Rams is all the evidence you need to understand that a fire-breathing unicorn is at its best when unbridled . Sunday feels like a “get right with himself” game for Allen. Look for Allen to play with less restraint early in Las Vegas, but don’t go in expecting him to detrimentally throw caution to the wind. In two games against the Raiders, Allen has played well. In two wins, Allen’s completed 55-of-71 passes for 562 yards with five touchdown passes and no interceptions. Where he hasn’t made as much impact is as a rusher, gaining just six yards on six carries. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook aren’t bothered by that stat, currently listing Allen with the best odds (-175) of scoring a rushing touchdown at any point in the game. He’s also the current co-leader with running back James Cook III (+350) as odds-on-favorites to score two-plus rushing (or receiving) touchdowns. Which leads to my next point… Keon Coleman excels as featured WR Under head coach Joe Brady, the Bills want to play high-level football where they’re constantly in pursuit of points and attacking a defense from the start. We’ve seen that in Brady’s preference for starting on offense when winning the coin toss. “Put the ball down” is this years mantra, fit for an oval car magnet. Brady wants the team to take the ball and score at every opportunity, and to stress defenses with a deadly and complete passing attack. Yet since Week 3, the long pass has been a struggle. Well, at least passes traveling a ton of distance in the air. Much of that has to do with wide receiver DJ Moore’s shoulder injury and the way defenses are playing tight end Dalton Kincaid. Where early on Moore and Kincaid helped fuel each other’s success thanks to the honesty teams had to utilize in covering both players, now Kincaid seems to have disappeared alongside Moore. To add insult to injury, now wide receiver Joshua Palmer is dealing with his own shoulder injury. Despite that, the Bills deploy the most explosive offense in the last decade . A key part of that fact is due to the emergence of wide receiver Keon Coleman. Once thought of as a potential trade candidate, Coleman has blossomed in year three. He continues making “wow” catches despite added coverage cheating his way with Moore sidelined. There’s plenty of meat on the bone still for Coleman to steal, and I expect him to be deployed as a true WR1 against the Raiders. Buffalo must figure things out with Kincaid, and the coaches should play it safe with Moore. They should also continue involving Shakir early, which could help calm the tsunami known as Maxx Crosby. All of those things should happen while trying to establish Coleman as the top target in the downfield passing attack. Through five games, Coleman has made 15 catches on 18 targets for 224 yards and two touchdowns. That’s a highly efficient stat line, which is made more impressive by his 11 catches for a first down. Coleman has proven to be reliable and an important part of the passing game in 2026. Last week he saw just two targets, with his lone catch going for seven yards and a touchdown. Expect to see Coleman worked into the plans well before crunch time on Sunday, even if…

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch at Las Vegas Raiders
summary: The Buffalo Bills are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders for just the second time in their history in the state of Nevada. In the first matchup between these two teams in Las Vegas, the Bills beat the Raiders 30-23 in an empty Allegiant Stadium thanks to COVID regulations in place for the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders for just the second time in their history in the state of Nevada. In the first matchup between these two teams in Las Vegas, the Bills beat the Raiders 30-23 in an empty Allegiant Stadium thanks to COVID regulations in place for the 2020 season. The stadium will be far from empty come Sunday, as the Bills will face a resurgent Raiders squad that’s off to a better start than anticipated. The team won its first three games this season before dropping contests to the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots in consecutive weeks. Can the Bills make it a three-game losing streak for the Raiders? There will be plenty of factors leading towards Buffalo’s ultimate success or failure in that endeavor, but one thing is certain: The Bills would love to enter their bye week at 5-1. Here are five players to watch this week as they attempt to attain that goal. _____________________________________________________________________________ James Cook III At the risk of beating a proverbial dead horse, this is a big week for Cook given his case of fumblitis he’s developed over the last 23 games. Cook has nearly as many fumbles (4) as he does touchdowns (5) this season, and he’s averaging a fumble on every 44 touches since the start of the 2025 regular season. When asked earlier this week, head coach Joe Brady said that, eventually, Cook needs to start protecting the football if he expects to play the snap share and maintain the carry share that he has over the last calendar year. Cook is obviously a dynamic runner—he’s averaging 5.6 yards per carry and already has 15 rushing attempts of ten yards or more this season—but his turnover rate is a tremendous concern. Will the fumbles be in his head? The Raiders will clearly have scouting information about the success of “Peanut Punches” on Cook, so they’ll likely be ripping and punching at the ball every time he touches it. Another thing I’m interested in watching is what happens to Cook if he does put the ball on the ground again. Will Brady follow through on his threat to limit Cook’s touches and snaps if it happens? TE Dalton Kincaid Where is he? Obviously, opposing teams are going to bracket him, especially if wideout DJ Moore isn’t on the field. That’s a pretty common tactic for any defense against any opposing player’s best receiving option. My concern is just how easily Buffalo, and Kincaid, allow their top receiver to be removed from the game. Joe Brady has to scheme some easy-button targets for Kincaid early to give him some rhythm and flow for the game. Just look at how badly the Buffalo passing attack struggled last week against the Los Angeles Rams in the early moments of the game as an example. It will help quarterback Josh Allen to settle into the contest if he can find some easy completions early. Kincaid is his best option. The Bills can’t let him be entirely erased like he has been for the last two games. DL T.J. Sanders The big fella made his presence felt in his 2026 season debut, and it’s pretty clear that the coaching staff views him as an important part of the defensive line rotation given his heavy usage. Sanders played on 51 snaps last week, trailing only Deone Walker (63) in playing time among Buffalo defensive linemen. Sanders rewarded the coaches by notching five tackles, adding a sack to thwart a two-point conversion attempt that might not appear on the stat record, but it does go down as an absolutely massive play in the game. Sanders looked strong, quick, elusive—all the things the Bills wanted from him when they traded up to select him at No. 41 overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. With Ed Oliver likely sitting again this week, expect a heavy dose of Sanders again against the Raiders. Inside Linebackers My goodness, can somebody just make a play? Dorian Williams looks fine on run downs and lost on passing plays. Terrel Bernard is a step slow and constantly involved in some sort of communication snafu with safeties and slot corners in coverage. I know that the coaching staff has said repeatedly that the linebackers are playing their assignments , but there’s no way that Brady and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard can watch the games and the film, and then still say that the middle level of the defense is performing well. The Bills were absolutely smoked in the intermediate levels last week, and while we could point at Puka Nacua and his incredible ability as a reason for that, the assignment isn’t easier this week. Tight end Brock Bowers is a stud, and fellow tight end Michael Mayer isn’t a slouch, either. One of Buffalo’s two veteran ILBs needs to start doing something on the field, or else they’re likely going to start watching someone like rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr take their place. CB Dee Alford Will he play this week? Given that the Bills released Anthony Kendall, who was signed from the practice squad and manned the slot last week, I assume that Alford will be ready to roll this Sunday. Kendall, for what it’s worth, looked no worse than the Bills’ other options in the slot so far this season, so it’s good that the team was able to re-sign him back to the practice squad. Alford started to look more comfortable against the New England Patriots before an ankle injury caused him to miss last week’s matchup. He’s probably have to deal with some big bodies in the aforementioned tight ends this week, but he also may find himself matched up against a speedster in Tre Tucker. He doesn’t operate much from the slot, but it’s a way that the Raiders can manipulate matchups and take Tucker away from someone like Christian Benford this week. If Alford is good to go, it helps Buffalo’s defensive depth. If he can play well on top of it, it will help the defensive unit tremendously.

Friday injury report pic.twitter.com/2PdAgLReXT — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 16, 2026 Both D.J. Moore and Joshua Palmer are questionable after a limited day of practice on Friday. Neither of them played in last week’s Monday night marathon game. Ed Oliver practiced for the first time in two weeks. It was limited, but it was practice. Now the Bills’ defensive tackle is listed as questionable with the knee injury that kept him out of Week 5. T.J. Sanders had an emergency appendectomy a couple of weeks ago. He got back to work quickly, missing just two games. But then he collected a shoulder injury last week in Los Angeles. He spent the first two practices of this week limited but was listed as a full participant on Friday. Despite the upgrade, the Bills listed him as questionable for game day. Then there’s Dee Alford. The only nickel cornerback on the roster missed a game and a half after injuring his ankle in Buffalo’s loss to the New England Patriots in Week 4. He was limited all week this week and is, of course, listed as questionable for Sunday. Last week the Bills signed Anthony Kendall from the practice squad to the active roster. Not an elevation, a signing. Not only didn’t they send Alford to Injured Reserve, the released Kendall on Monday (they signed him back to the practice squad on Tuesday after the third year corner cleared waivers). title: NFL predictions: Panthers and Eagles are two injured teams trending in opposite directions
summary: The Carolina Panthers are set to take on the Philadelphia Eagles in a contest that may well be decided by who can put eleven players on the field for every snap. Injuries abound on both sides, but the teams do appear to be trending in opposite directions for the moment. The Panthers are slowly getting […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after a touchdown against the Detroit Lions during an NFL football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are set to take on the Philadelphia Eagles in a contest that may well be decided by who can put eleven players on the field for every snap. Injuries abound on both sides, but the teams do appear to be trending in opposite directions for the moment. The Panthers are slowly getting healthier after a fortunate early bye week, while the Eagles are continuing to fall apart as they return home from a game in London just last week. It seems particularly rude for the NFL to pit a jet-lagged Eagles against a Panthers team that just had a week off, but that’s just the kind of thing that you have to expect in s 17-game season filled with as many international games as they can squeeze in. Does that mean the Panthers are expected to win? Yes, more or less. They have opened on FanDuel as 1.5-point underdogs and have moved to -3.5 point favorites on the eve of the game. Does that mean that we, the long suffering and well meaning staff here at Cat Scratch Reader expect them to win and win easily? Of course not. We’ve watched the Panthers before. Staff predictions for Week 6 Walker Clement Panthers 17, Eagles 21 – NFL Teams are 0-4 coming off of an international trip while facing an opponent coming off of a bye. The Nick Sirianni -Eagles are a baffling 0-6 as underdogs over five years. The Panthers are facing a back up quarterback and an off-the-streets running back rotation. It’s too good to be true. Prove me wrong one more time and I’ll start to believe, Bryce, but we’re not to “trust” just yet. Jonathan DeLong Panthers 20, Eagles 13 – The offense struggles against a good Eagles defense but are able to take advantage of a depleted Eagles attack. Brian Beversluis Panthers 14, Eagles 17 – Panthers lose 17-14 because Panthers reasons Daniel Belton Panthers 34, Eagles 14 – With the lack of offensive players, the Eagles struggle to put points on the board while Bryce Young continues dicing up defenses Eric Buchanan Panthers 23, Eagles 17 -The Panthers take advantage of the extra week and look more prepared versus a team suffering from injuries and a post international game hangover. Andrew Sweat Panthers 30, Eagles 24 – The Eagles haven’t scored more than 24 points in a game this season. The Panthers are averaging 30 points per game and getting healthier. title: 5 Questions with Bleeding Green Nation
summary: The Panthers are back and they’re facing what’s left of the shockingly 2-3 Eagles as they return from a game in London just six days ago now. Tomorrow we’ll see if they are awake and healthy enough to contend with a Panthers squad that should be freshly rested from their early bye week. To see […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee #16 looks on during the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 4, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Panthers are back and they’re facing what’s left of the shockingly 2-3 Eagles as they return from a game in London just six days ago now. Tomorrow we’ll see if they are awake and healthy enough to contend with a Panthers squad that should be freshly rested from their early bye week. To see what other storylines and shenanigans we should be on the lookout for this week, I spoke with Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to get the inside scoop on the Eagles quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and edge injuries, among other concerns. It really does sound like only one team is going to walk into this game on two feet and that may surprisingly be the Carolina Panthers. Here’s what Brandon had to say. With Jalen Hurts out for the game, what’s next for the Eagles at quarterback? Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers. It’s been a pretty weird run for him dating back to Week 18 of last season. Prior to that regular season finale, there was optimism about McKee’s outlook. He had previously shined in preseason settings; so much so that the Eagles decided to rest him after their first preseason game last year. With the Eagles deciding to rest starters in Week 18, McKee got the start and there was hope that he might be able to beat the Washington Commanders. He looked good early on in the game before DeVonta Smith left … but then much less so afterwards. It seems like this performance shook the team’s confidence in him because they went out and acquired Andy Dalton from your Carolina Panthers. (Great deal by Dan Morgan.) It was originally thought that Dalton was only being brought in to be QB3 behind Jalen Hurts and McKee … but in OTAs it became apparent that there was a real QB2 battle going on. With neither candidate making a strong case over the other, that battle continued into the lead up of the Eagles’ Week 1 game. Dalton was Hurts’ backup for the first three weeks before his sole passing attempt with the team was intercepted in the end zone during the Eagles’ Week 3 loss. The Eagles then demoted Dalton to QB3 before cutting him. And that’s how we got to McKee becoming No. 2 again. It’s hard to predict how much time Hurts is going to miss due to his blood clot. McKee figures to be the starter until Hurts is back, if he even returns this season. Though it would seem like the Eagles could pivot to intriguing rookie Cole Payton at some point if they get knocked out of the playoff picture. Then again, the NFC East is looking so bad that the Eagles might hang around longer than expected. As for what Panthers fans can expect from McKee, I’m really not sure. He looked the worst I’ve ever seen him play during offseason practices and preseaosn games. He’s also going to be operating behind the Eagles’ patch-work offensive line while missing some key skill players. I can’t say I’m very confident that he’s going to play well. But I don’t want to write him off entirely until we see him in some regular season action because he has shown signs of promise in the past. UPDATE! As I was answering this question, the Eagles reportedly signed Dallas Cowboys practice squad quarterback Joe Milton to their roster. Guessing he’s the emergency third quarterback this week behind McKee and Payton? Your running back position looks about as injured as the Panthers’ [insert position here]. With the signing of training camp/practice squad running back Ja’Quinden Jackson, what do you expect the Eagles ground attack to look like on Sunday? Funny enough, they didn’t even sign Jackson (despite reporting that suggested otherwise after hosting him on a visit)! Not as of me typing this sentence, at least. They added Ian Wheeler to the practice squad instead. But, yeah, the Eagles are really thin at running back. It looks like their top three options are going to be out: 1) Saquon Barkley, 2) Tank Bigsby (on injured reserve, and 3) Will Shipley. That leaves the team with Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele, who were both called up from the practice squad last week. They also have Jaydon Blue and the aforementioned Wheeler on the practice squad now. The Eagles managed to gain just 22 yards on 18 carries in Week 5. Give the Jags’ run defense, which has been stingy this season (fewest yards per carry allowed), for being stout. But it’s hard to expect the Eagles to be awesome on the ground when their offensive line is dealing with a lot of key absences and they’re down to RB4 and RB5. I’m expecting the ground game to look a little better against the Panthers because … how much worse could it get than Week 5? That was the fewest rushing yards the Eagles have had in a game since Week 2 of the 2015 season. But there’s no good reason to expect it to fully click until we actually see it happen. Perhaps Panthers fans feel differently since Carolina is allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Speaking of injuries, the Panthers early season has so far been defined by them. Where are the Eagles hurting the most right now, besides running back, and how will that affect their game? The Eagles have 24 players listed on their injury report this week. Not ideal! Here are the key positions to monitor (outside of running back): WIDE RECEIVER — It sounds like DeVonta Smith might be able to play after being upgraded to limited in Thursday’s practice. But with Dontayvion Wicks being downgraded to not practicing, the Eagles might be without another starter as they’re getting their top target back. OFFENSIVE LINE — Lane Johnson retired and the Eagles traded Cam Jurgens, who was struggling anyway. The Eagles opened Landon Dickerson’s practice window to return from IR but they don’t seem to be in a rush to activate him. Drew Kendall, who was brought in from the bench to play center after Dickerson got hurt and they moved Jurgens to left guard, returned to practice on Thursday in a limited capacity. If he’s healthy, he’ll probably start at center. If not, look for Jake Majors — who made his NFL regular debut last week after being called up from the practice squad — to get the nod instead. Starting right guard Tyler Steen is banged up but it seems like he might be play. The Eagles’ projected starting offensive line for Sunday: LT Jordan Mailata (pretty good starter), LG Willie Lampkin (fan-favorite undersized blocker who struggled in pass pro making his first regular season start last week), C Jake Majors (fringe roster player), RG Tyler Steen (cromulent starter now playing at less than 100%), and RT Markel Bell (massive player who is playing like a third-round rookie, which he is). EDGE RUSHER — Starter Jalyx Hunt is out. He leads the Eagles in quarterback hits so far this season. The Eagles’ pass rush has already been lacking, so, missing him isn’t great. The Eagles are hoping Jonathan Greenard, who was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, can return from an ankle injury. Rotational rusher A.J. Epenesa could also miss this week’s game. Arnold Ebiketie is also on the injury report, albeit as a full participant. The only Eagles edge rusher NOT on the injury report this week is Nolan Smith. There are loud rumbles from columnists and fans alike that the Eagles should consider “punting” on the still young 2026 season. What’s been wrong so far and might the Eagles be eyeing the wounded Panthers as a get-right game? I think a win here would be a pretty nice feeling for an Eagles team that’s endured a lot of chaos through the first six weeks of the season. Especially after nearly having the Los Angeles Rams beat in Week 4 and the Jacksonville Jaguars beat in Week 5. But I struggle to give this team the benefit of the doubt. While they’re not far off from being 4-1, they would be…

full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) with the ball in the second half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The fickle nature of these SB Nation Reacts confidence polls are the same for all 32 fan bases. Our favorite team wins, and we’re riding high. It’s all sunshine and rainbows. But our favorite team loses, and the sky is falling. It’s all doom and gloom. A division loss just exacerbates the doom, and when it’s the Green Bay Packers beating the Chicago Bears, the confidence poll drops from 94% of us believing the team is heading in the right direction to just 55%. The NFC North is the only division where all four teams have winning records after five weeks, and this is the third straight year they’ve done that. If the season ended today, all four NFC North teams would qualify for the seven-team playoff bracket. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook have the undefeated Minnesota Vikings with the second-best odds to make the NFC playoffs at -450. The (3-2) Detroit Lions have the fourth-best odds at -178. The (3-2) Bears, who are last in the division, have the fifth-best NFC postseason odds at -146, while the (3-2) Packers are ninth at +142. The Bears are on the road to face the (2-3) Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, while the Packers host the (2-3) Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Minnesota and Detroit are on byes.

title: Chicago Bears vs. Atlanta Falcons – Game Picks and Predictions
summary: Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium (noon CT), the 3-2 Chicago Bears look to bounce back from a lopsided 31-7 loss in Green Bay by traveling south to face the 2-3 Atlanta Falcons. Chicago could get Caleb Williams back under center for the first time since Week 2 after he practiced in full this week (still listed […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 20: Fans take a selfie with the giant stainless steel falcon before the Sunday afternoon NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on November 20, 2022 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium (noon CT), the 3-2 Chicago Bears look to bounce back from a lopsided 31-7 loss in Green Bay by traveling south to face the 2-3 Atlanta Falcons. Chicago could get Caleb Williams back under center for the first time since Week 2 after he practiced in full this week (still listed as questionable), while the ground game will lean on D’Andre Swift with Kyle Monangai out again (thumb/toe). The Bears will also be without T.J. Edwards, Dayo Odeyingbo (IR), and Montez Sweat (suspended), but are getting Shemar Turner back for the first time since he was lost to an ACL injury last season. Kyler Gordon was also activated today. Atlanta counters with a potent offense featuring Bijan Robinson and Drake London, and Michael Penix Jr. appears ready to go after missing early action, although he is dealing with a rib injury. Both sides bring explosive pieces, so the game figures to turn on who protects the ball, who scores the touchdowns, and whether anyone goes off—whether it’s Williams or Penix throwing for big yardage (and how many interceptions each throws), Swift or Robinson finding the end zone, or a receiver like Rome Odunze or Drake London dominating. Below is our roundtable with the score predictions and the individual highlights we think will decide it. Josh : 30-27 Chicago, with a missed PAT by the Falcons and a missed field goal by the Beloved, just because that seems to be how the NFL is going. Dexter gets the lone sack because of course he does, but Swift and Loveland do enough as Ben lets Caleb take the reins and he stops trying to make Roush happen. Of course, Bijan still gets two TDs and Penix throws for 2. Jeff Berckes : 41-34 Bears. I think this one is super high scoring with skill player talent providing a lot of fireworks. Caleb’s return lifts the offense with a 300+ yard passing day and everyone of your fantasy options makes you happy…including those holding shares of Drake London and Bijan Robinson. Sam : I am worried about the defensive home/road splits and the Falcons’ ability to put up points. I am also expecting a shootout, though. I’ll take Bears 35, Falcons 31. GOOCH : What a difference a week makes. The Bears got their heads handed to them by the Pack last week after two dominant performances against the Eagles and the Jets. What team will show up on Sunday? I think the offense bounces back, but the defense is going to have their hands full with Bijan Robinson. I think Robinson puts up two touchdowns and rushes for 150 yards. Penix adds a passing touchdown to Drake London – JJ again struggles to cover a #1 wide receiver. However, Booker books another sack and Penix turns the ball over twice (one interception, one fumble). Swift comes close to matching Robinson in yards – rushing for over 100 yards in the game. But it is Caleb and Loveland that put the Bears over the top – Caleb throws for 275 yards and three touchdowns, with two going to Loveland as he breaks out. Bears over the Falcons, 40 – 28. Superfans: Caleb Williams might be a little rusty in his first game back, so he’ll throw for only 312 yards, and the Bears offense may not hit their Week 1 point total as they recalibrate with Caleb back. So let’s call it… Da Bears 47 and the A-T-L 19. What are your picks and predictions for the game? View Link

full_text: Oct 6, 2024; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) celebrates after the game against the Carolina Panthers at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Daniel Bartel-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Chicago Bears announced several roster moves today, including activating defensive back Kyler Gordon from the Physically Unable to Perform list. Gordon has not played this season while rehabbing a calf injury he suffered in the offseason. He was in the midst of his 21-day practice window and was a full participant for all 9 practices over the last three weeks. He’ll likely be eased back into the lineup, as this regime has brought players back that way in the past. At yesterday’s press conference, head coach Ben Johnson said this about Gordon, “He’s done a great job taking everything that we’ve assigned him so far. I feel good about him — whether that’s this week or next week — being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there’s a number of ways he can do that. But I’m encouraged with what I’ve seen so far.” On Thursday, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen met the media and said this about Gordon, “He’s been working extremely hard. He’s been great around the building. He’s been doing everything we’ve asked him to do. I’ve been impressed with him.” It’ll be interesting to see how the Bears deploy Gordon on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, because while most of his NFL experience has been at nickel, he’s also played and practiced at corner and safety. His versatility, if he can stay healthy, will provide the Bears’ defense a huge boost as the season progresses. The Bears also signed defensive back Nick McCloud to the 53-man roster from their practice squad, placed defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) on injured reserve, and released safety Xavier Woods. Odeyingbo is second on the team with 3 sacks, third with 3 tackles for loss, and he leads Chicago defensive linemen with 2 batted passes. He’ll miss at least 4 games on IR. Chicago also announced that they’re elevating linebacker Buddy Johnson and running back Zavier Scott from the practice squad for Sunday’s game. They’ll revert to the practice squad after the game.

title: Bears-Falcons Franchise Connections
summary: Going into their Week 6 matchup on Sunday, the Chicago Bears and Atlanta Falcons have faced off against each other 30 times. It’s been a pretty even history between the two franchises, as the Bears have the slight 16-14 series lead since the first time they squared off against each other in 1966. Each week […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - JANUARY 10: Gervon Dexter Sr. #99 of the Chicago Bears runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFC Wild Card Playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Going into their Week 6 matchup on Sunday, the Chicago Bears and Atlanta Falcons have faced off against each other 30 times. It’s been a pretty even history between the two franchises, as the Bears have the slight 16-14 series lead since the first time they squared off against each other in 1966. Each week going forward, we’re going to highlight some of the connections that the Bears’ coaching staff and roster each have with their opponent, as well as their opponent’s ties to Chicago. This week, we’re looking at the overlap between the Bears and the Falcons. The Bears currently have three players on their roster who have suited up for the Falcons before. The recent most recent addition of the bunch is cornerback Clark Phillips III, who came over to Chicago in the Gervon Dexter Sr. trade (more on him later). Phillips got drafted by the Falcons in the fourth round in 2023, and he played in 28 games for the team over three seasons, starting in seven games and tallying 63 tackles, an interception, and ten pass deflections. He has suited up for three of the Bears’ five games this year but has not recorded a statistic. Defensive tackle Kentavius Street also spent three seasons with the Falcons before joining the Bears in free agency this offseason. In his 25 games with Atlanta, he combined for 50 tackles, 4.0 sacks, and 11.0 tackles for loss. So far this year in Chicago, he has seven tackles and a sack in five games. Additionally, Bears practice squad wide receiver Scotty Miller had 11 catches for 161 yards and two touchdowns with the Falcons in his lone season there in 2023. There’s a considerable presence of former Bears on the Falcons’ roster, as Atlanta has five players in its organization who have suited up for Chicago. Part of that likely comes down to the influence of former Bears general manager Ryan Pace, who was a key executive for the Falcons from 2022 to 2025. However, the most notable name with Bears ties on the Falcons’ roster is Gervon Dexter, whom Chicago drafted in the second round in 2023 and traded to Atlanta just before the season. Going into Week 6, he ranks No. 24 among 118 qualified defensive tackles with a 79.2 PFN DT Impact grade. For reference, nobody on the Bears ranks higher than No. 83 this year. Olamide Zaccheaus returned to the Falcons this offseason, having spent 2019 through 2022 in the organization. He bounced around a little bit after that stint, including a one-year stint with the Bears last year. In 2025, Zaccheaus caught 39 passes for 313 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran wide receiver played a big role in Chicago’s offense in the early stages of Ben Johnson’s system installation. Two other players on the Falcons’ active roster played for the Bears: linebacker Josh Woods and defensive tackle LaCale London. Woods signed with the Bears in 2018 as an undrafted free agent, and he spent four seasons in the organization. He didn’t play in any games as a rookie, but he’d go on to play 25 games over his next three seasons with the team, primarily as a backup linebacker and special teamer. London was an undrafted free agent signing by the Bears in 2020, and though he would stay with the team until August of 2022, he only ever played one regular season game with the team. After a stint in what was then the XFL, London signed with the Falcons in 2023 and has since turned into a solid rotational piece along their defensive line. The Falcons also have former Bears running back Khalil Herbert on their practice squad. As fans may recall, Herbert was a sixth-round pick by the Bears in 2021 and played in 48 games with them, finishing with a grand total of 372 carries for 1,791 rushing yards (4.8 yards per carry) with nine rushing touchdowns and two receiving touchdowns. Off the field, the major connection between the two teams is Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham, who was previously the assistant general manager under Ryan Poles for Chicago. I don’t have to remind fans about the whole compensatory pick debacle. Cunningham was Poles’ right-hand man from 2022 to 2025. Atlanta also has two coaches who played for the Bears: assistant defensive backs coach Ricky Manning, and outside linebackers coach John Timu. The Bears’ coaching staff has two notable ties to the Falcons’ organization. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen got his first NFL job with the Falcons, serving as a defensive quality control coordinator from 2002-03 and a defensive assistant from 2004-05. Bears linebackers coach Richard Smith was also the Falcons’ defensive coordinator from 2015-16, most notably serving in that role during Atlanta’s run to the Super Bowl in 2016.

title: Chicago Bears Week 6 Flashbacks: A meltdown, a milestone, and a breakout
summary: 1. 2006, Bears @ Cardinals: They Are Who We Thought They Were! October 16, 2006 | Bears win 24-23 There are weird wins, and then there is what happened in Arizona on Monday Night Football in 2006. The Bears entered Week 6 undefeated at 5-0 and looking like one of the best teams in football. […]
full_text: A Jay Cutler pass to Matt Forte with 18 seconds left in the game put the Chicago Bears ahead 18-17 on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2015, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo. (Keith Myers/Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) 1. 2006, Bears @ Cardinals: They Are Who We Thought They Were! October 16, 2006 | Bears win 24-23 There are weird wins, and then there is what happened in Arizona on Monday Night Football in 2006. The Bears entered Week 6 undefeated at 5-0 and looking like one of the best teams in football. By halftime, none of that seemed to matter. Arizona had built a 20-0 lead while Rex Grossman and the Chicago offense completely unraveled. Grossman eventually finished just 14-of-37 for 144 yards, four interceptions and two lost fumbles. The Bears offense never scored a touchdown. Somehow, Chicago still won. The comeback began when Mark Anderson stripped Matt Leinart and Mike Brown recovered the fumble for a touchdown. Later, Brian Urlacher ripped the football away from Edgerrin James, allowing Charles Tillman to scoop it up and race 40 yards for another defensive score. That still left the Bears trailing 23-17 with under three minutes remaining. Enter Devin Hester. Hester fielded a punt at his own 17-yard line, found daylight and took it 83 yards for the go-ahead touchdown, completing one of the most ridiculous comebacks in franchise history. Arizona still had a chance to win, but Neil Rackers missed a 40-yard field goal in the closing seconds, allowing Chicago to escape with a 24-23 victory. The numbers make the result even harder to believe. The Bears committed six turnovers, gained only 168 yards and did not score an offensive touchdown. Urlacher finished with 19 tackles and forced the fumble that completely changed the game. Of course, the night became even more memorable after Cardinals coach Dennis Green stepped to the podium and delivered one of the most famous postgame rants in NFL history. “They are who we thought they were!” He wasn’t wrong. The Bears were 6-0. 2. 2014, Bears @ Falcons: Cutler leads Chicago to its 750th victory October 12, 2014 | Bears win 27-13 The Bears entered Week 6 desperately needing to get things moving in the right direction. Back-to-back losses had dropped Chicago to 2-3, and a road trip to Atlanta presented another difficult challenge against Matt Ryan and a dangerous Falcons offense. Instead, Jay Cutler put together one of his best performances in a Bears uniform. Cutler completed 26-of-38 passes for 381 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, setting what would stand as his highest single-game passing total during his time in Chicago. He had plenty of help from his receivers. Alshon Jeffery caught five passes for 136 yards, while Brandon Marshall added six receptions for 113. Matt Forte once again did a little bit of everything, finishing with 80 rushing yards, 77 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Chicago led 13-3 at halftime, but Atlanta erased that advantage with 10 unanswered points in the third quarter. With the game tied at 13, Cutler delivered the play that swung momentum back toward the Bears. Facing third-and-long, he launched a deep ball down the sideline to Jeffery, who hauled it in for a 74-yard gain. Forte scored a touchdown shortly afterward, and Chicago never trailed again. The Bears defense shut Atlanta out in the fourth quarter, while Forte added another touchdown to finish off a 27-13 victory. Cutler’s performance and the win itself were already noteworthy, but the afternoon also carried some franchise history. The victory was the 750th regular-season win in Chicago Bears history, making them the first NFL franchise to reach that mark. A big road win, Cutler throwing for nearly 400 yards, and another number added to one of the league’s oldest franchises. Not a bad afternoon in Atlanta. 3. 2024, Bears vs. Jaguars: Caleb Williams shines in London October 13, 2024 | Bears win 35-16 The Bears traveled across the Atlantic in Week 6 of Caleb Williams’ rookie season with some momentum beginning to build. By the time they left London, that momentum had turned into one of Williams’ first real statement performances as an NFL quarterback. Jacksonville actually struck first and held a 3-0 lead after the opening quarter, but Chicago quickly took control. Williams found Cole Kmet for a 31-yard touchdown early in the second quarter before connecting with him again from two yards out just before halftime. The Bears went into the locker room leading 14-3 and never really looked back. Williams continued spreading the football around after halftime, this time finding Keenan Allen for a pair of touchdowns as Chicago’s lead continued to grow. He finished the afternoon 23-of-29 for 226 yards, four touchdowns and one interception, while also causing problems with his legs by rushing for another 56 yards. It was the first four-touchdown passing game of Williams’ young career. Kmet caught five passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns, Allen added two scores of his own, and D’Andre Swift rushed for 91 yards and another touchdown as Chicago rolled to a 35-16 victory. Kmet’s afternoon deserves a little extra appreciation as well. When long snapper Scott Daly suffered a knee injury, Kmet suddenly found himself pulling double duty. Not only did he lead the Bears in receiving and catch two touchdowns, he also stepped in as Chicago’s emergency long snapper. Because apparently catching touchdowns in London wasn’t enough. The win moved Chicago to 4-2 and gave the Bears their third straight victory, while Williams walked away with the first four-touchdown game of hit young career. For Bears fans watching from back home, waking up early turned out to be worth it. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts after a touchdown is scored during the first quarter against the Carolina Panthers of the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images I know some Chicago Bears fans are down after that loss to the Green Bay Packers, but was Week 1 really that long ago? Are we letting the game in the pouring rain and three straight starts by backup quarterbacks cloud our outlook for the Bears? After an offseason of real hope, hype, and anticipation, Caleb Williams and the Chicago offense dropped 59 points in a road game to kick off the year. Sure, the defense was exposed a bit, but the Bears were the talk of the NFL. After that Week 1 performance, the offseason buzz around Williams as a dark-horse Most Valuable Player candidate ramped up even more, as a bunch of money poured in on him to win MVP, thus lowering the odds. Then a tough battle against an aggressive Minnesota Vikings defense came in a downpour, and Williams was carted off. Most thought the season was doomed, but the injury wasn’t season-ending, and the Bears regrouped to go 2-1 in Caleb’s absence. Week 6 for the Bears is a road game against the Atlanta Falcons, and our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the Bears at -1.5, with the over/under at 51.5. A road favorite with some uncertainty at quarterback is exactly what the Bears were one week ago, and we all remember how that one turned out. But this time, the talk is positive about Caleb starting for the first time since Week 2. He practiced on Thursday, said he could do everything, had another practice today, and was full again, presumably with no setbacks. Assuming he plays*, I like the Bears to win and cover the 1.5 points. I also like the over on the total because Atlanta’s offense will get theirs. I also like the over on Williams’ passing yards, set at 225.5 by FanDuel. There’s still plenty of season left, so if you think Caleb can get his MVP case back on track, those odds are at +10,000. Not gonna lie, a few bucks on that at those odds could be a fun one to monitor. *If the Williams doesn’t play, I still like the Bears to win and cover, but I’d stay away from the total. full_text: With the Bengals on a bye week this week, and Ohio State traveling to face the defending National Champion Indiana Hoosiers, it feels like a good time to sneak a little draft talk into the mix. There are a ton of talented skill position players in this game, including Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith. However, the Bengals are not going to be in the market for a first round wide receiver. Even if they were, they are not going to be in a position to take Smith. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh are ultra-talented receiver prospects for the Hoosiers, but enough about the skill players. Austin Siereveld Siereveld has played all over the line for the Buckeyes the last few seasons. He has experience playing everywhere but center for Ohio State. Ultimately, his best position may be at guard at the next level. The Bengals Dalton Risner is playing good football, but is scheduled to be a free agent after the season. The Bengals drafted Brian Parker II in the sixth round, and he will have an opportunity to be a future starter somewhere on the Bengals line. When you want to compete for Super Bowls, you will need depth on the offensive line regardless. A player like Siereveld with his versatility should be of interest to every team in the league. Austin Siereveld (#67) Ohio State ✅ Positional versatility ✅ Leg drive as a run blocker ✅ Plays with good technique ✅ 83.3 run blocking grade in 2025 ✅ Allowed 15 pressures and 0 sacks during the 2025 season pic.twitter.com/WKtFnM7ZPk — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) June 4, 2026 Amare Ferrell Jordan Battle is coming off a really solid performance against Miami. However, that doesn’t take away from some of his early-season struggles in the secondary this season. Battle still misses too many tackles and is scheduled to be a free agent after the season. The Bengals could decide to bring in another day two safety to fill his spot. Amare Ferrell is an experienced safety prospect for the Hoosiers, having already eclipsed 2,000 snaps during his career. He has good enough size for the position at 6’2” and 205 pounds. He possesses impressive ball skills with 8 interceptions over the previous two seasons. Ferrell is a player to keep an eye on at safety. The Buckeyes have a couple of players at the position that could be mid-round draft selections also. Those guys are Earl Little Jr. and Jaylen McClain. Amare Ferrell will be entering his 3rd season as a starter. He has 8 interceptions over the last two seasons. He has a high football IQ, good size at 6’2” and 210 pounds, and an 82.8 coverage grade in 2025. pic.twitter.com/8D1qL7oS85 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) May 3, 2026 Jermaine Mathews Mathews is another experienced defensive back. He has played over 1,600 career snaps earlier at corner. He has the flexibility to play in the slot or on the outside. He currently has a 76.0 coverage grade during the 2026 season. He played pretty well going up against the Texas Longhorns’ talented receivers during week two. This week will be another big test for Mathews against Becker and Marsh. Mathews doesn’t have the greatest size at around 5’11” and 195 pounds, but he is a physical player. Mathews is a more than willing tackler, instinctive in zone coverage, and should test fairly well at the combine this year. The Bengals will have a decision to make at corner with both DJ Turner and Dax Hill scheduled to hit free agency after the season. Even if they bring both of those guys back, you can never have too much depth at the corner position. I would expect an early-round investment at the position come April. Chris: “Baltimore made a big change at head coach this year — has there been a clear visible change in the way the Ravens play under Jesse Minter, or does it still seem like Ravens football?” Nikhil : “I would call Jesse Minter’s Ravens an evolution of the team’s longtime ethos. I think the Ravens’ new identity has more to do with their newfound ability to actually win in the fourth quarter. Their Week 3 and 6 victories in Brazil and Atlanta proved that Minter and his staff can make the right game management decisions; that the roster can weather adversity, penalties, and injuries; and that maybe, just maybe, this team is not completely broken if Lamar Jackson is injured.” Chris: “What do you view as the Ravens’ biggest strength and weakness on defense right now?” Nikhil : “I cannot identify any one particular strength of the Ravens defense right now aside from its pure talent. Kyle Hamilton looks like a DPOY candidate every week, even if his position and statistics may not get him there, Nnamdi Madubuike has come back strong from last year’s neck injury, and Trey Hendrickson was constantly generating pressure before missing time due to finger surgery. He’s back this week for just his second game sharing the D-line with Madubuike. Younger players like Mike Green, Trenton Simpson, and Tavius Robinson are also putting together breakout campaigns. In terms of weaknesses, though, the unit does not feel cohesive yet. Nowhere is this more evident than third down, when the Ravens’ coverage scheme and pressure packages lack synergy and precision, allowing opponents to convert far too many third-and-longs. Rushers and coverage defenders are a split-second too late before and after the pass, though tackling was much-improved in Atlanta.” Chris: “Which of the Ravens’ 2026 draft picks has the best chance of making an immediate impact in Week 6?” Nikhil : “Vega Ioane is the easy answer here. He’s starting his third straight game at center, a position played for just a handful of snaps in college, and has graded out as the Ravens’ best blocker while doing it. His snaps have been inconsistent, which is among the reasons Baltimore traded for Cam Jurgens last week, but the Browns’ DT injuries could set him up to make a big impact up front.” Chris: “Tell us about one player who Browns fans may not have heard of, but who could have an impact on this Sunday’s game.” Nikhil : “The Browns’ blocking scheme will rightly prioritize Hendrickson and Madubuike on Sunday, which should continue to create opportunities for fourth-year edge rusher Tavius Robinson. The 2023 fourth-round pick has been a force against the run since he entered the NFL, but htis year, he is quietly leading the Ravens with three sacks. The motor and finishing ability that showed up in run defense have finally translated to the pass rush, and Robinson is consistently taking advantage of his 1-on-1 opportunities. Browns right tackle Tytus Howard has struggled to start the year; now, he’ll face a hungry, confident Robinson looking to keep boosting his value in a contract year.” Chris: “The Browns are underdogs against the Ravens on Sunday (Browns +3 as of this question, per FanDuel). Who would you pick to win the game?” Nikhil : “I’ll admit, I was not confident in the Ravens last week. For much of the Falcons game, I felt vindicated – Baltimore was losing at the margins and badly missing the reliable downfield passing of Lamar Jackson. But Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley is the definition of a gamer, and like his two 2025 wins, he played his best football when it was needed. Both teams are dealing with injuries, but Baltimore seems better-equipped to overcome theirs and grind out their first AFC North win of the year.” Thanks again to Nikhil for taking the time to answer my questions.

title: NFL predictions: Which running game excels in Browns-Ravens matchup to take over the AFC North?
summary: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (3-2) take on the Baltimore Ravens (4-1). I’ve harped on this a bunch of times already, but last week’s game was […]
full_text: This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns (3-2) take on the Baltimore Ravens (4-1). Below, we analyze a few advantages, disadvantages, or general thoughts about the two teams before getting to our predictions for the game. Can the Browns’ Run Defense Come Through? I’ve harped on this a bunch of times already, but last week’s game was mostly a non-factor for what I think of the Browns, except for one thing (I’ll get to that in a bit) due to the weather conditions. The weather is set to be great in Cleveland for Sunday’s big divisional game against the Ravens. If you jump forward to the predictions this week, though, I’m picking the Ravens, even with knowing Tyler Huntley is starting for them. I certainly think the Browns can win, and am only putting the edge slightly in Baltimore’s favor, but the big reason centers around Cleveland’s run defense and the status of Mason Graham and Mike Hall. The Ravens rank 3rd in the NFL in rushing yards per game (164.4) and are also 3rd in yards per carry (5.07). Side note: It seems pretty stunning that with how poor the Browns’ rushing attack has been, they are ranked 21st in rushing yards per game . The Browns’ run defense is 18th in rushing yards allowed per game (117.4) and 23rd in rushing yards per play allowed (4.48). They allowed their first rushing touchdown of the season last week against a Jets rushing attack that had previously been anemic. For a team that has relied on close, last-second victories, I see that successful rushing attack for the Ravens being the defining factor this week in them taking over the game late. High Stakes for Cleveland The stakes couldn’t be higher for Cleveland this week. If they win, they go back into first place in the AFC North, and would have victories over two division rivals already. If they lose, they are suddenly two games back of first place, and without the tiebreaker, which really makes it like three games back. Here are some of the positives I can think of this week, along with some general notes: I liked what Isaiah Bond did in training camp, and it’s unfortunate that his time to shine came in rainy conditions, which likely contributed to a couple big dropped passes. With that said, KC Concepcion was meant for those targets, and he’s expected back in the lineup this week as he returns from a concussion. Zay Flowers is obviously a lot more proven than the rookie, but we’ll get to see each player on both sides (and a lot like to compare Todd Monken’s utilization of the two). If the defense can find a way to be better against the run, then certainly they pose a problem for Tyler Huntley (or anyone for that matter). Last week against Geno Smith , after that first drive, he practically could not get anything going. That is an important point to make, though: on that first drive, the team should lock up with Zay Flowers right away, because if the Browns don’t adjust in-between weeks, then those crossing routes will burn them early again. The eye test continues to tell me that Quinshon Judkins hasn’t been right this season. There was a time last season when he looked just as impressive as the rest of the team’s young rookie class, and even though he averaged 3.6 yards per carry, the eye test always said, ‘Man if our offensive line wasn’t so bad, I wonder what Judkins could do,’ because you saw the ability there. Now, everything is so pedestrian looking with his running style, that he looks like just another guy. Don’t get me wrong, there is plenty wrong with the blocking as well, but Judkins’ stock has fallen to the bottom of the pool in comparing the team’s promising young players. The offensive line took a step back in pass protection last week, but that’s one of those things I don’t get overly concerned with unless it happens in normal weather conditions. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 3 point underdogs against the Jets. The over/under is 39.5. Quick Hitters Offensive coordinator Travis Switzer was asked about the offensive line breakdown last week that led to a bunch of sacks, and how communication comes into play: “Yeah, it’s about taking every rep, whether it’s a walkthrough rep, a practice rep, it might be a meeting rep, where we’re just talking through things, and it’s making sure everybody’s on the same page and they’re hearing guys communicate, because they’re the ones out there that have to do it. Certainly, we kind of give them the guidelines, if you will, but communication is the priority there. I mean, even if they maybe didn’t do it exactly the way that we talked about it, if we’re all on the same page, we have a chance. So, I think it’s just taking advantage of every single possible rep you could get, whether it’s a walk, a practice, a meeting rep, and making sure everybody’s on the same page there.” Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg talked about making adjustments to the defense pretty quick last week after the Jets’ opening-drive score: “A game is like a week in practice. It’s like the Wednesday to the Thursday to the Friday. They say the first drive to the second drive, and you’re constantly trying to find your different edges. Eliminate Browns hurting Browns, eliminate things that could hurt us, build on things that could help us, figure out what they’re doing. ‘Oh, this can work, let’s go here.’ It’s a constant adjustment process, or it’s a constant, ‘hey, let’s settle back. Let’s let our players get their cleats in the ground, their eyes right, and play fast as hell.’ And every game, no matter the first drive, the third drive, the tenth drive, it’s a constant process of all of us together on the sideline just trying to figure out what’s best for the next drive and then don’t even think about anything after that. And shoot, whatever happens in that drive, what’s best for the next drive. And sometimes it is adjustments, sometimes it is just take a step back, let’s let our play style take over. So, it’s a credit to those guys, the way they responded. And also, part of that is just the heart, the resilience after a tough first drive to bounce back, is credit to our players.” Special teams coordinator Bryon Storer said both the long snapper and punter made mistakes on the game-costing punt last week: “Well, it started with the snap. We had a high snap. I talked to Rex (Sunahara), me and Rex watched the tape, and he brought his hips up, which brought the ball up, and then it slipped right through Corey’s hands. And so that was an unfortunate series of events on the one play. Usually those two guys, this was the eighth punt of the game, so they had done a pretty darn good job up to that point in the game. And for whatever reason, they both made a mistake on the same play. And usually when guys that handle the ball every single play that they’re out there, if both of those guys make a mistake, there’s going to be something bad that’s going to happen. That’s part of the job.” Here are predictions from multiple staff members at DBN: Predictions Chris Pokorny: “As I said earlier, I had to lean toward the Ravens this week. If the Jets were able to run all over the Browns last week with the defensive tackle issues, then Baltimore will do the same to them. Let’s hope that besides that, the Browns play a relatively clean game, minimizing turnovers, and getting a few clutch plays to give them a shot at the end of the game. Unfortunately, I think the Ravens will utilize that won’t be able to deter the mighty Ravens’ run game too much.” Ravens 23, Browns 17 Jared Mueller : “The injury issues with both teams tell me this will be a battle between RB Derrick Henry and QB Deshaun Watson. Can the Browns defense hold up without a few defensive linemen and, likely, LB Carson Schwesinger? Can Cleveland’s offense get things going without RBs Quinshon Judkins (likely) and Raheim Sanders (for sure)? Watson could get WR KC Concepcion back, which could give HC Todd Monken some options to use the short pass game as an extension of the run game. In the end, especially with WR…

title: Shedeur Sanders trade: What Browns GM Andrew Berry is rumored to think about the QB
summary: While it may not be the be-all-and-end-all in the NFL anymore, the quarterback position always gets an outsized amount of attention. The search for a long-term franchise quarterback continues for the Cleveland Browns. Few, if any, believe that QB Deshaun Watson will ever fulfill the value that the Browns paid to acquire him in a […]
full_text: While it may not be the be-all-and-end-all in the NFL anymore, the quarterback position always gets an outsized amount of attention. The search for a long-term franchise quarterback continues for the Cleveland Browns. Few, if any, believe that QB Deshaun Watson will ever fulfill the value that the Browns paid to acquire him in a trade, much less his huge contract. Second-year QB Shedeur Sanders seems more likely to replace Watson as the starter in 2026 than the potentially short-lived idea of Watson signing a contract extension . Sanders’ future all of a sudden became part of rumors after the young QB hired an agent for the first time in the NFL. After a poor rookie season and losing out to Watson in this year’s quarterback competition, it is possible that Sanders is looking for a fresh start away from Cleveland. It is equally possible that Sanders is just getting ahead of things to be prepared no matter what happens in the future, whether that is at the NFL trade deadline or beyond that. According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic , Browns GM Andrew Berry is fond of the young quarterback, making it less likely that he would trade him away: If Sanders is seeking a trade, that might be difficult. Berry is said to have a great affection for Sanders, whom he took a chance on 18 months ago while the rest of the NFL passed over him several times. Sanders was one of the worst starting quarterbacks last season, by several metrics, among qualified passers, but he showed growth in the preseason and training camp. Jones went even further, calling it a “stunner” if it were to happen: There is belief in Sanders and his ability. He’s also on a fifth-round rookie contract for another two-plus years. Berry’s current starting quarterback is not under contract beyond this season and has a history of injuries. Blanket caveat that anything can happen over the next few weeks, but the Browns dealing Sanders by the deadline would be a stunner. What do you think about Berry’s rumored affection for Sanders? title: Browns among many teams uncertain at the QB position; “franchise QBs” rare long-term
summary: Few, if any, Cleveland Browns fans believe the team has its long-term franchise quarterback on the current roster. Most hope that Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel, or Taylen Green become that guy, and quickly. Given veteran QB Deshaun Watson’s history, age, and injuries, a future in Cleveland seems unlikely, even with extension rumors starting before the […]
full_text: Few, if any, Cleveland Browns fans believe the team has its long-term franchise quarterback on the current roster. Most hope that Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel , or Taylen Green become that guy, and quickly. Given veteran QB Deshaun Watson’s history, age, and injuries, a future in Cleveland seems unlikely, even with extension rumors starting before the team’s Week 5 loss . The NFL continues to undergo an interesting process, with no end in sight, as usual, when it comes to winning Super Bowls. At one point, it was assumed (because of Patrick Mahomes, Tom Brady, Matthew Stafford, Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Lamar Jackson, etc.) that a team had to have a top-level quarterback to be in championship discussions. Then, Jalen Hurts and Sam Darnold , both good to very good but not considered at the same level as those players listed above, won the last two Super Bowls with great supporting rosters around them. As the league pivoted to smaller, faster defenders, the importance of the running back increased, including Super Bowl MVP and Kansas City Chiefs’ huge free-agent addition Kenneth Walker. The quarterback position has also struggled to keep up with Brady, Drew Brees , and others retiring, while Stafford and Aaron Rodgers are on the doorstep of moving out of the league. This week alone led to even more “franchise quarterback” discussions, with Los Angeles Chargers Justin Herbert and Denver Broncos Bo Nix struggling and a potentially very serious health issue for Hurts. Jackson will miss Week 6 versus the Browns , has a contract that needs to be addressed before next season ($84 million cap number), and has a history of injuries and playoff flameouts. In fact, if we use the following criteria, there are few teams that feel confident that they have a franchise quarterback for the long term: 35 years old or younger Limited injury history Proven top-level track record during the regular season of carrying the team to multiple wins Playoff success and/or reasonable expectations of such Under contract for multiple seasons that are likely to be picked up or extended Certain Franchise QBs Patrick Mahomes Josh Allen Caleb Williams Brock Purdy Drake Maye Jordan Love Dak Prescott Arguments could be made for a few other names to make the list and against a few on this list, that is what our comment section is for. QBs that barely missed the list and why Joe Burrow – Injuries Baker Mayfield – Injuries, needs more playoff success Trevor Lawrence – Lacks playoff performances Matt Stafford – Age Jared Goff – Rarely carries the Lions Justin Herbert – Overall and playoff success lacking Lamar Jackson – Injuries, contract, playoff success lacking Jalen Hurts – Newly added due to blood clot, contract coming up, and questions about carrying the Eagles Aaron Rodgers – Age, recent seasons’ performances Jayden Daniels – Injuries CJ Stroud – Contract, playoff performance lacking, questions about him carrying the Texans Then there are the younger quarterbacks, like Nix, Cam Ward , Fernando Mendoza , and others who could join one of the above lists. The point is, there are fewer than 10 franchise quarterbacks that can be counted on for now and the future for their current teams. Cleveland is hoping to find one, but as quickly as Herbert, Nix, Burrow, Mayfield, Lawrence, Jackson, etc. look like THE guy, we’ve seen quarterbacks fall off. Browns GM Andrew Berry has done a very good job of building the roster, including adding two wide receivers and two offensive linemen who are already holding their own as rookies. While adding a top-level quarterback, at least one who will join one of the two lists above, is vital, it is rarer than ever. We know lists lead to arguments, so who is on the wrong list? Who deserves to be on a list that they are not on? What do you think when you see all the different quarterback names noted above? Join the conversation! title: Cowboys need to approach the next two games as must wins
summary: There are currently some very frustrating vibes surrounding the Dallas Cowboys. Through the first fives games, they’ve alternated wins and losses, which is the epitome of an average football team. When they lost to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, it wasn’t that they didn’t win, it was how poorly they looked while doing it. Their […]
full_text: Amanda McCoy/Fort Worth Star-Telegram/Tribune News Service via Getty Images There are currently some very frustrating vibes surrounding the Dallas Cowboys. Through the first fives games, they’ve alternated wins and losses, which is the epitome of an average football team. When they lost to the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, it wasn’t that they didn’t win, it was how poorly they looked while doing it. Their defense made undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels look like a seasoned pro, and their offense, which is usually what they can fall back on, scored just 16 points. It’s been a display of inconsistency by the Cowboys so far this season. One thing that’s in their favor in terms of having a shot at the playoffs is that the NFC East, or NFC Least as its been nicknamed, is still more than winnable. The New York Giants lead the division at 3-1-1. Behind them are the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cowboys at 2-3, and the Washington Commanders are 1-3-1. Dallas has the Green Bay Packers on their slate for Sunday Night Football in Week 6 followed by the Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 7. These games are very important of course, but the Cowboys need to approach these as must wins. As much as the Cowboys could win the next two games, their up and down play could easily lead to back-to-back losses as well. They would fall to 2-5 if that was the case, and put them in a very bad spot not even half way through the season. It would not only result in them being 1-2 in division play, but that would give them four losses in the NFC, which would be crippling when it comes to tie breakers for a potential playoff spot. Since the playoff extension in 1990, 155 teams have started the season with a 2-5 record. Only nine of those teams have made the postseason, which is 5.81%. It’s just a very deep hole to dig out of and the Cowboys still have teams like the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Los Angeles Rams, and Jacksonville Jaguars on their schedule. Those teams have the flaws as well, but they’ll also be extremely difficult to beat. The Cowboys need to adopt a back against the wall mentality going forward and stack up some wins quickly. After the Packers and the Eagles, they will face the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals and the 2-3 Indianapolis Colts. So, if they can pull out victories over the next few weeks, they have a shot to go on a nice run and climb up the standings in the NFC significantly. Do you think the Cowboys can knock off the Packers and the Eagles in the next two games? Let us know your thoughts and prediction in the comments.

title: Cowboys vs Packers: Writer predictions for Week 6
summary: Dallas heads to Lambeau Field looking for a response after the disappointing 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay. Green Bay comes in at 3-2 after dominating Chicago 31-7, making this another difficult Sunday night road test. The Cowboys need their offense to rediscover its rhythm, but the biggest question remains whether the defense can finally slow […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images Dallas heads to Lambeau Field looking for a response after the disappointing 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay. Green Bay comes in at 3-2 after dominating Chicago 31-7, making this another difficult Sunday night road test. The Cowboys need their offense to rediscover its rhythm, but the biggest question remains whether the defense can finally slow down an explosive passing attack. When Green Bay has the ball Expect Green Bay to attack Dallas through the air. Jordan Love is coming off a 367-yard performance against Chicago and has thrown 10 touchdowns through five games. Christian Watson has become his biggest big-play threat, averaging more than 18 yards per catch with six touchdowns, while Matthew Golden gives Love another receiver capable of stretching the field. That is a worrying matchup for a Cowboys defense that has already allowed 37 explosive plays and still has zero interceptions this season. Green Bay’s running game is less threatening without Josh Jacobs, who remains out, so this should be a game where Dallas can concentrate more resources on Love. The opportunity is there for the pass rush as well. Love has already been sacked 10 times, but Dallas has produced only five sacks all season. Rashan Gary and Kenny Clark returning to Lambeau against their former team adds another storyline, but Dallas simply needs more pressure regardless of who creates it. For Green Bay, the route to victory is straightforward where they need to protect Love long enough to attack Dallas’ vulnerable secondary and keep creating explosive plays. When Dallas has the ball Dallas needs to get back to the offense they had before the Tampa Bay game. Dak Prescott has thrown for 1,381 yards with nine touchdowns through five games, and having CeeDee Lamb as a full participant after his thigh injury is significant. Lamb and George Pickens have combined for 857 receiving yards, and Green Bay could be vulnerable at cornerback because of injuries Protection is still where the game could turn. Green Bay has 14 sacks, seventh-most in the NFL, and leads the league with seven interceptions. Tampa Bay showed what happens when Dallas becomes uncomfortable, Prescott threw two interceptions and the Cowboys turned the ball over three times. Brian Schottenheimer needs balance on offense. Green Bay is allowing 128 rushing yards per game, while Dallas ranks near the bottom of the league in rushing offense. That makes this a good opportunity to get Javonte Williams involved early rather than leaving Prescott in obvious passing situations all night. Now onto the predictions from your BTB writers… Tom Ryle (2-3) I have no idea what to expect from the Cowboys. I hope they come out fired up and Mike Pettine has some kind of answers to offer. But I just don’t have a good feeling. So I hope this is a reverse jinx. Packers 31 Cowboys 27 Brandon Loree (3-2) What worries me most of all in this game is the passing attack headline by Christian Parker and Matthew Golden. Last year’s first-round pick for the Packers has led the league in 20+ yard passing targets. Jordan Love is gonna try to test the Cowboys secondary that’s on the verge of falling apart now with Mike Pettine in the building. Just like the Cowboys’ three losses this season, I think this game came down to the final minutes, and unfortunately, Dallas left with more questions than answers, losing 28-24. Dyllan Rivers (3-2) The key this week for Dallas will be to establish the run. They have to keep the Packers offense off the field. Until I see it though, I’m not convinced this team has the ability to commit to their ground game consistently enough to keep the opposing offense sidelined. On the other side, Dallas hasn’t displayed the defensive prowess to limit a red hot Jordan Love and his deep threat receivers. Dallas falls 34-24 in Lambeau. Matt Holleran (3-2) I have no rhyme or reason to the pick, but I think we see a motivated Cowboys team in Green Bay on Sunday. Dallas plays with their hair on fire and puts together their best all-around performance of the year. The game comes down to the defense, and finally, they come up big in a key moment. Joey Porter Jr. picks off Jordan Love, sealing a huge win for Dallas. Give me the Cowboys, 30-26. Mike Poland (2-3) The Packers are dangerously thin on defense due to injuries. Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary, and the newly appointed Mike Pettine all have in depth knowledge on this Packers team which gives Dallas the edge. The Cowboys defense have struggled against the run, but they’re up against an offense that ranks last in rush yards per game, meaning the Cowboys defense can concentrate more on locking down Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Dallas wins this week 31-27.

title: Cowboys at Packers: Offensive, defensive impact players in Week 6
summary: Anytime the Dallas Cowboys and the Green Bay Packers play one another it’s almost guaranteed to be a slobber-knocker type of game.
