title: 2027 draft prospects to watch for the NY Giants in Week 7
summary: Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 7 of the 2026 College Football season! We have an incredible slate of games this week with the potential to be one of the two or three most consequential weeks on this year’s schedule. There are several match-ups this week that have the […]
full_text: Ole Miss defensive tackle Will Echoles pressures the Vanderbilt quarterback. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Good morning New York Giants fans! Happy Saturday and welcome to Week 7 of the 2026 College Football season! We have an incredible slate of games this week with the potential to be one of the two or three most consequential weeks on this year’s schedule. There are several match-ups this week that have the potential to shape, or reshape, the landscape of the College Football Playoffs. As always, we’re going to try to focus on players who could fit the Giants’ needs as we perceive them at the moment. And as things stand now, their biggest needs seem to be: Interior offensive line – The center position in particular here, as John Michael Schmitz seems to be on his way out and Bryan Hudson might not be a long-term answer. Defensive tackle – Pretty much chalk since Dexter Lawrence forced his way out the door. Wide receiver – The Giants currently have three (3) true or pure wide receivers on their roster, and just two under contract beyond this year. Malik Nabers is great, but his history of shoulder injuries is a concern. Running back – Cam Skattebo and Najee Harris have the power back rotation nailed down and they’re good for a high-volume grinder of a running game. But the Giants need a dynamic change of pace to create explosive plays on the ground. Tyrone Tracy is more dynamic, but he may also be too valuable as a returner to give significant reps as a runner. I’m going to break with my usual format and highlight a running back who’s caught my eye: UCLA back Wayne Knight . Knight is a fifth-year senior who followed Bob Chesney from JMU to UCLA and he has absolutely exploded this year. Knight was always a dynamic back, averaging 6.3 yards per carry (though just 10 touchdowns), with 61 receptions at JMU. At UCLA, he’s averaging a fantastic 7.7 yards per carry and already has 10 touchdowns. Knight is an “undersized” running back at 5-foot-6, but is also stoutly built at (roughly) 195 pounds. He has good speed and will likely run a low 4.4-second 40, but also runs with fantastic toughness, great vision, quickness, burst, and contact balance. Combined with his low center of gravity, he’s tough to find and tough to bring down. I wouldn’t be surprised if guys like Jadan Baugh (Florida) or Kewan Lacy (Ole Miss) wind up high on the Giants’ draft board, but a player like Knight could be a great complement to Skattebo and Harris, while being a great value as a likely Day 3 pick. I’ll probably circle back to Knight when UCLA and USC play in the final week of the season. For now, however, let’s get to this week’s games. (5) Indiana vs. (4) Ohio State Fox – noon I said today’s slate is fantastic, and we’re starting off with a (potential) banger. This game has the potential to be a preview of this year’s national championship, and features the reigning National Champion going against the best player in all of college football. This game is so big that I never even thought about featuring (7) Texas vs. Florida or (22) LSU vs. (16) Mississippi State. In addition to the stakes, this game features the two best wide receivers in football in Jeremiah Smith (Ohio State) and Charlie Becker (Indiana). However, I’m going to hope that the closest the Giants get to being able to draft either of those players without a costly trade up is looking at them longingly from the stands at the 2027 NFL Scouting Combine. Don’t get me wrong, it’s neigh impossible to watch anything besides Jeremiah Smith when Ohio State has the ball — he might actually be Captain America out there. Likewise, Becker would likely be in the conversation for WR1 in almost any other year. But I want to focus on the “other” receiver on the field. Player highlight: Nick Marsh (WR, Indiana) Marsh is probably the best “1B” receiver in the draft. He has prototypical size for the outside at 6-foot-3, 215 pounds, and combines his catch radius with great body control, and track speed. Marsh is a multi-sport athlete who played both basketball and ran track (100m) in high school, both of which are evident in his tape. He has much more shiftiness than you’d expect from a receiver his size (as a former basketball player) and he reportedly runs in the low 4.4’s or 4.3’s, and can simply run past corners who underestimate his long speed. Marsh is also physical wideout who can fight through tight coverage and win contested catches. His skill set gives him options to beat man coverage, bust zone coverage, be a deep threat (he already has 3 catches of 35+ yards), and a threat after the catch. Add to all that, Marsh is very well coached in Curt Cignetti’s Indiana program. Maybe not quite as well coached as in Brian Hartline’s “WR-U” when he was at Ohio State, but well coached nonetheless. Expect to hear Marsh’s name with “first rounder” buzz as the season, and then the Draft Process, unfold. (9) Ole Miss vs. (13) Missouri SEC Network – 3:30 p.m. I normally don’t like spotlighting games that not everyone has access to, however this really could decide whether Trinidad Chambliss gets to the College Football Playoffs. Missouri isn’t to be taken lightly, but Chambliss is just a gamer . I expect the Giants to be very interested in the running backs in this game, but I want to circle back to a player we’ve already looked at. Player spotlight: Will Echoles (iDL, Ole Miss) The Giants’ defensive tackles have been playing better than anticipated before the season began, but we should still expect a significant investment in the position going forward. We’ll see what happens over the remainder of the season and free agency, but it wouldn’t be at all surprising to see a defensive tackle pick to be included in just about every mock draft for the Giants going forward. If we’re looking at first round defensive tackle prospects, Will Echoles is right near the top of the board. He possesses prototypical traits at 6-foot-3, 315 pounds, with a very good first step, agility, and short-area quickness. He also plays with a red-hot motor as well as plenty of nasty to his game. Echoles has the play strength and anchor to eat blocks one-on-one, but he’s at his best when he’s attacking into the backfield and can be disruptive against both the run and the pass. Echoles will get plenty of opportunities to show both aspects of his game against Missouri. The Tigers feature a potent rushing attack, as well as the interesting dynamic of Austin Simmons at quarterback. Simmons is an incredibly intriguing player and was a teammate of Echoles in 2024 and 2025. He’s the former Ole Miss starter who was groomed to take over for Jaxson Dart before being injured early in 2025. Echoles is currently considered a first round prospect and has the potential to be a Top-15 pick. Defensive tackle draft stock can be volatile, however, and it’s entirely possible that he could fall into the Giants’ lap if they’re drafting in the 20’s. (8) BYU vs. (2) Notre Dame ABC – 7:30 p.m. All eyes at the national level will be on Notre Dame C.J. Carr, who has risen to the top of many quarterback rankings this year. Carr is an advanced processor who is just carving up the competition, but level of competition has been a question for the Irish so far this year. However, my eyes will be on the guys in front of Carr, and his left guard in particular. Player spotlight: Anthonie Knapp (OG, Notre Dame) Knapp wasn’t highly recruited out of high school, but immediately made an impact when pressed into service as a rookie when he was forced to start at left tackle as a rookie. He played well and held onto the job until this year, when he transitioned inside to left guard. Knapp is somewhere around 6-foot-4 and 305 pounds, but has a reputation as a gym rat and plays with excellent power. He’s emerged as a solid Day 2 prospect and could be in the mold of Zack Martin, Justin Pugh, or Joel Bitonio. My question is whether he can transition further inside and move to center in the NFL. As a…

title: Giants-Saints ‘5 questions’: What impact will Gayle Benson’s remarks have?
summary: With the New York Giants hosting the New Orleans Saints on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, we turned to Canal Street Chronicles for this week’s ‘5 questions’. Nic Jennings is our man with the answers. Ed: What is your reaction to the comments this week by owner Gayle Benson? Will they make a difference? What changes […]
full_text: Saints coach Kellen Moore | Getty Images With the New York Giants hosting the New Orleans Saints on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, we turned to Canal Street Chronicles for this week’s ‘5 questions’. Nic Jennings is our man with the answers. Ed: What is your reaction to the comments this week by owner Gayle Benson? Will they make a difference? What changes do you really believe she would be willing to make? Nic: I don’t take her comments lightly. Whether they lead to actual moves remains to be seen, but they certainly put pressure on everyone in the building. If the Saints fall to the Giants, there is a real possibility we’ve seen the last of Kellen Moore in New Orleans. This situation is different from the previous one with Dennis Allen, who had spent significant time with the organization and was part of a Super Bowl team in New Orleans. Allen had a longer leash. Moore hasn’t produced the results, and his seat is getting increasingly hotter. It’s now or never for Kellen Moore. Ed: What has gone wrong? Do you still see the Saints as a team that can win an NFC South that, like the NFC East, doesn’t seem to have a team likely to run away with it? Nic: At this point, no, I don’t see the Saints winning the division. There are simply too many characteristics of a bad football team: slow starts, poor discipline, no run game and the inability to stop opposing offenses from getting the ball in the endzone. All the offseason promise Who Dat Nation had has faded. If we don’t start seeing results soon, significant changes will be necessary. For once, those changes don’t need to come at quarterback. The focus should be on the coaching staff surrounding him. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him in New Orleans’ lineup, who would it be? Why? Nic: I’d have to go with Abdul Carter. A young, promising edge rusher to pair with Chase Young is exactly what this defensive line has been missing. It’s something I hope the Saints address this offseason, whether through the draft or free agency. According to Next Gen Stats, Young accounts for 21 of New Orleans’ 57 pressures. That speaks to the impact he’s making, but it also highlights the need for more players to step up around him. Ed: Who are a couple of players on the Saints’ roster we may not know a lot about, but that we should be familiar with for Sunday? Nic: On offense, it has to be Devaughn Vele. After the Saints invested a fourth-round pick to acquire him from Denver last year, Vele has become the contested-catch slot receiver they’ve been searching for since Michael Thomas. He’s quickly become one of Tyler Shough’s favorite targets and a go-to option on third-and-long situations. He and Juwan Johnson have also been effective in the red zone. For a six-foot-five receiver to move the way he does and display that kind of body control is remarkable. I expect him to continue garnering more attention as the season progresses. Defensively, keep an eye on second-year defensive back Jonas Sanker. He consistently finds his way to the football and has been impressive in his first year starting in the slot. He returned a fumble for a touchdown against the Vikings last week and had another return for a touchdown in Week 1 against the Lions that was called back after Jared Goff apparently “intended” to throw the football forward. Expect Sanker to be flying all over the field on Sunday. Ed: I see this as a 50-50 game. If the Giants are going to win it, how should they plan on attacking the Saints? Nic: Run the football. When teams establish the run against New Orleans, they tend to keep exploiting it throughout the game because it’s so effective. The interior of the Saints’ defensive line is one of the weakest areas of the roster, and that continues to plague them in run defense. Aaron Jones had 25 carries for 113 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans last week. I expect Cam Skattebo to have a big day if the Giants commit to the ground game.
author: Ed Valentine

title: New York Giants mailbag: Cam Skattebo, ‘peanut punch’, more questions
summary: Robert Stolzenberger asks: A lot has been made, rightfully, about the Commanders’ poor deciding and executing at the end of OT in game 5. But wouldn’t it have been much safer and smarter for the Giants to have tried the field goal on 2nd down (I think it was) instead of handing it off to […]
full_text: Robert Stolzenberger asks: A lot has been made, rightfully, about the Commanders’ poor deciding and executing at the end of OT in game 5. But wouldn’t it have been much safer and smarter for the Giants to have tried the field goal on 2nd down (I think it was) instead of handing it off to Skattebo for a couple of more yards up the middle? They were already inside the 25 yard line and any score would have won the game immediately. Winston had been on fire and the Washington defense was pretty grabby already on every play. Seems to me I recall Parcells and other team’s coaches not waiting for 4th down or taking more time off the clock in similar situations — rather just get it over with. Also, who would make that call, the OC or Harbaugh? We should be 4-1. Ed says: Robert, no. Stay with me, and I will explain. Skattebo ran for 5 yards and a first down right before the overtime two-minute warning. So, what you are asking is if the Giants should have simply kicked the field goal on first down coming out of the two-minute warning. Now, of course if the Giants make the kick there they win the game, Both teams had already possessed the ball once. But … there is always a’but’. Remember that placekicker Dominic Zvada missed three of five field-goal tries in the game, and had already missed from 46 yards during overtime. Washington had already used its two allotted timeouts in overtime. Yes, if you make the kick there you win the game. If you miss, though, you are handing the ball to Washington at about the 32-yard line with 1:50 to play. They have plenty of time to go down the field and kick a game-winning field goal, even without timeouts. We saw that play out. Had the Commanders not screwed up the clock management they moved down the field after the fumble and had plenty of time to get off a makeable field-goal try. The idea is to run the ball twice, maybe three times and work the clock down so that the game-winning field goal try by Zvada would be the final play of the game. That way, you take away any chance Washington has of winning the game. Here is how Harbaugh explained it Sunday night: “The idea was to run it twice, and then run it down, get as close as we could, protect the football, which we talked about numerous times, and then run it down and take the knee. So in case he doesn’t make the field goal, there’s no time for them to come back and get the field goal. That’s the strategy.” It was absolutely the proper way to play the situation. If Skattebo does his job, the Giants leave the Commanders with no opportunity to win. The only other way to do it is to take a knee three straight times, but that does result in moving the ball back a bit. Peter Calamari asks: I wonder jf anyone says a connection between the deterioration of the Giants running game and the substitution of Hudson for Schmitz at center. It seems like since that switch was made the Giants are running much less effectively although possibly pass blocking somewhat better. Ed says: Peter, it’s not the move to Bryan Hudson at center in place of John Michael Schmitz. Hudson has been better than Schmitz. If you judge by Pro Football Focus grades, which isn’t always the best way to judge, Hudson has been about 30 points better as both a run- and pass-blocker. The difference is adjusting to a run game where the big difference-maker was supposed to be Jaxson Dart’s mobility. Dart’s Week 1 22-yard run is still the longest of the season for the Giants. Without the threat of the quarterback run game, the Giants are much more predictable and limited on the ground. Neither Cam Skattebo nor Najee Harris are guys who can outrun NFL defenders or possess enough wiggle to make defenders miss. The blocking has to be perfect, and with teams loading up the box and outnumbering the Giants at the line of scrimmage it hasn’t been. Another thing that doesn’t help is Andrew Thomas’s groin injury. He is clearly laboring to get through games, and while he is playing well, he isn’t playing as well as a healthy Thomas is capable of. Peter Smyth asks: I’m wondering about the “punch” play that Washington used to get Skattebo to fumble in OT and used on Likely’s second TD (didn’t count as a fumble). I guess I’ve never noticed a defensive player just standing there and making no attempt at a tackle, just waiting, watching the ball, then punching it as the guy goes down. My questions: How to protect against this play? Are the Giants doing this to other teams? Has this been going on for years and I’m just noticing it? Isn’t this on the head coach to prevent? It must work a lot if they are trying it. Interested in your thoughts. Ed says: Peter, I am not crazy about the play. It is legal, though, and has been around for a while. It does seem to be becoming more of a thing in recent years. Yes, the Giants do it to other teams. Jevon Holland is good at it. I have seen Arvell Reese try to do it. It is becoming standard practice when one defender has a player under control for the next defender to try and punh the ball out. Tell me what a head coach is supposed to do about it. If a runner has the ball securely in two hands with a good grip on it and a defender punches the ball in the right spot with enough force it is going to come out. Maybe the smartest thing a runner can do is realize when it’s time to stop fighting for six more inches and get to the ground before somebody knocks the ball out. Bob Donnelly asks: With Sunday’s tie the NY Giants are in first place in the NFC East and, with a .700 winning percentage (3.5 /5), have the third best record in the NFC. Could you please share the scenarios of how, at the conclusion of the 18 game season, a tie helps/hurts a team? Ed says: Bob, tie games count as a half-win and half-loss. So, let’s say the Giants and Eagles both finish with nine wins atop the NFC East. The Eagles, unless they also tie a game this season, would be 9-8. The Giants would be 9-7-1. The way the NFL looks at ties, they would technically be 9.5-7.5, so they would have the better record and would be division champs. This played out in 2022. The Giants were 9-7-1. They made the playoffs as a wildcard. The 9-8 Detroit Lions went home without a playoff berth. Right now, there is no way to know what all of the scenarios will look like at the end of the year. ctscan123 asks: Hey Ed, I do not understand any resistance whatsoever to J.J. McCarthy being a Giant. I don’t see how it could be considered anything less than a slam dunk. It’s a fifth-round pick for a quarterback drafted 10th overall who missed his entire rookie season due to injury and started only 10 games in his second year. The expectation that young quarterbacks should make the leap from college to the NFL and immediately hit the ground running is bordering on ridiculous. If he develops into a starting quarterback, whether for us or for another team after we’ve developed him, it’s an absolute steal in terms of trade value. If he becomes a competent backup, it’s still a good deal. And for those keeping track, regardless of whether he blossoms and supplants Winston, we do actually need a backup quarterback this year. If he fails, you’ve lost a fifth-round pick. For Pete sake, what is the hit rate on fifth round picks in the NFL? I’m not much of a gambler, but isn’t this deal basically all upside? What am I missing here? I know this is a rant disguised as a question which is one of your favorite things, but the opposition to this move is one of the bigger head-scratchers I’ve encountered in a long time. Ed says: CT, where are you reading about resistance to the McCarthy trade? I have not seen much resistance to the trade itself, but everyone is entitled to his or her own feelings about whether or not the Giants should have done it. I wasn’t crazy about giving up a fifth-round pick, but the Giants felt he was the best quarterback available at the time and that the price was reasonable. There are people who will argue the Giants simply should have…

Giants hint at ‘explosive’ change to offense: ‘You’ll see a lot more’ | NJ.com Scheme matters, too. And to that end, Tracy and Skattebo […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know for the Giants battle with the New Orleans Saints set for 1 p.m. tomorrow at MetLife Stadium. Giants hint at ‘explosive’ change to offense: ‘You’ll see a lot more’ | NJ.com Scheme matters, too. And to that end, Tracy and Skattebo offered some interesting insight into the Giants’ rushing problems — and how they might solve them this week. “We’ve had mental errors,” Tracy said. “We had a lot of plays that were one block away or one cut away. We’ve just got to feel like one. There were a couple times we were seeing things differently — whether it’s o-line, running backs, even quarterback making the checks…if we all see it the same way,” results will improve.” He said this wasn’t just an issue in Washington. “It has come up before,” he said. Giants RB coach on fumbling issues "Just imagine if that's your paycheck you were carrying around, you're going to do a damn good job taking care of the football…that's the number one job as a running back. They'll get it corrected." RB Coach Willie Taggart on the Giants' fumbling issues: pic.twitter.com/vgMTh0US7M — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 16, 2026 The Giants are embracing accountability — for themselves and one another | New York Post There was one priority as the Giants were moving toward a potential game-winning field goal in overtime. “Coaches were echoing on the sideline, ‘Protect the football.’ And we just kept running the clock out, protecting the football and the game was over,’’ tight end Theo Johnson said. “I think that’s what everyone was thinking.’’ Giants-Saints prediction: Why New York can keep winning even with Jaxson Dart sidelined | The Athletic Beginning with a home matchup with the 1-4 New Orleans Saints on Sunday, the Giants’ next four games are against teams with a combined 5-14-1 record. The schedule will stiffen later with matchups against the Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1), San Francisco 49ers (5-0) and Seattle Seahawks (3-3) looming during a four-week stretch, but in a division full of flawed teams, the Giants might be able to stack enough wins to capture the NFC East for the first time since 2011. That the Giants are having success while having so much room to improve is a positive considering the strength of the coaching staff. But the margin for error has been impossibly small. The common refrain after close wins has been that the team would have lost similar games in recent seasons. It’s impossible to argue that point. Having an edge in those tight games is the reason Harbaugh’s hiring was celebrated as a franchise-altering move. Does Anyone Actually Want To Win NFC (L)East? Predicting NFL ’ s New Worst Division | FOX Sports Why they can win the division: Well, a lead at the quarter pole isn’t nothing. Also, they may have the best coach in the division in John Harbaugh, who is certainly the best they’ve had in New York since the Tom Coughlin days. They still play strong, opportunistic defense and they can run the ball. QB Jameis Winston sure does have a bunch of good weapons to throw to as well, at least when he’s throwing to the right team. Prediction: They will hold the line and the lead until just before Thanksgiving, when they’ll run into a four-week brick wall, of sorts, with home games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and San Francisco 49ers while hitting the road to take on the Indianapolis Colts and Seattle Seahawks during that stretch. That will be their reality check. Maybe they’ll have a big enough lead that it won’t matter. But more likely that stretch will drag them back to the pack, where at the very least they’ll be in the chase until the end. Second place, 8-8-1. It just winds up just connecting on the field.” “I would say any up or down, he’s going to stay here. When we’re down, he’s going to lift everybody up. Even when he’s down, he’s lifting himself up out here, talking to himself on the sideline. He’s always implementing the same thing. If I’m not on my game, he’s always telling me, ‘Look, come on, next play, flush it. Let’s go out. Cause I need you at the end of the game’.” Why Giants ’ Arvell Reese is a running back’s worst nightmare | The Record Rachaad White is among the NFL’s best running backs in pass protection, and the blocking metrics have validated that opinion as fact over the last two years and counting. title: Jets make roster moves ahead of Patriots game
summary: The New York Jets will be activating rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. from the injured reserve list for this Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. They will also be elevating linebacker Jaden Keller from the practice squad. Omar Cooper is a 6’ 0”, 200 pound receiver out of Indiana University. He was drafted […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 13: Omar Cooper Jr. #11 of the New York Jets runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets will be activating rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. from the injured reserve list for this Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. They will also be elevating linebacker Jaden Keller from the practice squad. Omar Cooper is a 6’ 0”, 200 pound receiver out of Indiana University. He was drafted by the Jets with the 30th overall pick in the 1st round of the 2026 NFL draft. Cooper has had a bit of a rough start to his NFL career. In training camp Cooper briefly fell behind Isaiah Williams to the fourth receiver on the depth chart. That didn’t last long, and Cooper entered the season as the WR3 behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell. It took only five NFL snaps for Cooper to make a splash, as he pinballed his way to a spectacular 30 yard catch and run on the Jets’ first drive of the 2026 season. It was an electrifying start to Cooper’s NFL career. Unfortunately, that was the last snap Cooper would see until the upcoming game against the New England Patriots. Cooper was injured on the play and was immediately removed from the game. He was placed on the injured reserve list and has spent the last four games there. On Sunday Cooper will try to pick up where he left off and give the Jets a boost in the passing game. With Adonai Mitchell out for this game Cooper will be a welcome sight on the field. Jaden Keller is a 23 year old, 6’ 3”, 235 pound linebacker out of Virginia Tech. He went undrafted in 2026 and the Jets signed him as an undrafted free agent before releasing him prior to the start of the regular season and adding him to the practice squad. Keller made his NFL debut two weeks ago when the Jets elevated him from the practice squad. In two games with the Jets Keller has played 39 snaps, all on special teams, and recorded one tackle. Sunday will mark Keller’s third elevation from the practice squad this season. Teams are limited to elevating any player three times in any given season. After this game if the Jets wish to activate Keller on Sundays they will need to sign him to the 53 man roster.

title: Three Things I’m Looking At in the Jets vs Patriots Game
summary: I had a blast at the Jets/Browns game, and it seems like the fanbase as a whole had a great time watching the Jets end a three game skid and get back into the win column. The team is undefeated vs. the AFC, and the same people who were screaming to fire Glenn two weeks […]
full_text: FOXBORO, MA - OCTOBER 16: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets is injured as he passes the ball during the fourth quarter against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on October 16, 2014 in Foxboro, Massachusetts. (Photo by Jim Rogash/Getty Images) | Getty Images I had a blast at the Jets/Browns game, and it seems like the fanbase as a whole had a great time watching the Jets end a three game skid and get back into the win column. The team is undefeated vs. the AFC, and the same people who were screaming to fire Glenn two weeks ago are now scheduling plans around a potential playoff berth in January. It always cracks me up to see how extreme the fanbase’s reaction is from week to week. I explained in last week’s piece why I didn’t think it was a must-win game, and several of you pushed back. I think we should all be able to agree that this upcoming game is the most important of the season so far. This is a chance at .500, a chance at beating a divisional opponent, and a chance to string together consecutive wins for just the second time in the Aaron Glenn era. All of those things would be monumental for this young, impressionable locker room. Aaron Glenn has yet to beat a divisional opponent as head coach of the New York Jets. I think we were all expecting/hoping that to change this year against a very poorly constructed Dolphins team, but why not shock the world against the New England Patriots that made the Super Bowl last year? They’ve been up and down all year, and even though they’ve won two straight games, we’ve seen chinks in the armor that prove the vulnerability of that team. Vegas has counted us out, but we’ll see how the chips fall on Sunday. Here are the things I’ll be looking at: Grand Returns Both teams are getting major reinforcements back into the lineup this week, so it will be interesting to see how each side adjusts to the changes. We all know Christian Gonzalez is an elite talent at cornerback, and with him back after two games, we can only assume he will be deployed to follow Garrett Wilson around and neutralize the Jets’ most explosive threat. What we don’t know is what Frank Reich will scheme up to counteract the assumed man-to-man coverage. Of course, this isn’t the only return, as Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is set to return after missing the last four games with an ankle sprain. The funny thing is, he had one catch against the Titans and still ended up with the most yards after the catch of any player in the game. We can say with absolute certainty that we don’t know the ceiling or even the nature of Cooper Jr.’s involvement in the offense – which is super exciting for the Jets. The Jets may still be missing WR2 Adonai Mitchell, but with Wilson, Cooper Jr., Sadiq, and Mason Taylor all healthy and ready to go, they won’t lack playmakers for Frank Reich and Geno Smith to work with. Even players with less star power, like Isaiah Williams, Tim Patrick, and Jelani Woods, could surprise in the passing game with the right opportunity. That’s the best part of having a willing, patient passer at the helm: there are plenty of options to choose from. Speaking of options, Drake Maye could get his top option, A.J. Brown, back from injury this week. It’s not confirmed whether he’ll play, but he’s been a limited participant since his practice window opened after suffering a Week 1 ankle sprain, unlike Cooper Jr., who was a full participant this week. That would be a decent-sized wrench in the game plan for both sides. I don’t have too many stats in this section, but the impact of these returns on the game is massive. The Jets get an explosive playmaker, and the Patriots get a shutdown corner. That same shutdown corner was getting carved up by Adonai Mitchell on primetime last year (albeit Mitchell had four drops, so it didn’t amount to much on the stat sheet), so I’m definitely curious to see how Garrett Wilson fares in the midst of his best NFL season to date. Mobility I spent a lot of time worrying about Deshaun Watson’s legs gashing the Jets defense last week, and while it ultimately didn’t turn the tide, Deshaun did have a solid rushing performance. Admittedly, the situation is hard to assess because he was sacked eight times, so the Jets clearly did a good job getting after the quarterback. Yet, watching in person, Deshaun seemed to be actively moving, and the stat sheet backs up my observations, as he had his most yards per rush in any game all season. Without the rain and all the calamity that comes with it, we should get a much clearer picture of how this year’s Jets defense fares with mobile quarterbacks. Watson entered last week’s game as the second-most frequent rusher at QB, and Patriots QB Drake Maye enters this game as the third-most. His designed runs are generally efficient, but his scrambles in tough situations are even more dangerous and timely. This isn’t to put Maye on a pedestal: he’s been quite awful so far this year. He was getting sacked three times a game until this two-game winning streak, when he was sacked only once in each game. His seven interceptions in five games tie for the most in the NFL this year, but again, he’s dialed it down during this two-game winning streak and has had only one interception since their Week 3 loss to the Jaguars. Can they force him to revert back to the indecisive, skittish QB that was a meme machine for the first three weeks of the season? To do that, the Jets will have to get through two former friends: OT Morgan Moses and OL Alijah Vera-Tucker. I spent so many years loving AVT and defending him through all of his injury-plagued seasons with the Jets that I felt personally offended to see him go to arguably the team’s biggest rival and instantly start trashing the Jets. A special part of my soul will be healed to see him or Moses be the one(s) responsible for letting up a sack. But if not, there’s a solid chance that rookie tackle Caleb Lomu could end up being barbecue chicken for the reigning AFC Defensive Player of the Week, David Bailey. The Bailey/Lomu matchup, plus McDonald’s familiarity with going against Moses day in and day out, makes me excited about the chances of pressuring Maye and containing him in the pocket. Complements Welcome One of my favorite parts of watching good football teams play is seeing how well they exemplify complementary football. The team’s phases work as a unit, cohesively operating toward a common goal (winning), and usually achieving it. I know, that might sound like a completely foreign concept to you if you’ve only watched Jets football. How many times have you watched a Jets game, seen the defense make a perfect play, only for the offense to completely squander the opportunity? Remember AG’s iconic sideline dance ? Special Teams makes a perfect play, only for the defense to choke away the win. The Jets have a long, rich history of failing in this area of football, but I’m bringing it up now for this pivotal matchup because we saw a glimpse of quality complementary football last week. With four minutes left, the Jets desperately needed a stop, and they forced a three-and-out. Then the football gods smiled on them when Corey Bojorquez dropped the punt, and the Jets started the next drive 23 yards from paydirt. Classic Jets would be to commit another turnover, or maybe get a three-and-out of their own and miss the field goal. Instead, Braelon Allen runs 22 yards for the touchdown, and the Jets win the game. This Sunday, I want to see this team be cohesive from one phase of the game to the next. I want to see the defense and special teams create momentum for the offense, and the offense capitalize on said momentum. The best coaches excel at complementary football, and I have to begrudgingly admit that next to outright cheating, it was Bill Belichick’s greatest strength. Vrabel has been spectacular in this area in his own right, and I want to see Glenn compete in this area. It’s also worth noting that with Blake Grupe signing…

title: Previewing the Jets’ opposition: New England Patriots
summary: The New York Jets find themselves in a familiar position heading into Sunday’s game in New England. If they could just find a way to upset the Patriots, it change the direction of their season and start to see them considered as a force to be reckoned with in the AFC. Could this be the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 28: Rhamondre Stevenson #38 of the New England Patriots runs with the ball against the New York Jets during the first quarter at MetLife Stadium on December 28, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Pamela Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Jets find themselves in a familiar position heading into Sunday’s game in New England. If they could just find a way to upset the Patriots, it change the direction of their season and start to see them considered as a force to be reckoned with in the AFC. Could this be the time when they finally achieve that, or will they be hanging on to relevance by a thread once again after Sunday? Let’s break down the Patriots’ roster going position by position: Quarterbacks Drake Maye is coming off a season where he was a legitimate MVP candidate. However, after three weeks, he wasn’t playing like that. The Patriots were 1-2 as Maye had thrown six interceptions and just one touchdown pass. However, he’s rediscovered himself over the past two games, leading New England to a come-from-behind win against the Bills and a blowout of the Raiders. His 374 yard output against the Raiders represented the second-highest total of his career, as he completed multiple deep balls. Over the two wins, he had seven touchdowns and just one interception. The Patriots’ number two is Tommy DeVito, who won three straight games as an undrafted rookie with the Giants but hasn’t had much success since then. Seventh round rookie Behren Morton is the number three. Offensive Line New England has a question mark on their offensive line this week after left tackle Will Campbell was injured and knocked out of the previous game. Campbell has been practicing on a limited basis all week but his game status is uncertain and he’s listed as questionable. In last week’s game, first round pick Caleb Lomu stepped in for Campbell and did well. In college, Lomu faced David Bailey and handled him well, although this was while Bailey was still at Stanford, so he hadn’t fully broken out yet. New England has multiple ex-Jets on their offensive line with Morgan Moses at right tackle and Alijah Vera-Tucker at left guard. They also have Greg Van Roten, but he’s on injured reserve. The 35-year old Moses is doing a solid job, although he does have five penalties in five games. So far, the injury-prone Vera-Tucker has been completely healthy with the Patriots. The other starters are last year’s third round pick Jared Wilson at center and veteran Mike Onwenu at right guard. However, Onwenu is also on injured reserve, so Ben Brown is currently starting there. Matt Pryor, Walter Rouse and sixth round rookie Dametrious Crownover are available as cover. Rouse already had to fill in for 41 snaps in week three. In the event of an injury to Wilson, Brown would probably slide across to center. Running Backs Similar to Campbell, running back TreVeyon Henderson has practiced on a limited basis this week but his status is uncertain after he picked up a high ankle sprain in last week’s game. He has said he feels pretty good but has been listed as questionable with New England also perhaps thinking ahead to their matchup with the Bears next Thursday. Henderson had 900 yards and nine touchdowns last year, but Rhamondre Stevenson is a more than adequate replacement, who has been a thousand-yard back in the past. He leads the team in rushing yards so far this year. The number three is Corey Kiner, who saw some playing time last week but fumbled once. Pass catchers The Patriots activated AJ Brown for practice this week, after he had been injured in the opener, so he may return to give their offense a further boost on Sunday, although his official game status is questionable. In Brown’s absence, Mack Hollins had been leading the team in receptions, but he is also now on injured reserve. Offseason signing Romeo Doubs leads the team with 219 receiving yards and Pop Douglas is coming off a game last week where he caught two touchdown passes. Slot receiver Efton Chism is now a regular part of the rotation and responded with the winning touchdown against the Bills on a spectacular one-handed catch. Kyle Williams also gets regular playing time and has been established as a big play threat. At tight end, Hunter Henry is off to a modest start, having caught 60 passes with seven touchdowns last year. Third round rookie Eli Raridon is the number two, and has eight catches with a touchdown, while Tanner Arkin and Cameron Latu are also on the roster with Julian Hill on injured reserve. Defensive Line The starters on the defensive line are former first round pick Christian Barmore, nose tackle Cory Durden and last year’s big money signing Milton Williams, who had 3.5 sacks. DaQuan Jones gives them an experienced backup at the nose tackle position with Joshua Farmer and ex-Jet Leonard Taylor III also on the team. All six of these players were active in the Raiders game, although Taylor has played the least on defense. Linebackers New England are without their top two pass rushers from last season, as K’Lavon Chaisson left during the offseason and Harold Landry is on the PUP list. These two combined for 16 sacks last season. In their place, the starters on the edge are Elijah Ponder and Dre’Mont Jones, with Ponder having really stepped up so far as he has 4.5 sacks and leads the team in quarterback hits and tackles for loss. Second round rookie Gabe Jacas is likely to see his role continue to expand though, as he’s flashed playmaking abilities as a rotational player with 1.5 sacks, an interception, three tackles for loss and five quarterback hits. The inside linebackers are led by Robert Spillane, who had 97 tackles last season and is leading the team again in that category. Alongside him, Christian Elliss also plays a full time role. Elliss is another Patriots player who is listed as questionable, although he practiced full on Friday. The reserves on the inside are Erick Hunter, Darius Muasau and sixth round rookie Namdi Obiazor, although they don’t play much. All three got some valuable reps in garbage time last week though. Defensive Backs New England has some real talent at cornerback with their three starters all having posted double digits for passes defensed last year. Former first round pick Christian Gonzalez was a pro bowler and the slot cornerback Marcus Jones intercepted three passes last year to prove he’s not just a punt returner. Carlton Davis was a big money signing who slotted well into the rotation. Davis has been ruled out due to injury and Gonzalez also had some injury issues, but he appears to be good to go. The main backup is Charles Woods, so he may need to step in for Davis. Fifth round rookie Karon Prunty, Channing Canada and Kindle Vildor are the other backups, but Prunty has been ruled out and Canada is listed as questionable. At safety New England brought in Kevin Byard to replace Jaylinn Hawkins, who had led them with four interceptions in 2025. Craig Woodson returns as the other starter with Dell Pettus on injured reserve. Woodson is also listed as questionable but was not limited in practice on Friday, so should be fine to play. Jaylen Reed has also started one game and seen action in three-safety sets, while Mike Brown is available in reserve and Brenden Schooler is mostly just a special teamer. Special Teams Kicker Andy Borregales missed seven kicks last season and has already missed two this year. He had the game winner against the Bills last season and also had the game-winner against Denver in the AFC title game, albeit in the third quarter. Punter Brian Baringer is on injured reserve so veteran Mitch Wishnowsky currently has this role. He has a net average of below 40 yards but has only allowed 64 return yards. In the return game, Jones is a two-time all pro as a punt returner and once had the game winning score against the Jets (albeit due to an obvious missed holding penalty). He had two more touchdowns last…

title: Geno Smith Appreciation Post
summary: As someone who prides himself on objective analysis, it’s equally important for me to acknowledge the highs, no matter how rare they are, in addition to the many lows that come with being a New York Jets fan. I’ll be the first to admit I was very underwhelmed with the Geno Smith acquisition – I […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - SEPTEMBER 27: Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets reacts to call against the Detroit Lions during the fourth quarter at Ford Field on September 27, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images As someone who prides himself on objective analysis, it’s equally important for me to acknowledge the highs, no matter how rare they are, in addition to the many lows that come with being a New York Jets fan. I’ll be the first to admit I was very underwhelmed with the Geno Smith acquisition – I understood the huge financial benefit of having a starting-caliber QB under contract for $3.3 million but had no belief in Geno in 2026. I didn’t even believe in him from 2013-2016. His Seattle Seahawks days were cool, but even his last year there started to look ugly until he went to Vegas and the wheels completely fell off. No QB in the NFL threw more interceptions from 2024-2025 than Eugene Cyril Smith. 15 in 2024 (2nd in the NFL), 17 in 2025 (1st in the NFL), I thought we were in for another brutal showing at quarterback this year. Boy, was I wrong. Only three quarterbacks this season have started every game this season and thrown zero interceptions: Jared Goff, CJ Stroud, and Geno Smith. After being the most prolific thrower of interceptions for two years, Geno has done a masterful job of avoiding throwing into harm’s way. In fact, he’s become the second passer this century to lead the league in interceptions and then have zero interceptions in his first five games the next year. I dug deep into ESPN.com to discover that fact – only Vinny Testaverde was able to do this, in 2001, after throwing 25(!) picks in 2000. Still, he got his first interception in Week 6 and ended the 2001 season with 14. Geno has six touchdowns and zero picks after five weeks just like Vinny did, but I’m not sure if this middle-of-the-pack New England defense has what it takes to pick him off. I’m thinking Geno might’ve actually turned over a new leaf. This isn’t to say he’s been perfect: he’s fumbled in four of the five games so far, and only four players in the league have lost more fumbles than Geno this season. He looks more “gun-shy” than normal this year, which has led him to hold on to the ball longer behind an offensive line that hasn’t lived up to expectations so far. But I promise this is an appreciation post , so that’s where my criticism ends! Geno’s avoided interceptions, and he’s put Garrett Wilson on pace for the best season of his career by a large margin. Garrett’s current pace is set for 105 catches, 1,271 yards, and 10 touchdowns this year – all of these numbers would break his previous career bests of 101 catches, 1,104 yards, and 7 touchdowns, which all came in 2024 with Aaron Rodgers slinging the ball. Smith’s numbers aren’t quite on pace to beat Rodgers, but you could argue his conditions have been less than ideal. We’ve only seen one drive of the Jets offense at full strength with the original trio of Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, and Omar Cooper Jr. on the field at the same time. We’re still unsure of when that will happen, as Mitchell works his way back from a somewhat mysterious finger injury that required surgery. Geno has also played 40% of his games in the rain, which is a less-than-ideal condition for pass-happy offenses. The Jets defense gets all the credit for holding opposing pass offenses under 200 yards during these games, but the Jets pass offense has also suffered from the precipitation. What would this offense look like with sunny skies, all the wide receivers healthy, Breece Hall healthy, and the confident Kenyon Sadiq who broke out against the Lions? It may be a few weeks until we find out, but Geno has done a superb job steadying the ship in the meantime. For me to enter this season as one of his biggest detractors, I cannot stress enough how impressed I am with this start and how hopeful I am for the rest of the season with him at the helm. Now the idea of having him start in 2027 with a young first-round pick QB learning behind him is starting to sound more like a dream than a nightmare. Let’s go, Geno!

title: Eagles Film Preview: The Panthers’ defense can be exploited
summary: Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite. I also record a video version for Patreon, where I break down […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 08: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles gestures during a game against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field on December 08, 2024, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Panthers 22-16. (Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite . I also record a video version for Patreon , where I break down the plays in greater detail and where you can further support my work. Before getting into the football, I want to acknowledge the news about Jalen Hurts. The Eagles have ruled him out against the Panthers after discovering a superficial blood clot in his calf. First and foremost, I hope he makes a full recovery. His health matters far more than anything I’m about to discuss in this article. Obviously, his absence has a significant impact on this matchup and what the Eagles can realistically ask their offense to do. However, these previews are primarily about understanding the opponent: what the Panthers play, who their important players are, and where their weaknesses appear. Most of that analysis hasn’t changed. There are opportunities against this defense, even with a backup quarterback, but the Eagles will need to protect well enough and finally get something going on the ground to take advantage. Pass Defense The Panthers aren’t a particularly good defense overall, but parts of their passing defense deserve respect. Ejiro Evero uses a lot of single-high coverage, with Cover 3 forming the foundation of the defense. You will also see Cover 4, Cover 6, and occasional man coverage. This is predominantly a zone defense, but you can’t assume every snap will give the quarterback the same answers. Their linebackers are particularly important to how they defend the middle of the field. Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke can read the quarterback, close underneath passing windows, and punish late throws. This is their biggest strength. Lloyd has been involved in all three of their interceptions this season, whether making the interception himself or helping create it I would be careful about treating short throws over the middle as easy completions against this defense. Lloyd is dangerous when he can see the quarterback and drive on a route. His coverage has been stronger than his run defense this year. The Eagles need Tanner McKee to understand where he is before releasing the ball. Panthers' Defense All22 Thread. 1) It's not a great defense at all, but they do some things well. They play a lot of single-high (but play it quite well), and their 2 LB's are dangerous in the middle of the field. Devin Lloyd in particular has played a hand in all 3 of their… pic.twitter.com/rwCqfNzhPf — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 16, 2026 The Panthers have also played Cover 1 successfully. Their man-coverage sample is relatively small, but the results have been excellent, and some of the film shows defenders competing aggressively at the catch point. In the play below, Jaycee Horn breaks up the quick slant and creates an interception opportunity. That’s an excellent individual play supported by a linebacker being around the football. However, there is a rather significant problem with using that play to describe the defense the Eagles will face: Horn won’t be playing! Neither will Mike Jackson. Losing both starting outside cornerbacks changes this secondary considerably, and the Panthers miss them massively. Their season-long coverage results include contributions from two players who won’t be available to help on Sunday. The Panthers have shown they can execute these structures with their best corners, but the replacements haven’t been as reliable. Even with Hurts unavailable, the Eagles should have opportunities outside. I would let McKee throw the ball vertically against this defense. 2) Here's Devin Lloyd, around the football again! They have played cover 1 very successfully this year, but they now have a huge issue with both of their top two cornerbacks injured. Here's Jaycee Horn breaking up the quick slant and causing the interception, but Horn isn't… pic.twitter.com/qz7lUm2k2v — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 16, 2026 The biggest obstacle to accessing those opportunities is the pass rush. I think the Panthers are pretty good here. They have two dangerous edge rushers. Their defense is at its best when the rush gets home quickly enough to prevent the secondary from having to cover for long. Jaelan Phillips is a player Eagles fans know well. He can win in multiple ways, and his combination of athleticism and power gives tackles a lot to handle. He may have a hamstring issue, but I still expect him to play well if he is out there. This is a big test for Markel Bell. 3) Pass rush-wise, they are pretty good and led by two excellent pass rushers on the edge. Their defense wins when they get pressure and can protect the secondary, because I don't rate their secondary at all with the injuries to Horn and Jackson. Eagles fans know Jaelen… pic.twitter.com/DlmME106Ff — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 16, 2026 Princely Umanmielen might be the most interesting player in their front. The second-year edge rusher has made a leap as a pass rusher. He was an explosive prospect coming out of college, and that athleticism is translating into impressive NFL reps. His ankle flexibility is outstanding. He is a true ‘bend the edge’ rusher. He also has more than one answer. There are outside setups, changes of direction, and counters that make tackles work rather than simply preparing for a straight speed rush. His 21.8% pass-rush win rate and three sacks show how disruptive he can be. I don’t think he is a complete edge defender yet, but as a pass-rush specialist, he is playing very well. I would expect the Panthers to give him opportunities against Bell, too. Evero also uses stunts and mugged A-gaps, presenting linebackers over the center before the snap, to complicate the protection. The offensive line needs to identify who is coming and pass off movement without creating the immediate free runners we’ve seen too often this season. 4) Second-year edge rusher Princely Umanmielen has made the leap. He was an explosive prospect coming out of college and is a pass-rush specialist. He's not a complete edge defender, but he's an impressive pass rusher. He has pretty insane ankle flexibility and can bend really… pic.twitter.com/plgqCJIJ8H — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 16, 2026 If the Eagles can protect, Akayleb Evans is the corner I would repeatedly test. He had a rough game against the Lions, giving up multiple big plays, and his coverage numbers this year are dreadful, considering he has only played in 3 games: 13 completions on 17 targets for 212 yards. 12.47 yards per target. The film backs it up, too. When he has to transition and react to a receiver changing direction, he can concede separation. But I would also challenge him vertically. The Panthers play enough single-high coverage to give their outside corners difficult assignments, and Evans hasn’t shown he can consistently survive those situations. The Panthers’ cornerback injuries should affect how aggressively the Eagles attack. 5) The Panthers have a huge issue in the secondary due to the injuries. Akayleb Evans isn't playing well and gave up multiple big plays against the Lions. Seeing as they play a lot of single-high coverage, the Eagles need to test Evans repeatedly with vertical shots because he… pic.twitter.com/oyQXN8cA2B — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 16, 2026 I wasn’t particularly impressed with their zone communication either. In some plays, defenders don’t appear coordinated when routes move between responsibilities, and the resulting space is far too easy for the offense to…

title: Jalen Hurts to injured reserve among four Eagles roster moves
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced four roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. JALEN HURTS On Saturday morning, ESPN reported that the Eagles were NOT going to place Hurts on injured reserve. On Saturday afternoon, ESPN reported […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during a game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced four roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. Here’s an overview: QB Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve. RB Jaydon Blue was signed from the practice squad to the roster. EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby and S Cole Wisniewski were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. JALEN HURTS On Saturday morning, ESPN reported that the Eagles were NOT going to place Hurts on injured reserve. On Saturday afternoon, ESPN reported that the Eagles are putting Hurts on IR after all. Breaking: After consultations with numerous doctors and experts that went into Saturday, the #Eagles are placing quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, sources tell @AdamSchefter and me. Hurts is now out for the foreseeable future. More information coming… pic.twitter.com/EHDeVw0Nye — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 17, 2026 By going on IR due to his “superficial blood clot,” Hurts is now out for at least the Eagles’ next four games: Week 6 vs. Jacksonville Jaguars Week 7 vs. Dallas Cowboys Week 8 at Washington Commanders Week 9 vs. New York Giants The Eagles then have a bye in Week 10. The earliest Hurts could possibly return is for the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The uncertain nature of Hurts’ situation makes it hard to predict exactly when he’ll be back. In the meantime, the Eagles will roll with Tanner McKee as their starting quarterback. It’ll be interesting to see how he fares in his first-ever extended NFL action. Cole Payton will likely be the backup for Week 6 since Joe Milton III only joined the team on Friday. To be determined if Milton will eventually overtake Payton or if he’ll just be the emergency third quarterback option. JAYDON BLUE With Saquon Barkley still dealing with a hamstring injury and both Tank Bigsby/Will Shipley now on injured reserve, the Eagles are currently without their top three running backs. Last week, the team called Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele up from the practice squad. Now Blue is joining them on the roster to give the Eagles three backfield options for Sunday’s game. The Eagles originally signed Blue, a former Cowboys draft pick, prior to the 2026 season. KEYSHAWN JAMES-NEWBY The Eagles are currently banged up at edge rusher. Jalyx Hunt was ruled out for Sunday’s game while A.J. Epenesa is doubtful to play. Jonathan Greenard will play while coming off an ankle injury. And so the team decided to temporarily elevate KJN to make his NFL debut. The rookie seventh-round pick missed most of the Eagles’ offseason practices due to injury but he flashed a little late in training camp and in the preseason. KJN will likely be most limited to special teams duty, barring more edge rusher injuries. Not necessarily surprising but a little interesting to see the Eagles elevated KJN instead of fellow practice squad edge rusher Mason Reiger. COLE WISNIEWSKI Wisniewski, another member of the Eagles’ 2026 NFL Draft class, is set to make his NFL regular season debut as a depth safety and special teams contributor. The Eagles are currently thin at safety. Andrew Mukuba and Cooper DeJean are the starters in base defense with Marcus Epps playing next to Mukuba in nickel packages. Epps is returning from injury this week after previously losing some snaps to Michael Carter II, who was ruled out of Sunday’s game. The Eagles also have Kenny Moore II, who is transitioning to safety after mostly playing nickel cornerback prior to coming to Philly. Wisniewski gives the Eagles another option on the back end of the defense in a pinch. NOTABLE NON-MOVES The Eagles did NOT temporarily elevate Zach Ertz to the roster. Ertz maxed out on elevations with three since he returned to Philly after Week 2. Ertz is now only eligible to play for the Eagles if they sign him to their roster. The Eagles also did NOT activate Landon Dickerson, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, or Jakorian Bennett from injured reserve. The team opened their 21-day practice windows to return from IR earlier this week.

title: Eagles place Jalen Hurts on injured reserve [UPDATED]
summary: UPDATED STORY: Lol. The Eagles actually DID decide to put Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after all. Just seconds after I published this story about the reporting how he wasn’t going to go on IR. Original story below. The Philadelphia Eagles will NOT be placing Jalen Hurts on injured reserve while the starting quarterback recovers […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the third quarter of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images UPDATED STORY: Lol. The Eagles actually DID decide to put Jalen Hurts on injured reserve after all. Just seconds after I published this story about the reporting how he wasn’t going to go on IR. Original story below. The Philadelphia Eagles will NOT be placing Jalen Hurts on injured reserve while the starting quarterback recovers from a “ superficial blood clot ,” according to a report from ESPN . Not yet , at least. Bold emphasis mine: The team, according to sources, has not even discussed the possibility of injured reserve, which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of four weeks. Hurts and the Eagles are still gathering more information and seeking additional medical opinions, with the quarterback’s health the foremost consideration. They believe the blood clot is treatable, with Hurts trying to determine the best course, sources said. The ultimate decision about when Hurts returns to play will come from his medical team, and the Eagles are ready to follow his lead. There is still a chance Hurts eventually ends up on injured reserve, if that is the direction the medical information indicates. The Eagles had until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday, October 17 to put Hurts on IR and have Week 6 count towards one of the four games he would be required to miss before being eligible to be activated. By not putting him on IR, then, the Eagles are keeping the door open that he can play in Week 9 by the latest. However, a clear timeline for Hurts’ recovery doesn’t seem to exist. At least not publicly. And this report acknowledges that Hurts might eventually end up on IR. On one hand, I can understand the Eagles not putting Hurts on IR. It wouldn’t be ideal if he ended up being fine sooner than expected but he couldn’t play due to IR mechanics. I’m guessing Hurts doesn’t want to be placed on IR right now and that sentiment is relevant to the Eagles’ decision. On the other hand, I wish the Eagles would put Hurts on IR in an effort to avoid any unrealistic expectations about him returning sooner than many would hope. The Eagles could also use the roster spot. With a retired Lane Johnson counting towards the limit all season long, the Eagles are already operating with a 52-player roster. And if Hurts is taking up a spot while missing a lot of games, it’ll effectively be a 51-player limit. We’ll see if the Eagles end up changing their minds down the road.

title: Eagles News: Riq Woolen mentioned among more trade buzz
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Early on Sunday last week, ESPN mentioned “it would not surprise those in the league if teams start calling on Eagles guard Landon Dickerson” in addition to how “rival GMs ask the question of whether they trade their top skill players […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Riq Woolen #2 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Early on Sunday last week , ESPN mentioned “it would not surprise those in the league if teams start calling on Eagles guard Landon Dickerson” in addition to how “rival GMs ask the question of whether they trade their top skill players like Saquon Barkley.” Now The Athletic is also mentioning Barkley and Dickerson in trade buzz … and Riq Woolen as well. I don’t think Howie Roseman has decided to be a seller at this moment in time. But I do think he’s making it known that some of the Eagles’ key players might be available. As he should be. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … What I’m hearing: Hurts’ blood-clot questions, Shedeur’s future, Micah Parsons’ return, trade deadline rumors – The Athletic If the losses pile up, you’ll begin hearing Philly’s big names in trade discussions, whether general manager Howie Roseman intends to deal them or not. I have had team executives already float whether the Eagles would/could/should part with running back Saquon Barkley and cornerback Riq Woolen. Offensive guard Landon Dickerson wondered aloud this week whether he’s in the team’s future plans. What becomes of Hurts’ and the Eagles’ partnership after this season appears complicated. The two sides did not renegotiate his contract this offseason, three years after his $255 million extension. A franchise that typically does big deals earlier than most teams, the Eagles have Hurts under contract for just two more years, and this season was viewed as critical to determining which way things would go. Roob’s Eagles Observations: What makes Tanner McKee unique – NBCSP LANDON’S FUTURE: I keep going back to this: If the Eagles were totally willing to trade Cam Jurgens, why wouldn’t they be totally willing to trade Landon Dickerson as well? If the offer is right? I think Howie would do it, for all the same reasons – freeing up a huge amount of future cash, moving on from a late-20s interior lineman who’s best days are likely behind him and adding to the growing draft pick stockpile. One difference is that the Eagles believed they already had an heir apparent to Jurgens in Drew Kendall, and I’m not sure they feel the same way about any of their other young interior linemen – Jake Majors, Willie Lampkin or Micah Morris. But they can figure out left guard. I think we’re seeing the first couple steps on what’s going to be an almost total o-line overhaul. Lane Johnson, Cam Jurgens and Dickerson made a combined 11 Pro Bowls and they could all be gone fairly soon. And don’t forget, Tyler Steen is unsigned beyond this year and with his level of play dropping off from last year they could be replacing everybody on the o-line other than Jordan Mailata. Which is crazy. Howie has drafted well on the o-line over the years with a couple notable exceptions that you know all too well, and he may need to repeat that success over the next year or two. Is losing getting to the Eagles? – BGN The crumbling usually starts like this. The subtleties surface like tiny lashing out spurts and the vacant facial expressions that take command when NFL teams are sinking without any answers available. General manager Howie Roseman may be feeling the sting of a three-game losing streak. Bleeding Green Nation recently learned he expressed frustration during an impromptu gathering with local media over a benign question about the offensive line. Roseman has been seen at practices more often than usual. He stormed off the sidelines visibly upset, his face distorted after the 19-17 walkoff loss to Jacksonville in London last Sunday. Poor offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has worn the look of a man escaping from the spin cycle of a Maytag washing machine during the Eagles’ current three-game losing streak. How the team has been covered by media this season has also drawn significant displeasure from some inside the building. Is losing getting to them? Touchdown Tanner? Eagles Locker Room Sees Greatness In Tanner McKee – PHLY Eagles Podcast That’s right, Zack Baun compares Tanner McKee to … Tom Brady of all people, dooming McKee to a future of losing to the Eagles in the Super Bowl, public divorce and no strawberries. Alas, his road to the Hall of Fame begins Sunday when he leads the Eagles into battle against the Carolina Panthers with Jalen Hurts on the sidelines. Oh, and the team signed Joe Milton! Deniz Selman and Brandon Lee Gowton join Bo Wulf to unpack another wild week for your favorite football team. 5 Questions with Bleeding Green Nation – Cat Scratch Reader The Panthers are back and they’re facing what’s left of the shockingly 2-3 Eagles as they return from a game in London just six days ago now. Tomorrow we’ll see if they are awake and healthy enough to contend with a Panthers squad that should be freshly rested from their early bye week. To see what other storylines and shenanigans we should be on the lookout for this week, I spoke with Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to get the inside scoop on the Eagles quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and edge injuries, among other concerns. It really does sound like only one team is going to walk into this game on two feet and that may surprisingly be the Carolina Panthers. Here’s what Brandon had to say. Panthers activate Taylor Moton, Turk Wharton, Trevor Etienne – PFT Panthers offensive tackle Taylor Moton is set to make his 2026 debut. Moton returned to practice this week after missing all of training camp and the first weeks of the regular season while recovering from blood clots in his lung. The Panthers announced that he has been activated from the physically unable to perform list on Saturday. Eagles-Panthers preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice This is not a great line. Bryce Young has been pressured a whole lot so far this season. The Eagles’ pass rush showed a little life against the Jaguars Week 5. Notably, Jalen Carter had a monster game. If the Eagles are going to “upset” the Panthers, the defensive line is probably going to have to make a few big plays. NFL Week 6 betting guide: Analysis, best bets and TD predictions – ESPN Tanner McKee 19+ completions (-101). The Philadelphia Eagles are as decimated of an offense as we’ve seen in the league this season. Three starting linemen from Week 1 are out for this game, as are RB1 Saquon Barkley, WR1 DeVonta Smith and now QB1 Jalen Hurts, who has a blood clot that might keep him out indefinitely. In for Hurts and contending with this depleted roster is backup Tanner McKee, who originally lost the QB2 job out of camp to Andy Dalton. But McKee isn’t a slouch. In two career starts, McKee has 30 and 24 completions. He’s a rhythm pocket passer who knows where to go with the football. The Carolina Panthers have been a stiff pass defense for much of this season by completion percentage, but they’re still down both starting cornerbacks in Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, and we’ve seen the backups play for only one game in Week 4 before Carolina’s Week 5 bye. It’s still unclear how good Carolina’s secondary will be in the interim. As such, I’m betting on McKee, in what is likely a trailing game script, to take underneath completions, especially with the running back injuries behind Barkley, which should discourage the Eagles from too many handoffs. I’ll be taking alts on completions here up to 24+. Agent’s Take: Making sense of Eagles’ salary cap manipulation after Lane Johnson’s retirement – CBS Sports The plan is for the Eagles to delay processing Johnson’s retirement until next June 2 at the earliest. That’s because only the current year’s bonus proration counts toward the salary cap with…

title: Eagles thoughts: The Panthers got paws
summary: The Carolina Panthers are 2-2, but look to be on their way to their first winning season since 2017. Carolina’s Got Hands (Paws?) Last year the Carolina Panthers offense didn’t run many plays (22nd most) and when they did, they were pretty bad at it (27th in yards per play). This year? This year the […]
full_text: CANTON, OHIO - AUGUST 06: Carolina Panthers mascot Sir Purr performs prior to the 2026 Pro Football Hall of Fame Game against the Arizona Cardinals at Tom Benson Hall Of Fame Stadium on August 06, 2026 in Canton, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Carolina Panthers are 2-2, but look to be on their way to their first winning season since 2017. Carolina’s Got Hands (Paws?) Last year the Carolina Panthers offense didn’t run many plays (22nd most) and when they did, they were pretty bad at it (27th in yards per play). This year? This year the Panthers offense isn’t messing around. Carolina is… 3rd in plays per game 3rd in pass attempts per game 5th in yards per play Bryce Young is… 1st in yards per game 3rd in completed air yards per attempt 7th in intended air yards per attempt Tet McMillian is not having any hint of a sophomore slump, but the Panthers receiving core is not a one man show, as Jalen Coker 17th in yards per game. Carolina is probably going to win the NFC South, and unlike last year, not just because someone has to. Hasn’t he suffered enough? Poor guy. Speaking of ambulances… Call the ambulance, but not for me When the schedule came out, this looked like a “trap” game. The Eagles were returning from London, and they face the Cowboys in two weeks. Meanwhile the Panthers coming off their bye in a ridiculously unfair scheduling disadvantage for the Eagles. Now if anything, the Eagles are the trap team. Carolina has an extremely winnable division game next week at home against the Bucs. Quite the sudden role reversal. College Football Watch List I have in the past tried to stay away from the obvious top 10 type of players, because they were out of reach of the Eagles. Not this year. As it stands now the Eagles are picking 10th, and they’re about to be out their starting QB for a couple of games. 12:00 – Ohio State at Indiana I doubt the Eagles go back to back WR in the 1st round. Still, this game has WR1 in a guy you may have heard of in Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith , and possibly WR2 in Indiana’s Charlie Becker . If the Eagles slide continues Smith could be in play. Becker is the physical and deep threat the Eagles lack. 3:30 – Missouri at Ole Miss Ole Miss DT Will Echoles is listed at 6’3” 315 and is fast off the snap. He’s an impressive physical talent, Ole Miss has lined him up on occasion as a stand up edge rusher. But he’s inconsistent. He had a good game against LSU but then Ole Miss as a whole predictably had a let down against Florida and got smoked. He later said it was because of “a lack of violence” which is an answer both I want to hear from a DT because that’s a good mindset to have, and not want to hear because it meant he did not wake up and choose violence. 7:30 – Notre Dame at BYU Notre Dame CB Leonard Moore is probably the best defensive prospect in the draft. CB is not a priority position of need but like Jeremiah Smith some players are just too good to pass up. He’s got everything you want in a corner prospect, size, speed for a CB who is 6’2”, versatility, excels in man coverage, and production (5 INTs last year). He might get the dreaded “safest pick in the draft” tag. Uh oh.
